text:
still processing some of the conversations from @EFDevcon day 3. 🇮🇳

a little late to the recap, but these are too interesting not to share.

i’ve been exploring many of these intersections through The Protocol, my independent research and writing project covering crypto, product design, brand strategy and what it takes to build better products in the onchain economy.

if you’re interested in these conversations, I’m sharing my notes and research here: 

read here 👉🏻 designprotocol ( dot) substack ( dot) com

day 3 went deep into some of the questions that will shape the next chapter of ethereum: privacy, security, censorship resistance, applied cryptography and the intersection of AI and decentralised systems.

a few topics that caught my attention:

> the post-quantum transition. quantum computing might not be an immediate threat, but preparing ethereum’s cryptographic foundations for what’s coming is work that needs to happen early.

> privacy by default. from private transactions to validator privacy, the conversation is shifting from whether privacy matters to how we make it practical and accessible.

> censorship resistance. anonymous broadcast and permissionless networks are essential to keeping open systems genuinely open. decentralisation means little if someone can decide who gets to participate.

> AI agents and security. as agents start interacting with wallets, protocols and onchain infrastructure, trust, identity and verification become much bigger challenges.

> formal verification. writing code is one thing. proving that it behaves as intended is another. security needs to go beyond audits and become part of how we build.

> ethereum’s networking layer. peer-to-peer infrastructure, network resilience and privacy are the less visible pieces that make the entire ecosystem work.

> the human side of open technology. sessions around civic AI, digital rights and permissionless systems were a reminder that the technology should ultimately expand what people can do.

outside the talks:

@KASTxyz deserves another mention. the Gold Party was easily one of my favourite side-event experiences of Devcon. incredible setting, music, people and execution. special credit to Hardeep and the KAST brand and design team for raising the bar.

one takeaway from day 3:

the future of ethereum isn’t just about making systems faster or cheaper. it’s about making them more private, secure, resilient and accessible without giving up the principles that made them worth building in the first place.

the deeper you look into the infrastructure, the more interesting the future gets.

more thoughts and research on The Protocol: designprotocol ( dot) substack (dot) com

Not your keys, not your coins?

Apparently, it's now:

Your keys, our RPC. Your coins, our permission.

A scammer sends 0.0001 dust to your wallet without your consent.

You didn't approve anything. You didn't interact with the scammer. You simply received an unsolicited transaction on a public blockchain.

Then Phantom's compliance filter kicks in:

"Your address has interacted with a flagged malicious entity. Transactions disabled."

Wait. WHAT?

So a random scammer can poison my wallet address with dust, trigger your automated risk detection, and suddenly I can't use your wallet interface to move my own assets?

Welcome to self-custody, where you own the keys but apparently need corporate permission to use them.

The blockchain didn't freeze my account.

The centralized frontend did.

The irony is almost too good.

We built crypto to escape banks freezing our money, only to end up with fintech apps wearing a decentralization costume.

If a wallet can unilaterally disable your ability to transact because some random third party sent you dust, maybe it's time to rethink what "self-custody" actually means.

Not your keys, not your coins?

More like:

Your keys. Their rules. Their permission.

Peak Web3 UX. 🤡

text:
One of my more recent size plays has actually been real life silver bars and coins

I’ve been accumulating a decent amount of physical silver over the past couple weeks and my average is sitting around $50.7 

I personally think silver has one of the best long term risk to reward opportunities in commodities rn and here’s why

A lot of people just look at silver as another precious metal like gold but don’t actually realize how important it is to the world (arguably the most important metal)

Silver has the highest electrical conductivity of any metal and is used in basically everything from electronics, solar panels, EVs, electrical infrastructure and even hardware used in AI/data centers (the future)

As technology continues advancing, the need for materials like silver isn’t just going to disappear, in fact with ev cars now stepping it up and potentially byd coming to America the demand and increase for silver is only gonna get bigger

Now the part that really interests me is the supply side and it’s what I have been telling family and friends

Silver has been running a supply deficit for 5 years straight with a 6th year projected for 2026

Basically more silver has been getting consumed than what’s being supplied through mining and recycling, and that difference has to come from existing inventories

On top of that, most silver isn’t even mined directly and it’s mostly produced as a byproduct of mining other metals like copper, zinc and lead

So even if silver starts moving up aggressively, it’s not like miners can just decide to double silver production overnight because the price went up

And unlike gold, a lot of silver is actually being used in industrial applications rather than just being stored away or women wearing fancy pretty jewelry 

Of course companies can find ways to use less silver when prices rise, but that doesn’t change how important the metal is especially at this price (-65% in a year aswell)

When you have something that’s genuinely needed across multiple industries, has limited short term supply flexibility and has been running deficits for years, I think it’s worth paying attention to and getting some exposure 

There’s also the investment side of it, If more capital starts flowing into physical silver while industrial demand remains strong, you’re adding another source of demand to an already tight market

I’m not saying silver is going straight up or that there won’t be corrections, but I personally really like the setup here and I think it’s a cool place to store cash 

I’m treating this as a long term position and plan on continuing to accumulate when I see good opportunities

这种"为捐而赚"的思路，是有效利他主义的核心主张：先尽量多赚钱，再把钱捐给最有效的地方。

FTX创始人SBF在麻省理工读书时，被有效利他主义创始人之一的Will MacAskill说服，之后进了华尔街，后来又创办了FTX。

Dario Amodei最终没有去做金融，但"赚钱再捐"的承诺留了下来：Anthropic七位联合创始人都承诺捐出个人所持股份的80%，公司在上市文件中再次确认了这一点。

text:
A successful revocation transaction gave Plakxio holders no protection at all.

During a Founder Security Sprint, Zealynx found that `isApprovedForAll()` treated every whitelisted operator as approved for every holder.

The class mask limited which badges an operator could move, but not whose badges. Even after a holder revoked approval, the whitelist still returned true, so the operator could move the permitted badge classes without the holder's signature or payment.

Plakxio fixed the High finding by enforcing holder opt-outs on the approval view and both transfer paths, while adding contract checks and delayed activation for operators.
author: ZealynxSecurity

text:
The whitelist accepted a bare address, so the privileged operator did not even have to be a contract whose code enforced signed orders.

Zealynx reran every step of the proof of concept against the fix and verified that the path was closed.

币安学习营回程的飞机上，终于有时间一个人静下来，记录这次的真实感受。

这次Trust Wallet以赞助商身份参与活动，
所以我看到的是一个第三方视角，
也想和大家分享。

-KOL线下活动，真的只是吃喝玩乐吗？

网上晒出来的都是海岛、沙滩、椰林， 但说实话，
KOL们在线下的投入程度远超我的想象。

每天早上9点到9点半开课，大家基本准时坐齐。

偌大的宴会厅安安静静，
我坐在最后一排，
还看到好几位KOL把PPT从第一页拍到最后一页。

就像土澳大师兄私下跟我聊到，
这波行情比较迷茫，
他甚至消沉了好一阵。
但借着线下机会和大家聊下来，
还是发现了不少潜在机会。

所以推文里看到的只是皮毛，
真正有价值的东西，还是要面对面聊。

— 为什么币安要在这个节骨眼上办海岛学习营？

最后一天的毕业典礼上，
一姐线上连线，
亲自回答了这个问题：

内部其实紧急讨论过，
但如果取消，
外面一定会传出“币安没钱了”之类的谣言。

不如踏踏实实，照常把线下交流的机会留给大家。

— Trust作为一个钱包，赞助这个活动有什么意义？

这是Trust Wallet第一次赞助纯华语区的活动。

我的大师课分享结束后，
有十几位老师主动在推特上分享Trust Wallet的内容，

还有几位KOL私下跟我说：
“没想到你们Trust的增长数据这么好。”

还有两位做返佣的老师，
在颠簸的车上一路拉着我给Trust提建议，好奇Trust CEO Felix的产品风格和方向，
建议我们做出差异化，
甚至还给了一些很有创意的想法。

这两个瞬间，让我觉得这就是Trust赞助的意义所在。

— 做线下活动，本质上是个苦力活

别人看到的可能是吃喝玩乐， 作为半个工作人员，我看到了另一面。

KOL们的航班晚点两小时，
晚上九点还没到。
sisi、丫丫、May、Mia、Alina、kim几位工作人员一直没吃饭，在暴雨里陪大家一起等，
直到所有人都吃上饭，她们才去吃。

其实这趟行程确实很波折。

沙滩晚宴摆好的Trust周边，
被突如其来的狂风暴雨淋湿，
我和同事冲去抢救物料，被淋成了落汤鸡；

陪了我五年的可爱行李箱，
惨遭航空公司毒手，摔得西八惨烈；

还有和老师们一起盯着暴跌的账户，
半天说不出一句话。

黑天鹅总比想象中多，
我们能做的，
只有调整心态，迎接挑战。

毕竟负面谣言，永远跑得更快， 而正面的建设，总显得微不足道。

飞机上的一些碎碎念， 祝大家周末愉快， 月底我们泰国BBW见！🌴

富国岛学习营结束了。来之前，我以为这几天是带着大家来学习。结果几天下来，我自己的本子上也记得满满的。

第一天，Jeff @taida88 给大家讲 Binance AI。他讲得很有画面感——同一个币安 App，刚入门的人打开，看到的是更简单的解释和提示；天天盯盘的人打开，看到的是更深的数据和市场背景。

后面几堂课，大家已经发了很多，我只说两点记得最深的。

一个来自 Binance Research 的分享：市场反应的，往往不是利率本身，而是大家的预期变得有多快。
另一个来自@AncoBinance 的钱包分享。钱包空投覆盖了 1199 万人，让我意识到，对很多人来说，币安钱包就是他们进入链上的第一道门。这道门容不容易迈进，比其他功能还重要。

最后一天，我们请老师们围坐在一起，挨个听大家的反馈。哪里用着不顺手、哪里还能改，都直接说出来。

听起来都是小细节，但每一条背后都是一个具体的人、一个具体的使用习惯。我也更理解 Jeff 说的「个性化了」。

以前的交易所，所有人打开看到的都是同一张行情表。以后，每个人看到的币安可能都不一样，但出发点是同一个——让更多人用得上、也看得懂金融工具。

我想这就是学习营最有意义的地方。产品做得再聪明，也得先听懂用的人。

当天晚上一姐@heyibinance 远程连线还提到一点，那就是用户的信任对我们来说是最贵的，币安能做的，是靠每天的经营和兑付，一点点把它累积起来。对我们来说，是一次次反馈能够落到实处，真的帮大家解决问题。

最后谢谢各位老师这几天的坦诚。币安一直说用户至上，我觉得它最真实的样子，就是像这几天这样，坐下来听你们说。很珍惜和大家相聚的时光，我们 #binanceblockchainweek 曼谷再见！

《关于更新币安广场社区准则的通知》
亲爱的币安广场用户：
感谢大家一直以来对币安广场的支持与陪伴。
为营造真实、理性、友善的交流环境，币安广场近期更新了《社区准则常见问题》，主要涉及返佣推广行为和社区交流秩序两方面，适用范围包括直播、帖子、评论、聊天室及个人主页等。具体如下：

一、返佣推广行为规范
根据返佣团队《超级返佣成员拓展市场行为规范》的明确要求，"严禁在币安广场内以任何形式引导老用户更换账户、重新注册或虚假宣传/承诺等行为"。为配合该规范落地，广场同步更新以下规则：
直播场景：直播画面及直播间装饰中，请勿展示返佣码、注册链接、助力人信息等推广性内容，以保障直播间的观看体验。
帖子及个人主页：请勿以返佣比例作为宣传卖点；请勿在个人简介中展示返佣码、注册链接或助力人信息，也请勿在个人主页置顶返佣相关帖子。
引导更换账户：在广场内任何场景中，严禁以任何形式诱导已注册用户注销、更换账户或重新注册，包括但不限于引导其使用亲属或他人身份信息注册新账户。

二、理性交流，拒绝人身攻击
我们欢迎不同观点之间的理性讨论，但不允许讨论演变为人身攻击和骚扰。以下行为将被视为违规：
侮辱攻击：基于外貌、职业、身份、健康状况等侮辱或贬低他人；攻击他人家人，或使用涉及亲属、性侮辱、人格贬损的内容攻击他人。
诅咒威胁：诅咒他人死亡、患病或遭受严重伤害，或威胁伤害他人。
针对性围攻：持续针对特定对象发布攻击性内容，或将冲突扩散至无关帖子、评论区、直播间或群聊；组织、号召他人集中辱骂、刷屏或围攻他人。
侵犯隐私：未经授权披露他人真实姓名、证件、住址、联系方式、财务信息等个人信息，或组织、参与人肉搜索。
以上行为即使使用截图、剪辑、暗语、谐音或影射等方式，平台也会结合上下文识别并处理。

三、整改安排
即日起至 11 月 20 日为整改期。请各位用户对照上述规范，对直播间画面、个人主页及过往发布的内容进行自查，如有涉及请及时调整或删除。
整改期结束后，相关规范将正式执行。对于未按时整改的内容，平台将统一重置个人简介、处理违规内容，并开展常态化巡查，依据《币安广场社区准则常见问题》对违规行为实行递增处罚。
社区的美好需要每一个人共同守护。如对本次更新有任何疑问，欢迎联系币安客服。感谢大家的理解与配合！

币安广场团队

King of the Markets has officially concluded.

KotM was built to pilot and prove out the Reserve's liquidity thesis, and the results have surpassed all expectations. A more detailed breakdown of the data will be released this week, but for now, some important information regarding rewards.

1) A big part of this process is making sure the reward pool isn't being diluted by sybils and people who tried to game the system (wash traders and token ruggers) so we're taking the time to review all the data before distributing anything.

We've already begun filtering through transaction data to identify wash trading and accounts that attempted to artificially farm points. We want to make sure rewards go to legitimate traders and deployers, not those who tried to game the system.

2) In approximately 6.5 hours, the KotM page will update to show your trading and launchpad activity. You'll be asked to sign with your wallet to confirm where you'd like to receive your rewards and in which token. This is completely free, requires no gas, and takes about 5 seconds.

3) You'll have 120 hours (5 days) to complete this step. If you don't sign within that window, you will not be eligible to receive rewards. Once the 120 hours are up, we'll run one final filter and redistribute any unclaimed rewards from wallets that didn't sign among eligible wallets that did.

4) For those who traded through FOMO, unfortunately, FOMO doesn't make its wallet API public, which makes tracking your activity extremely difficult. We still want to make sure FOMO users aren't left out of rewards, so the best solution we have for now is to export your EVM private key from FOMO and import it into a compatible wallet.

From there, check the FOMO box and complete your payout confirmation, even if your stats show zero activity. We'll manually review these wallets over the coming days to make sure legitimate activity is accounted for.

Please only import your private key into a trusted wallet app. Never share it with anyone or enter it on the KotM website.

5) Once the final filtering and redistribution are complete, rewards will be airdropped directly to your specified wallet in your selected currency.

We appreciate everyone who participated in the pilot. The results have given us a lot of confidence in what we're building, and there's much more to come.

Let me tell you something absolutely BONKERS from last night’s midterms…

Democrat Ericka Lomick just “won” Texas House District 93 despite being a convicted felon who suspended her campaign months ago.

She pleaded guilty in 2011 to federal charges including mortgage-fraud conspiracy, bank fraud, and money laundering. Her sentence? 63 months in federal prison.

On her candidate paperwork, she checked the box claiming she had not been finally convicted of a felony. After her criminal record surfaced in September, she suspended her campaign and stopped running.

But Texas election deadlines had already passed, so her name remained on the ballot for both the regular general election and the special election.

And voters still elected her by roughly 51–49%.

Here’s the kicker: Under Texas law, a final felony conviction generally makes someone ineligible to hold office unless they’ve been pardoned or had their disabilities released.

Meaning she can’t actually serve. Her “victory” simply creates a vacancy and triggers yet another special election.

A convicted federal fraudster who quit campaigning still got elected to the Texas House.

Are blockchains actually built for AI agents, not humans?

At our latest @FinalityForum, we brought together leaders from @nansen_ai, @base, and @virtuals_io to unpack the rise of Agentic Commerce and what happens when AI gets its own wallet.

3 key takeaways:
🟪 Blockchains have a human UX problem; agents fix this.
Humans hate interacting with complex on-chain UX. But for AI agents? Permissionless, 24/7, low-cost rails are their natural habitat. Humans stress-tested the pipes; agents are going to run them.

🟪 Autonomy requires smart guardrails.
AI agents are non-deterministic, but blockchain transactions are completely final. When an agent misinterprets intent, there are no chargeback mechanisms on-chain. Bridging this gap takes practical guardrails i.e. from strict spending thresholds and human-in-the-loop confirmations to "evaluator agents" and programmable compliance.

🟪 AI-native institutions are inevitable.
We’re moving beyond personal assistant tools. From autonomous treasuries to "AI Senates" managing protocol rewards, agent-to-agent transactions will generate an entirely new layer of digital GDP.

Unpacking these kinds of shifts with the operators building the future is exactly why we created Finality Forum and Convergence Summit at Ethene Labs.

We’re already organizing the next editions... stay tuned! 🚀

What’s your take, are we ready for autonomous AI agents managing protocol treasuries and executing complex commerce loops by the end of this cycle? Let me know in the comments.

Today I’m excited to introduce our @PaymanAI Gateway product. The secure and safe way for your customers to interact with your bank using AI Agents. This has been our most in demand product since we’ve launched, and rightfully so!

Banks are asking the question, how do we prevent this from happening, or how do we make it safe? We have the solution.

The idea is fairly simple. Your bank gets its own AI Agent and it’s able to then talk to the other AI Agents your customers are using.

Anytime a request for anything comes in, your bank’s agent is the one that is actually executing within your firewall on behalf of an authenticated user. The data stays with you, the relationship stays with you, and more importantly your customer is safe!

When a user asks Muse “What’s my balance and how much have I made in interest?” Muse has to go to your bank and ask the bank’s agent on behalf of the user. The Payman Gateway authenticates the user, makes sure the AI Agent is on its approved list for asking, and allows the question to then go through to the bank’s agent on behalf of the authenticated customer.

The questions that your customers are asking other AI Agents now get back to you. The data doesn’t leave your systems as your banking AI Agent controls what it’s allowed to respond to or not, and your customer relationship only gets strengthened.

We’ve had a tremendous response from banks already and it has quickly become THE topic of conversation when speaking about Agentic Banking.

Our systems have been built for this future for years now. All around the one question, how do you trust AI with money? Well the time has come and we’re excited to be a helpful partner, as many bank boardrooms are quickly asking “What do we do about Muse & Instinct”.

King of the Markets has officially concluded.

KotM was built to pilot and prove out the Reserve's liquidity thesis, and the results have surpassed all expectations. A more detailed breakdown of the data will be released this week, but for now, some important information regarding rewards.

1) A big part of this process is making sure the reward pool isn't being diluted by sybils and people who tried to game the system (wash traders and token ruggers) so we're taking the time to review all the data before distributing anything.

We've already begun filtering through transaction data to identify wash trading and accounts that attempted to artificially farm points. We want to make sure rewards go to legitimate traders and deployers, not those who tried to game the system.

2) In approximately 6.5 hours, the KotM page will update to show your trading and launchpad activity. You'll be asked to sign with your wallet to confirm where you'd like to receive your rewards and in which token. This is completely free, requires no gas, and takes about 5 seconds.

3) You'll have 120 hours (5 days) to complete this step. If you don't sign within that window, you will not be eligible to receive rewards. Once the 120 hours are up, we'll run one final filter and redistribute any unclaimed rewards from wallets that didn't sign among eligible wallets that did.

4) For those who traded through FOMO, unfortunately, FOMO doesn't make its wallet API public, which makes tracking your activity extremely difficult. We still want to make sure FOMO users aren't left out of rewards, so the best solution we have for now is to export your EVM private key from FOMO and import it into a compatible wallet.

From there, check the FOMO box and complete your payout confirmation, even if your stats show zero activity. We'll manually review these wallets over the coming days to make sure legitimate activity is accounted for.

Please only import your private key into a trusted wallet app. Never share it with anyone or enter it on the KotM website.

5) Once the final filtering and redistribution are complete, rewards will be airdropped directly to your specified wallet in your selected currency.

We appreciate everyone who participated in the pilot. The results have given us a lot of confidence in what we're building, and there's much more to come.

$USDC 不交易的时候，可以获得收益，同时，还可以保留日常使用资金的流动性 ！

用户通过 TopNod 入金usdc ➡️ Axil Pot ➡️ 资金赎回T+0 和 T+7

text:
在接连出现CEX被盗事件后，很多人不禁灵魂发问：
如果交易所遇到极端安全事件，假设所有的热钱包都被清空，该怎么办？🤔

今天Gate给出了自己的答案——冷存储覆盖证明 (PoSEC)

有人可能要问，为什么要做冷存储覆盖证明呢，不是已经有储备金证明了吗？

和常见的储备金证明（PoR）对比。它们不是替代关系，而是分别回答两个独立的问题：储备金证明回答“资产够不够”，冷存储覆盖证明回答“资产放得安不安全”。

因为热钱包是交易所资产中最脆弱的一环，而传统的 PoR 恰恰把热钱包资产也计入了“储备”，从而掩盖了这种结构性风险。

用一个比喻来理解：PoR 像查看一个人的总资产净值，证明他“不破产”；而 PoSEC 像检查他有没有一笔锁在保险柜里、平时不动用的“救命钱”，专门用来应对“钱包被偷光”这种最坏情况。

Gate首创的冷存储覆盖证明已经正式上线，冷存储覆盖率达104.58%。换句话说，即便遇到极端情况，Gate依然能为你兜底。

安全问题透支行业信任，Gate始终将用户资产安全置于首位，并愿意成为安全领域的先行者，推动行业不断进步。💪

text:
经常有小伙伴问我，怎么用 AI 做出好看的产品设计，不那么 AI Slop，其实不是很好答，因为自己也不是专业的，只能站在产品工程师视角来给大伙聊一聊，怎么做出不丑且易用的产品。

首先要知道一个前提，很多时候好看的设计也救不了不解决问题的产品，设计在这里只是锦上添花的作用，而非决定产品的成败，假如要我选择产品优先级，应该是能解决问题 > 易于使用 > 好看美观，好比先解决不饿着、再解决温饱、最好解决吃好一样。

能解决问题这里不多说，更多取决于产品本身，它是去解决一个具体的需求，有人需要，有场景需要，刚好你这个产品可以提供一个解决方案让人或者 Agent 使用完成目标就好了，只不过解决问题有大有小。

那么如何做易用且不丑的产品呢？哈哈，可以照着走一遍，也可以把下面的这一大段给你的 Agent 让他去帮你 Review 一下你的产品代码仓库。

1. 把自己当做一个普通不懂技术的小白，他拿到我们产品，能否把主链路走完产出他所需要的东西，哪些地方有卡点，哪些地方没有讲明白，哪些地方的衔接不通顺，全部去修复，让用户不用说明书也可以完成产品的使用，假如实在不能，可以适当补充提示说明。

2. 所有文案需要符合对应语言当地人的使用习惯，需要仔细斟酌词藻，不要干巴巴的翻译，可以从 Apple、Windows 系统以及知名网站去找同类词的最好翻译和解释，文案做到尽可能让本地人感觉非常简单、易懂、清晰。

3. 产品上能用产品本身表达清楚的地方就不要再加文案说明，不要啰嗦的解释一个东西，仔细思考每一个说明文案是否达意且不啰嗦，交互视觉可以说清楚的地方就不要用文案再表达一遍。

4. 在数字的表达上需要让用户明白这个数据指的内容，以及考虑到数据表达意思后的易读，比如钱、指标、距离各种单位需要考虑到本身的最佳实践，数据的准确性非常重要，不要为了偷懒少了数据的校验。

5. 对于用户确定的操作不需要反复找用户确定，只有在会产生不可逆影响的时候二次找用户确定是否需要执行，防止满屏都是各种弹框确定，对于危险的操作不要出现大片的红，需要考虑用户操作一个产品的愉悦度，用户不是傻子不要过度担心会犯错。

6. 视觉上，一个页面只留一个强调色，尽量不要使用橙色、陶土色和后台常见的那种老企业亮蓝色，灰色全部用偏暖的灰，不使用冷冰冰的蓝灰，找不到合适的颜色可以去中国传统颜色里面去找到合适的。

7. 字号类型尽可能少一点，一个页面最多控制4种不同的字号，需要考虑到页面整体的阅读节奏感，清晰感以及文字的对比度，确保符合无障碍，包括考虑到行间间、字间距、段落间距需要反复调整，同时保持整体的规范一致。

8. 少用斜体、等宽字体、全大写，要用的场景必须要有详细的理由说明，说明文案不要使用斜体，等宽字体只用于代码、路径、指标，按钮和标签里面的字不要大写，少用中间点 · 来连接内容。同一个动作在整个产品里面只用一个动词，此外动词的考虑尽量不要催促用户去执行，比如少用立即购买这种营销词。

9. 页面的按钮、间距、圆角、分割线、弹窗、动画、阴影这类设计规范保持一致，同时保持克制，不打扰用户，嵌套的圆角要同心，里面的圆角等于外面的圆角减去间距会更好看。页面默认是平的，不叠阴影、不发光、不加毛玻璃，阴影只给真正浮起来的弹窗，不要卡片套卡片。

10. 在多语言的环境下，优先考虑最长文案的排布，优先考虑达意而非为了好看而改变原意，可以改文案，但不要变字号和截断。需要特别考虑在不同尺寸下的展示效果是否都良好，考虑到用户常用的设备，全部去测试，遇到不好的地方全部修复。

11. 对于反复调整不好的设计，或者做了好多轮都感觉不好看的设计，让 Agent 帮你出3个他认为最好的方案来让你挑选，然后你选择一个更好的，告诉他去优化，直到改到你满意，我比较喜欢让 AI 生成对比前后的图片放到一个pdf里面，这样我的阅读对比体验会更好。

大概就是上面这些，不过还有一个非常重要的就是你自己的耐心和反复调整，我比较强迫症，经常会因为了一个文案、一个颜色、一个设计和 AI 讨论十几轮，直到自己满意了才舒服，虽然 AI 很聪明，但是很多时候你对他的要求要更多，以及你需要付出更多的时间和耐心，才可以做出满意的效果，或者说你多花时间，多去看好的设计，其实就可以做出易用不丑的产品了。

He also believes digital credit and bank lending could absorb all new Bitcoin supply, while monetary expansion, institutional investment, tokenization, and the 2028 halving could further drive demand.

text:
币安学习营回程的飞机上，终于有时间一个人静下来，记录这次的真实感受。

这次Trust Wallet以赞助商身份参与活动，
所以我看到的是一个第三方视角，
也想和大家分享。

-KOL线下活动，真的只是吃喝玩乐吗？

网上晒出来的都是海岛、沙滩、椰林， 但说实话，
KOL们在线下的投入程度远超我的想象。

每天早上9点到9点半开课，大家基本准时坐齐。

偌大的宴会厅安安静静，
我坐在最后一排，
还看到好几位KOL把PPT从第一页拍到最后一页。

就像土澳大师兄私下跟我聊到，
这波行情比较迷茫，
他甚至消沉了好一阵。
但借着线下机会和大家聊下来，
还是发现了不少潜在机会。

所以推文里看到的只是皮毛，
真正有价值的东西，还是要面对面聊。

— 为什么币安要在这个节骨眼上办海岛学习营？

最后一天的毕业典礼上，
一姐线上连线，
亲自回答了这个问题：

内部其实紧急讨论过，
但如果取消，
外面一定会传出“币安没钱了”之类的谣言。

不如踏踏实实，照常把线下交流的机会留给大家。

— Trust作为一个钱包，赞助这个活动有什么意义？

这是Trust Wallet第一次赞助纯华语区的活动。

我的大师课分享结束后，
有十几位老师主动在推特上分享Trust Wallet的内容，

还有几位KOL私下跟我说：
“没想到你们Trust的增长数据这么好。”

还有两位做返佣的老师，
在颠簸的车上一路拉着我给Trust提建议，好奇Trust CEO Felix的产品风格和方向，
建议我们做出差异化，
甚至还给了一些很有创意的想法。

这两个瞬间，让我觉得这就是Trust赞助的意义所在。

— 做线下活动，本质上是个苦力活

别人看到的可能是吃喝玩乐， 作为半个工作人员，我看到了另一面。

KOL们的航班晚点两小时，
晚上九点还没到。
sisi、丫丫、May、Mia、Alina、kim几位工作人员一直没吃饭，在暴雨里陪大家一起等，
直到所有人都吃上饭，她们才去吃。

其实这趟行程确实很波折。

沙滩晚宴摆好的Trust周边，
被突如其来的狂风暴雨淋湿，
我和同事冲去抢救物料，被淋成了落汤鸡；

陪了我五年的可爱行李箱，
惨遭航空公司毒手，摔得西八惨烈；

还有和老师们一起盯着暴跌的账户，
半天说不出一句话。

黑天鹅总比想象中多，
我们能做的，
只有调整心态，迎接挑战。

毕竟负面谣言，永远跑得更快， 而正面的建设，总显得微不足道。

飞机上的一些碎碎念， 祝大家周末愉快， 月底我们泰国BBW见！🌴

text:
这可能昨晚纳指一个巨大实体阴线且没有一丝下影线迹象的元凶，大摩衍生品团队美东时间5号中午（正好昨晚美股盘中）推算：假设价格维持在下午1点的水平，收盘前杠杆ETF的被迫卖出规模约为520亿美元。其中仅半导体一个板块就要吃掉210亿，纳斯达克100再吃150亿。

核心就是两类产品：
1）杠杆ETF，比如“两倍做多纳斯达克”。它们每天收盘前必须做一件事：把当天的盈亏重新平衡回目标杠杆比例。当市场大跌时，这意味着它们必须在收盘前卖出大量股票——跌得越惨，卖得越多，这是被动的、机械的、不可避免的。
2）还有一类叫波动率控制基金（Vol Control），当市场波动率飙升时，它们会系统性地降低股票仓位——同样是机械的，且通常滞后一到两天执行。

所以昨晚美股这两股力量叠加在一起，规模很大。报告出来、那华尔街不得炸锅了，这520亿的“死亡倒计时”变成了人尽皆知的明牌。知道了这笔机械卖单，交易员们的反应是什么？自然是“抢跑”。

逻辑很简单：既然收盘前会有一波大规模被动抛售，那我现在就卖，等它砸完了再低价买回来。

所以我们就看到昨晚上纳指收了一个巨大的实体阴线、尾盘放了巨量。

text:
Robinhood Chain的野心，可能远不止再造一条公链！PONS或许正站在新生态的入口。

11月6日，X上的加密行业账号 Ripe（@BTCKiK）发布了一篇对Robinhood创始人兼CEO Vlad Tenev 最新发言的整理，其中几个观点值得关注。

Vlad的核心意思是：Robinhood认真研究了其他生态，却发现没有一条链能够完全满足自己的需求，因此决定自己建链，目标是打造全球领先的真实世界资产（RWA）与Meme双头驱动的公链。

几个细节尤其值得关注：

股票代币化： 已经上链，未来还会围绕股票代币构建更多产品。
Permissionless： 任何人都可以在链上部署自己的应用和产品。
AI Agent： 将成为未来链上金融的重要组成部分。
RWA与加密融合： 真实世界资产与加密金融融合，有机会让整个市场规模实现数量级增长。
生态扩张： 长期目标是将Robinhood美国版App中的产品尽可能迁移到链上。

这意味着Robinhood想做的，可能不是一条单纯依靠加密原生用户生存的公链，而是把传统金融用户、股票资产、Meme文化和链上金融连接起来。

那么，PONS的机会在哪里？

PONS作为Robinhood Chain上的Meme发射平台，如果能够持续吸引创作者、用户和交易资金，就有机会成为这条链早期的重要流量入口。

想象一下：

未来Robinhood Chain不仅有股票代币化，还有Meme、AI Agent、衍生品和各种Permissionless金融应用，整个生态需要的不只是基础设施，也需要能够持续创造用户和交易活动的应用平台。

当然，生态发展不等于PONS一定成功，Robinhood也没有因此宣布PONS为官方合作伙伴。

但我认为，研究PONS不能只盯着今天的价格和市值。

如果Robinhood Chain未来成为连接传统金融与加密世界的重要入口，那么早期建立用户和交易网络的应用，是否有机会获得生态扩张的红利？

这才是我真正关注PONS的原因。

币圈小玩家——专注基本面与低估值机会研究。

text:
The next wave of fund investors runs on software: neobanks, onchain reserve managers and, soon, AI agents.

For regulated funds to reach them, infrastructure must evolve. Combining onchain vaults with digital transfer agency brings more of the fund lifecycle into the same system.
author: centrifuge
quoted_text:
Vaults give funds a native onchain structure. A digital transfer agent adds the rest of what a regulated fund needs: the shareholder register, investor onboarding, transfer controls and investor servicing. Put both on the same stack and the whole fund lifecycle can be automated, from subscription to redemption.

What that looks like:
- the register and the onchain holdings are the same record
- onboarding status decides who can subscribe and transfer
- transfer restrictions are enforced by the share token itself
- subscriptions, redemptions and investor servicing run programmatically
- the share can plug into wallets, markets and apps while ownership and servicing stay in sync

So a regulated fund can run onchain with far less manual work in between.

Excited to build this with @itsjawknee___ .

text:
BAIDU JUST DROPPED AN ABSOLUTE GAME-CHANGER FOR DOCUMENT AI

It’s called `Unlimited-OCR`, and it can literally transcribe an entire book in a single pass 🤯

Most vision models read a single page, forget the context, and eventually hit a wall where performance degrades and inference slows down.

@Baidu_Inc built this on top of `DeepSeek OCR` but fixed the memory bloat with a single change to the attention mechanism.

The design mimics how a human hand-copies a book.

Instead of trying to hold the entire book in active memory, each token only looks at the current page plus the last 128 words.

This creates a sliding window that keeps memory usage completely flat, no matter how long the output gets.

The architectural shift delivers three massive upgrades for document parsing:
→ A fixed memory footprint
→ Steady generation speed on massive documents
→ The ability to process dozens of pages per pass

The numbers back it up.

Unlimited-OCR scores 93% on standard parsing benchmarks, beating the older baseline by a full six points.

Even when pushed past 40 pages, the error rate stays under 0.11.

More importantly, it maintains a flat speed curve where older models suffered a 35% slowdown.

Free and open-source.

Repo, weights and paper in 🧵↓

text:
想稳定用 Claude 的，不被封号的，日常有刚需的！

听我的，用 Devin 吧！

有几点理由：

1，可以满血用 Opus 5.5 ,不注水，不降智。Pro 额度少点，但 Max 经测试有 5 倍左右的 API额度。

2，有个混合模式，有点意思，就是你可以把难度高的，有设计的任务给到 Opus 模型来执行，粗活可以分配给，它自己的免费模型来做。

说是自研的模型是基于 Kimi K3 训练的，编程能力只比 Fable 5 低了一分。所以能力也相当不错。

3，如果你同时有 GPT 的订阅，它可以直接调用 GPT 额度。Tibo 也帮着做过宣传。

这就有意思了。

大家多数人反应Codex 的Harness基座可能过于庞大，用起来比较慢，也笨。

Devin 的小巧灵活，调用 GPT 的模型，速度和智能方面都有了显著的提升。

4，它可以调用全部模型，这你敢信？

前沿模型都可以随时切换，写作编程，选择不同模型来做。随时切回，相当于自己是个 CC switch了。

简单问题，直接用他自己的免费额度。做动画，就调用 Claude 的 Opus 系列。

总结一下：有缺点吗？

有，我实测 20 美元的订阅，Opus 的额度不多，比Cursor 都扣。

但是上 200 美金的订阅，这个额度就是相对可以的。 5 倍 API 的额度，要啥自行车啊。关键是不封号啊。

如果对 Claude有刚需的朋友们，可以考虑一下。

还有界面就是全英文，需要你有点文化。

第三方里，它算是比较良心的（200 美元的订阅）当然和官方没法比。

Pro 就没必要定了，体验用的。

text:
DEUX PUISSANCES. DEUX HISTOIRES. DEUX ÂMES.

D'un côté, les États-Unis.
De l'autre, la Chine.

On te dit que l'une est la liberté, l'autre est la dictature.
On te dit que l'une est le bien, l'autre est le mal.

Mais regarde l'histoire. La vraie. Pas celle des films.

LES ÉTATS-UNIS : UNE PUISSANCE BÂTIE SUR LE VOL.

L'Amérique n'est pas née du travail. Elle est née du vol.

On vole la terre des Amérindiens. On les massacre, on les parque dans des réserves, on leur prend tout.
On vole des millions d'Africains. On les enchaîne, on les vend, on les fait travailler gratuitement pendant 250 ans pour construire le coton, le tabac, la richesse du Sud.
On vole le Mexique. La moitié du Mexique devient le Texas, la Californie, l'Arizona.
On vole le monde entier après 1945. Avec le dollar, avec les guerres, avec la CIA, avec les coups d'État. Chili, Iran, Irak, Libye, Vietnam, Panama. La liste est trop longue.

Et après, on appelle ça la liberté. On appelle ça le capitalisme. On appelle ça le rêve américain.

Mais quel rêve ? Le rêve de celui qui vole et qui dit aux volés : "Travaillez dur, vous y arriverez aussi."

Le capitalisme américain, c'est ça : une poignée qui possède tout, et des millions qui travaillent pour eux, qui s'endettent pour se soigner, qui dorment dans la rue à Los Angeles, à 50 mètres des villas de Beverly Hills.

C'est une puissance qui se construit sur la fourberie. Sur la ruse. Sur la guerre. Sur l'esclavage.

LA CHINE : UNE PUISSANCE BÂTIE SUR LE Labeur.

La Chine, c'est l'histoire inverse.

Pendant 100 ans, de 1840 à 1949, la Chine est humiliée. On l'appelle le siècle de l'humiliation.

Les Anglais lui imposent l'opium. Ils droguent tout un peuple pour le voler.
Les Français, les Allemands, les Russes, les Japonais, les Américains découpent la Chine comme un gâteau. Ils prennent Hong Kong, Macao, Shanghai, Qingdao, Taïwan.
Le Japon envahit. Nankin. 300 000 morts. L'Unité 731. Des expériences sur des humains vivants.

En 1949, la Chine est le pays le plus pauvre du monde. Le peuple mange de l'herbe. L'espérance de vie est de 35 ans. Il n'y a pas d'industrie. Pas d'écoles. Pas d'hôpitaux. Rien.

Et là, que fait la Chine ?

Elle ne va pas voler un autre pays. Elle ne va pas coloniser l'Afrique. Elle ne va pas faire la guerre pour du pétrole.

Elle travaille.

Le peuple chinois travaille. Des millions de paysans, d'ouvriers, d'ingénieurs, de médecins, de professeurs, travaillent jour et nuit, génération après génération, pour reconstruire leur pays de leurs propres mains.

Ils construisent des barrages. Des chemins de fer. Des autoroutes. Des hôpitaux. Des écoles. Des usines. Des villes entières sorties de nulle part.

En 70 ans, 800 millions de personnes sortent de la pauvreté. C'est le plus grand miracle de l'histoire humaine. Aucun pays capitaliste n'a jamais fait ça. Jamais.

Et aujourd'hui, la Chine a les trains les plus rapides du monde. Les ponts les plus longs. Les villes les plus sûres. Les hôpitaux qui soignent tout le monde, même les plus pauvres.

Pas parce qu'elle a volé. Parce qu'elle a travaillé.

ET POURTANT, ON TE DIT QUE LE COMMUNISME NE MARCHE PAS.

Les États-Unis passent leur temps à combattre le communisme. Ils disent que c'est le mal. Qu'il faut le détruire.

Mais regarde.

Le capitalisme américain a besoin de la guerre pour survivre. Il a besoin de vendre des armes. Il a besoin de piller.

Le communisme chinois a besoin du labeur pour survivre. Il a besoin de construire. Il a besoin de la vertu. Du sens du collectif. De l'idée que le pays passe avant l'individu. Que l'intérêt du peuple passe avant le profit d'une entreprise.

Les États-Unis ont la puissance de l'argent.
La Chine a la puissance du travail.

Les États-Unis ont la puissance de la fourberie.
La Chine a la puissance de la vertu.

L'une a construit sa puissance en écrasant les autres.

I feel like we're going to have as much fun gaming as we did 10 years ago!!!

text:
在一个无人在意的角落，百度悄悄发布了他们的下一代基础模型，文心5.5 Flash Base，而且直接开源了权重。

280B总参数，14B激活参数，使用33.5T Tokens完成预训练，微调和推理阶段最长支持1M上下文。

我仔细看了一下官方的Benchmark，成绩确实还挺不错的。
百度把它和DeepSeek、腾讯混元、小米MiMo的同级别参数的模型放在一起比较，在30项Benchmark中拿下了24项第一。
当然，这里需要说明一下，它对比的是其他厂商此前发布的Base模型，没有和现在各家最新的后训练版本比较。
但这次确实基本是同参数规模对比，几家的总参数都在280B～310B之间，激活参数也比较接近，腾讯甚至达到了21B。
所以至少从模型尺寸上看，百度这次的成绩还是有含金量的（但是base model对于用户有什么价值么）。

不过看到这个模型发布，我突然想起来，百度最近的模型团队好像正在经历一轮密集的人事变动。
今年7月，97年出生的孙天祥接手基础模型研发部。
10月底，在百度工作了20年的原文心大模型负责人吴甜确认离职，随后宣布加盟三一集团。
紧接着，11月初，又有消息称，百度文心大模型后训练负责人刘璟也离职了，下一站可能是中关村学院。
同时据爆料，后训练团队还有几个人提出了离职，内部在大模型研发方向上也存在不同意见。

这就很有意思了。
因为百度昨天开源的，恰好是一个刚完成预训练、还没有经过中期训练和后训练的Base模型。
官方说，完成后训练的文心5.5 Flash还会在后面推出。
结果现在Base模型的Benchmark确实很能打，负责后训练的人却先走了。
我现在还真有点好奇，接下来这个模型的后训练准备让谁来做。

不过还是希望百度能把这个模型做好。
这次Base的成绩也证明他们依然有能力做出有竞争力的模型。
希望下一次看到文心的新闻，是模型又进步了，而不是团队又少了几个人。

毕竟很多人都是从PaddlePaddle第一次接触的机器/深度学习。

text:
民主党限制 AI 发展是半导体和 AI 大跌的原因 ？民主党发出禁止超级 AI 的禁令？？违者判 20 年？？？

周三在民主党获得两会后半导体和 AI 就在下跌，到了周四这下跌更加的严重了，很多小伙伴都说是民主党在限制 AI ，甚至还有媒体发出了美国民主党禁止超级 AI 的禁令，甚至个人违规会被判处 20 年，企业违规直接解散的新闻。

先辟谣一下，媒体发的本身是真的，但这只是一个议员提出的议案，别说成为法律了，就连边都够不到，而且这条信息是9月24日的，这都超过40天了，更炸裂的是，这条议案的提出者并不是民主党人士，是独立人士，只是长期于民主党合作罢了。😂😂

就像共和党参议员 Cynthia Lummis 也提出过法案，希望美国政府在五年内购买 100 万枚 Bitcoin 一样，这只是一个提议，距离成为法案还有 八 辈子那么远呢。更扯不到什么民主党提出的，完全就是“无脑爽文”。

实际上，确实是有部分民主党对于 AI 的发展加以限制，担心 AI 发展过快、失去控制，也有人关注数据中心的大量用电、用水以及对当地居民的影响。但民主党内部并没有统一到都支持暂停 AI 研发的程度。另一部分议员仍然支持美国发展 AI，希望在推动研发的同时制定安全和监管规则。

而这次半导体和 AI 股下跌，民主党胜选带来的监管预期确实是原因之一。市场担心民主党控制国会后，会对 AI 公司和数据中心建设进行更严格的审查，得州和佐治亚州等数据中心重要地区的选举结果，也让投资者担心未来项目审批和建设可能放缓。

但这次下跌也有其它原因的。比如 AI 企业建设数据中心需要投入大量资金，在利率和融资成本较高的情况下，投资者一直在担心这些投入多久才能收回，再比如油价开始上涨，这些都是导致 AI 和半导体板块下跌的原因，而所谓的民主党禁止 AI 发展起码目前来看，尚未成立。

从另一个层面来说，AI 的发展已经是美国的支柱产业。并不是任何一个党派想要禁止就能禁止的，美国科技公司投入大量资金建设数据中心、购买芯片和服务器，这些投入也带动了电力、建筑和设备等行业。美联储的研究也提到，数据中心、软件和计算机设备等相关投资，已经对美国经济增长作出了明显贡献。

同时 AI 也关系到美国和其他国家的科技竞争，民主党和共和党内部都有支持美国继续发展 AI 的议员。在这样的情况下，全面禁止 AI 发展会面临很大的政治和经济阻力。

换一个角度想，就像是在互联网高度发展的时代，有人说美国禁止互联网发展了，有可能吗？不过，对先进模型加强安全审查，或者限制部分地区的数据中心建设，这确实是有可能的。

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
为啥周四美股开盘后大跌了？不是中期大选利好吗？为啥 Bitcoin 也跌了？？

😂我晚上开始码字到现在还没有一个小时就出现大跌了，Bitcoin 都已经跌了超过 6% 了，这种情况下原罪大概率是出在美股身上，果然英伟达、AMD 和数据中心相关股票都在下跌，也就是科技股和 AI 都在下跌。

主要的原因就是民主党获胜，等等，不是说民主党获胜是利好吗？你 TMD 昨天还说是利好，怎么今天就是利空了？好坏坏话怎么都你一个人说的！！

先别打，这个逻辑是这样的。

昨天是因为民主党获得了胜利，控制了国会，尤其是参议院民主党领袖舒默都表示要结束美国和伊朗的战争了，这个利好确实带动了市场的上涨，甚至是 bitcoin:native ，这是没错的。

但就像昨天有小伙伴说的一样，这不是利好吗？为啥科技股在下跌，科技股昨天和今天下跌的原因都是一样的！主要原因就是因为数据中心建设的不确定性增加。

实际上民主党在得州、佐治亚州等数据中心建设较集中的地区取得胜利，部分地方民众此前就反对数据中心扩张，担心用电、用水和电费上涨。投资者担心，未来部分项目可能面临更严格审批或暂停建设。如果数据中心建得慢，芯片、服务器和算力供应商的订单增长也可能受到影响。

说人话，民主党没有那么激进，所以在民主党主要获选的地区可能就为了选票而降低对 AI 数据中心的支持，而且现在本身市场就担心 AI 的扩张带来了资本开支的增加，结果科技股的投资者就开始担心，出现了抛售。

这是第一个主要原因，其次就是油价又开始回升了，主要是市场昨天买入的是情绪，今天卖出的是情绪落地，所以我是在早晨看到油价反弹的时候就直接清空了做空的仓位，如果不算资金费率的是小赚，算了资金费率仍然是亏损的，但我觉得只要伊朗有明确的信号，我就在做空就行了。

上一轮七月就是因为觉得还能跌硬生生的从 80% 的利润变成了超过 100% 的亏损，和头疼的资金费率，所以这次就更果断了。

而在 bitcoin:native 我还是判断错了，虽然我知道 AI 会跌，油价上涨了，但是白天就已经是这样了，但白天 BTC 没啥动静啊，我就觉得 BTC 问题不大，结果到时间就买入抄底了，结果就成这样了，但我觉得现在买入的问题仍然不会很大，我在继续做空油价的时候，BTC 的价格就应该回来了。

但 AI 和半导体，我给小伙伴的建议就是不要着急抄底。

这张卡来自 2019 年日版 SM10b《スカイレジェンド》，是 TAG TEAM GX 时代非常有代表性的一张卡
火焰鸟、闪电鸟、急冻鸟三只传说鸟用彩绘玻璃拼在一起辨识度极高。
作为初代三神鸟 + TAG TEAM + 教堂彩窗画风的结合，这张在日月时代的 TAG TEAM 收藏里属于门面级别的存在。平台 FMV 3306U

喷火龙
这张喷火龙来自 2016 年日版 CP6由 有田满弘绘制，用的就是大家最熟悉的那版经典喷火龙：张着嘴喷火、翅膀展开、红底金边。20周年那一弹开始把初代神绘重新收录进来

九尾
这张九尾来自 2009 年日版 L1，是 LEGEND 世代的闪卡，画师是 TOKIYA。卡面最大的特点是九尾几乎占据整个画面，周围带着流动的绿白色能量，有一种油画质感，和后来很多偏平的卡面很不一样。
作为 HGSS 时期的老闪，时间属性和画风都在。

2021 年日版剑盾时代的 S-P Promo
不是卡包抽出来的，而是 2020–2021 赛季冠军积分达到 30 分以上的选手才能拿到的奖励卡，卡面上皮卡丘带着小火龙、杰尼龟、妙蛙种子一起庆祝，还带有 Championship Series 2021 的标识，节日氛围很足。
因为是赛事积分兑换的限定配布，流通本来就不是公开包抽那套逻辑。平台 FMV 也是 504U，和上面那张九尾一个价位，抽到的话可以当一张有故事的 Promo 留下来。

text:
TESTBED is the new open-source toolkit setting the gold standard for Bayesian experimental design. It breaks down the whole workflow into modular, reusable pieces—so you can mix, match, and drop in new models or algorithms with just a few lines of code.

With 8 benchmark tasks, fast estimators (up to 10^9 samples), and reference implementations of every major BED method since 2020, TESTBED runs the largest head-to-head comparison yet: identical compute, identical architectures, every method, every task.

Key findings:
– Adding time embeddings to policy architectures can boost performance by 5+ nats—enough to flip the rankings.
– Static designs, tuned with enough compute, rival learned policies on several “canonical” benchmarks; some community tasks may be too easy.
– Simple variational-posterior methods are just as strong as more complex algorithms if you match the architecture and compute.
– More contrastive samples during training outweigh less frequent updates.

If you work on experiment planning, adaptive surveys, or automated scientific instruments, TESTBED is the plug-and-play framework—and the empirical reality check—you need.

Get the full analysis here: https://t.co/kpdJJklynA

text:
突然的闪崩，
不仅让我开始缩减接下来的「旅行预算」，
甚至重新打开了PDD，准备海淘泡面。
行情不好的时候，能省一点是一点。

昨天晚上和小伙伴聊起最近都在用什么AI，
也聊到了一个很现实的问题：AI 的使用成本。
我们发现一个很有意思的现象：
免费版GPT和收费版GPT，根本不是一个物种！GO版本和PRO版本，也完全不是一个物种。

既然不同版本的体验差距这么大，那么当我们为了省钱，选择通过API调用AI模型时，又该怎么确定服务商提供的，真的是我们付费购买的那个模型？

同一个模型 ID，不同服务商可能使用不同版本、不同精度，甚至存在工具调用失效、上下文缩水等问题。更麻烦的是，这些问题未必会体现在API的返回结果中。

针对这个问题，Mira Network @miranetwork 推出了Sterling|Sterling提供的是经过验证的推理服务。
Mira会持续对每个模型背后的服务商进行五项检查，包括模型身份、工具调用、参数遵循、静默故障和上下文长度，并公开验证评分。Sterling 则根据验证结果，优先将请求路由给通过验证的服务商。
目前首批支持 Claude、GPT 和 Gemini，DeepSeek、GLM 也即将上线。
使用上只需要一个API Key，支持USDC或MIRA支付，部分模型上线期间最高享50% 折扣。

我觉得，随着AI的发展，大家关注的不应该只有模型有多强，还应该关注模型背后的推理服务是否真实、稳定、可信。
毕竟，行情不好可以少吃几顿好的，但花钱调用 AI，至少应该确保自己买到的是真正想要的服务。

It's fairly easy to make a fake seinfeld clip that tricks 50% of people. Harder to trick 80% of people, extremely hard to trick 99% of people

We have an assumption though that this will nonetheless happen. At some point, the technology will improve enough that tricking virtually 100% of people will be effortless. It's probably true

But there's a chance that instead, people decide it takes too many resources and isn't worth it to progress past an arbitrary point. Maybe they decide tricking 98% is good enough and more on.

This happens a lot in society. You can break almost every law without getting caught if you're top 2% determined/resourceful. It's often not cost-effective to make something robust against the extreme tail edgecases

In the case of AI video this would result in there being a group of people, the 2% with the highest discernment, being trapped in some cartoonish hell where everyone in their life is constantly sitting there laughing at these AI generated videos, sharing AI generated news, forwarding AI generated reels with them saying things like "haha, this is so true, check it out man!"

As they sit there slowly going insane, knowing that this is all totally fake but being unable to prove it to anyone

text:
我自己做的 BTC 面板这一轮只亮了两天，那两天我在搬家，就这么踏空了。

先说下我的仓位。我的「BTC 估值面板」是左侧抄底的策略，价格没到就不触发。这一轮它只触发了 5.7 万那两天，我想着怎么也不可能一轮就两天在低估区域吧，没想到最后真的就只有两天。

面板是我自己一行一行搭的，结果偏偏是它让我踏空了，BTC 突破 120 日均线那次我一点都没买到，这个我当时真的有点接受不了。挣扎了一段时间，才在 7.7 万刀左右补了一个底仓。

底仓之外，我手里一直拿着大量现金，看着别人买入以后资产上涨，我心里也会有挣扎，难受。

我会怕，怕被别人超过，怕被这个时代落下。尤其是做了那么多面板还是买不到底部，有一阵我是真的怀疑自己是不是很笨。

我承认，嫉妒、攀比、想赢、怕输，这些我全都有，我也是正常人。

从 BTC 突破 120 日均线开始，我无数次想追高。

每次有情绪我就去和 AI 聊，拿荣格说的「阴影」剖自己——阴影说白了就是你不愿意承认自己有的那部分，上面那些怕和比，全在里面。一遍一遍地剖析自己，不断整合自己，一直没有出手。

中间我把更多时间放在了美股研究上，除了 CRCL，也开始看 AI 的 beta 资产。谷歌这些大公司跌下来，我去研究为什么跌，才明白大家对 AI 的预期变了——不是不信 AI 了，是不知道投出去的钱什么时候能赚回来。

美股这边我也没躲过。SOXL 我从 100 刀开始抄，90、80、70 一路往下买，现在浮亏 50%（账面亏，还没卖）；DRAM 买完就没再动过，也是浮亏 50%。好在两个仓位都很小，但亏起来一样肉疼。

之前不太懂三倍做多的资产来回震荡是有磨损的，这也算是踩了个坑，交学费了。

但其实对我来说，真正难熬的不是这点亏损，还是手里一大堆现金，看着别人买完就涨，这让我痛苦得多。

直到昨天，终于等到一个我觉得还不错的位置。

昨天我买了 BTC、CRCL、SOXX、SMH，都是我长期看好的资产。SMH 和 SOXX 的历史回撤我自己回测过，我觉得这两个的「赔率」开始有了，现在这个位置划算了。除了 BTC 还不算特别便宜，其他几个我觉得都到了不错的位置。

现在打出去了 40% 多的仓位，手里还有 50% 多的现金。

接下来怎么走我不知道。但用我们练体操的话说，这一次没有「动作变形」，没犯大错，没有大回撤。

等一个合适的位置真的很难，尤其是看着别人赚钱的时候，更难。我认为好的投资可能真的就是等一个合适的价格，甚至是别人都恐慌的价格，昨天的美股有一点这个味道了。说起来简单，经历一次才知道，长期不动比天天操作难太多——既要对市场保持敏感，又不能因为敏感就乱动。

这几个月我觉得过得特别漫长，一直在和心里那些阴影打交道，一点一点整合，一点一点把情绪调回来。我相信往后会越练越好，但这个过程真的不轻松，经历过一次才知道有多不容易。

这一轮我最大的收获可能不是昨天买在哪，而是这几个月没乱动。

这不是投资建议，只是我来时的路，后面加不加仓我也还没想好。

text:
Weeks of legal work. And the taker still carries the dealer’s counterparty risk.
Every OTC derivatives trade where the dealer asks for collateral to be posted directly to them opens the same conversation:

→ Are the assets segregated?
→ What can the dealer do with them?
→ What insolvency protections apply?
→ Which jurisdiction governs a dispute or insolvency?
→ What does enforcement look like?

Then come the drafts, redrafts, and legal and risk sign-offs on every term. It can takes weeks, sometimes months. And the taker still carries the dealer’s counterparty risk, whilst the assets sit on the dealer’s balance sheet without protections.

There is another way: ClearLoop Assigned Collateral (CAC).

With CAC, collateral assets still sit on the dealer’s balance sheet, but they’re ring-fenced within Copper, restricted to use on connected exchanges through ClearLoop and cannot be withdrawn. The protection isn’t negotiated. It’s enforced by the infrastructure.

For dealers, that means faster onboarding of new takers. For takers, it could be the difference between executing this quarter and executing next year.

#ClearLoop

HYPE has been underperforming recently despite one of its biggest catalysts of the year, fully retracing the entire announcement candle.

Many people argue that this happened because Democrats won the midterm elections, creating significant uncertainty around the legalization of perps in the US.

But is this the entire reason behind the current price action, or is there something else going on?

We traced the onchain activity to see what was really happening and uncovered the real reason.

Hours after the NYSE announcement, FalconX (a well-known brokerage desk) received roughly 910k HYPE ($86M) from several different addresses. Between October 30 and November 3, they distributed most of that HYPE across Coinbase, OKX, and Bybit, likely to sell it over those days and the following ones, causing the dump.

Trace the transactions here: https://t.co/n6OGAmkfw0

Who did this HYPE belong to?

There's no way to know for sure, but our strongest lead points to Paradigm.

In August and September, they sent 692k and 770k HYPE to Coinbase Prime, respectively. They could have held most of it there until they found exit liquidity, and this announcement might have been the catalyst they'd been waiting for to liquidate those bags.

On November 1, Paradigm unstaked 2.55M HYPE. If their strategy is to keep some liquid HYPE in custody until they find new exit liquidity (e.g., when PURR trades above 1.2x mNAV and starts buying HYPE again), this unstaking makes sense, as they seem to have already sold all the liquid HYPE they had left.

So, at this point, there are three likely outcomes:
- If our theory is correct, they'll send that HYPE to Coinbase Prime, where it will sit for a while.
- If not, they might sell it or they might consolidate it into a single address.

text:
Citrini's "State of the Themes" article kinda strengthens the Onchain/Decentralized AI thesis
 
The article argued that the AI infra/semis trades are ending because Neoclouds/Hyperscalers CAPEX is hitting ~$1T while AI eco ARR is only $200B and the huge gap won't be filled any time soon. Plus, financing constraints, construction delays and model price competition add pressure to the trade
 
That creates an interesting setup for projects helping operators monetize existing capacity and buyers access cheaper compute.
 
This is where Onchain/Decentralized AI gets interesting
 
1. Turning idle/crowdsourced GPUs into revenue
 
GPU marketplaces like @lium_io help operators rent out unused capacity, connecting existing hardware with paying customers.
 
For data centers and smaller operators, better utilization means more revenue from assets they’ve already paid for. Buyers get more options and competitive pricing (e.g. rent idle B200s on @lium_io for $4.25/hr).
 
As financing gets tighter, making existing hardware earn more becomes increasingly valuable.
 
2. Building markets for surplus/excess inference
 
Inference Providers and AI gateways have inference capacity they can sell. Some are expirables because they run subsidy campaigns but they couldn't get users to fully use them.
 
@AskSurplus connects these participants through an inference marketplace, routing requests across discounted supply. Selected offers carry discounts of 50–99% relative to listed API prices.
 
This creates a way for sellers to monetize unused allocations and buyers to reduce their inference bills.
 
Onchain settlement and tokenized credits add building blocks for developers to create new markets, routing tools and products around that supply.
 
3. Bootstrapping inference networks with existing GPUs
 
Decentralized AI crowdsources idle GPUs across the world.
 
Token emissions are used to pay for compute & inference instead of debt & equity financing huge CAPEX for data center buildouts.
 
Teams like @engyai and @dphnAI are already proving that it's possible to host top open-weight models on a hybrid/fully decentralized network that's fast, reliable, and cheap for users.
 
The opportunity is to turn fragmented hardware into useful, competitively priced inference.
 
The economics become stronger as paying customer demand grows enough to support suppliers with progressively smaller subsidies.
 
4. Expanding access to GPU financing
 
@USDai_Official connects onchain capital with operators financing GPU infrastructure.
 
That gives smaller operators another route to funding hardware purchases and deployments, with loans secured by GPUs and supported by their cash flows.
 
As traditional financing becomes more selective, access to additional capital sources could become increasingly valuable.
 
5. Making inference access a tradable asset
 
Pilots of inference tokenization are happening onchain first
 
@AskVenice tokenized its platform credits into "DIEM", people are buying & selling inference like a commodity and builders are building on top of it, creating venues where users can speculate & earn from their credits.
 
This creates the market for future inference access. Users can acquire capacity, trade the token representing that access, and earn revenue from it (if they don't use it).
 
Other teams are experimenting with similar models, creating more ways to price, distribute and monetize inference.
 
For tokens, this creates a link with extraneous demand outside of crypto. The more people use the platform, the more valuable the credits, the more valuable the token.
 
The investment case gets stronger when usage translates into value for token holders
 
The best part is that this sector is growing fast and teams are starting to align interest with token holders through buybacks & burn, revenue distribution, and more utilities.
 
Onchain/Decentralized AI provides the opportunities for better GPU utilization, cheaper inference, new financing channels and tradable access to compute/inference.
 
All real economic problems that crypto teams are building products around them.
 
2025-26 is the year of AI infra/semiconductors
 
2027 will be the year of Onchain/Decentralized AI

Robinhood launched a chain for real-world assets.

Traders used it for memecoins.
@vladtenev cheered them on. Then he went silent for 22 days.

This is how Robinhood Chain out-traded Solana for a week, then lost the story.

July 1

- Robinhood Chain goes live
- "purpose-built for real-world assets from day one"

July 2

- Vlad on CNBC: "What's the benefit of making a million different memecoins?"

July 7

- daily DEX volume has gone from $1M to $56M in a week
- Vlad: "it works great for memes too"
- next day: $568M

July 17

- Vlad posts the two wolves meme. MEMES on one side, RWAs on the other
- "Why not both?"

This part is important.

August 6

- Robinhood lists $CASHCAT in its app
- It's still the only Robinhood Chain token you can buy there

Week of August 31

- Robinhood Chain does $18.0B in DEX volume
- Solana does $16.7B

September 3

- AMC's CEO calls Robinhood's stock tokens "vile"
- Vlad: "What's the concern?"

The next day

- Robinhood's top lawyer: "Send your lawyers and we'll educate them."

2 days later

- Vlad follows $MEME, a coin paired with the AMC stock token
- it goes from $37M to $178M in two minutes

September 17

- Vlad: "Tokenization is coming to America"
- hours later, his last chain post for 22 days

Meanwhile...

- HOOD Summit comes and goes without the chain on stage
- Robinhood asks what we want from its next 100 days. ~300 replies, no answers
- Coinbase lists $PONS. Robinhood still hasn't
- Binance keeps paying out its $4M Stonks Szn
- Raydium: "I like Stonk coins."

October 12

- a trader asks Vlad: "Why didn't you speak about the Robinhood Chain?"
- Vlad: "Fair feedback… we're not going anywhere."

October 19

- Vlad follows a parody account of himself
- its token goes 11x in a minute
- the chain's biggest memes still don't get a mention

October 27–28

- Earn for all, the new wallet integrations, 8 new stock tokens
- 14 of the chain's 16 biggest tokens go up
- Binance gets hacked the next day
- All coins go down again

So did the silence kill the memes?

I checked. Every chain's stock memes fell 64–72% from their own peaks. Solana kept posting and Binance paid $4M, but they got the same drop. The fall also started before the silence.

What moved money was what Robinhood did, like listing CASHCAT or Vlad following MEME.

November 4

- Robinhood's first chain roundup
- 23 builders, $1.8M in grants, zero memes

Vlad posted a meme about feeding both wolves.

Three and a half months later, the roundup he shared didn't name a single meme.

Dems won big in the midterms and even Vance blames the Iran war for the loss, so Hegseth is the obvious fall guy. Massie (R) will force an impeachment vote in the House next week, and odds jumped from ~30% to ~50%.

My take:
• Trump today: “I have every intention to keep him.” Voluntary resignation <5%.
• Leadership will likely move to table it, i.e. kill it before it’s even debated. GOP still controls the lame-duck House, but only ~4 defections or no-shows sink the tabling motion. Many Republicans just lost their seats and owe Trump nothing, so impeachment passing is a real risk (~30%).
• Even if impeached, removal needs 67 senators. Not happening.
• If it’s tabled, I expect odds back to ~30%.

Real risk: Trump swaps him on his own terms while the GOP Senate can still confirm a successor (until Jan 3).

I’m on No for Dec 31.

text:
聊聊中期选举、万斯、彼得蒂尔。

1、执政方天然就容易积累民愤，所以历史上中期选举执政方主要就赢过三次：

1934年：罗斯福的新政取得政治上的成功
1998年：克林顿受益于经济繁荣和反对党的过度攻击
2002年：小布什受益于911事件后的全国团结

所以懂王这种拉完了的，输，以及输的惨完全意料之中的。

2、有意思的是中期选举对金融市场的影响，摩根大通统计了1937—2025年的标普500表现：自1950年以来的19次中期选举，标普500在选举结束后12个月全部取得正收益。

3、既然中期选举大概率反对党赢，赢了后又很大概率形成跛脚政府，那为什么要有这种低效率的制度呢？

冠冕堂皇的理由有2个：
第一，美国宪法实际上是一套高度不信任掌权者的制度。
第二，为了让错误的事情难以发生，宁愿接受正确的事情推进缓慢。

其实我觉得还有一个角度是更有意思的：
中期选举其实对执政党也不是完全有害的，因为它可以起到提前泄洪民怨的作用。

我们想象一下，假设这次不是中期选举，而直接是总统大选，积攒了那么多民怨的情况下，共和党可能赢么？

正是有了中期选举，民怨释放了很大一部分，接下来2年执政党开始猥琐发育，反对党开始咄咄逼人，民怨很可能从执政党做错事，转移到反对党阻止执政党做对事上。直到大选前形成一个相对平衡的环境。

Anyway，目前我还是挺看好万斯的，一方面万斯算是少数特朗普政府里头脑清醒，膝盖又没那么软的人，也算的上是青年才俊；另一方面万斯背后站着彼得蒂尔、马斯克这帮人。我相信这群又聪明又有权势的人不至于坐等被清算。

要了解万斯的实力，就得了解彼得蒂尔：
彼得蒂尔，硅谷教父，Paypal黑帮核心，我愿称他为特朗普政府的黑衣宰相。他有多牛呢？

万斯，完全是彼得蒂尔一手精心栽培，直到成为副总统的；

David Sacks，特朗普前 AI 与加密政策特别顾问，现任总统科技顾问委员会联席主席，彼得蒂尔在 Paypal 的长期伙伴；

Michael Kratsios，白宫科技政策办公室主任，彼得蒂尔曾经的幕僚长；

彼得蒂尔创办公司 Palantir 深度参与美国国防与情报技术体系；

彼得蒂尔还是Mark Zuckerberg、Sam Altman的早期投资人和导师。

马斯克，不用介绍，世界首富，另外一个身份是 Paypal 黑帮核心。

接下来万斯表面上可能会跟特朗普做一定切割，特朗普也一定会配合的演一下双簧，因为民主党上来，老特也够吃一壶的，都被暗杀了几次了。

万斯真能当上总统的话，目前看对加密肯定是好事，拭目以待吧。

text:
1分钟FAQ了解香港加密税务新规

1️⃣ 新规定了炒币的人如何缴税吗？
并没有，这次只是规定了从2027年开始相关平台收集加密交易信息，进入跨境交互系统，怎么缴税还是沿用过去的方法。

2️⃣ 哪些信息会被收集？
用户的身份信息，加密币交易信息，平台转入转出，加密币之间互换以及和法币互换等

3️⃣ 哪些用户需要申报或者配合申报？
主要看个人税务居民所在地，而不是只看身份证、国籍或开户地址。用户做的是填税务居民自我证明，跨境申报是平台的事。

4️⃣ 申报完怎么缴税？
针对香港的情况，普通投资加密币投资，不需要缴资本利得税；只有“经营性交易业务”，才需要缴税；如果薪酬用加密币支付，也需要交薪俸税

5️⃣内地有加入这个加密税收互换地区吗？
草案上没有说明，实际操作未知，建议大家当作内地也可以获取信息。

6️⃣ 内地税务居民，境外炒币以后提现到香港卡，需要申报和缴税吗？
这种情况不需要向香港缴所得税，但是原则上需要缴内地的个人所得税，建议留好成本记录。另外，如果是法币，那么香港银行账户CRS 已经通了，内地可以获取银行账户余额信息。

7️⃣ 草案的最大意义是什么？
加密交易信息被跨境记录，政府查税会更加容易。
author: DeFiTeddy2020
quoted_text:
《香港通过加密税务新规，炒币赚的钱要交 20% 的税吗？》
11 月 4 日，香港立法会正式通过加密资产申报相关法案。从 2027 年起，符合规定的加密资产服务提供商将开始收集和申报用户交易资料，香港税务局计划于 2028 年首次与合作税务管辖区交换相关信息。

消息出来后，不少币圈用户开始担心：以后炒币要缴税了吗？把币安的钱提现到香港银行卡，会不会被征税？

这次新规并未增加加密货币交易税，不过，随着加密资产交易逐步纳入跨境税务信息交换体系，部分交易所的用户交易资料将受到更严格的申报要求。

🌟 以后炒币，哪些交易会被申报？
这次香港引入的是 OECD 制定的加密资产申报框架（CARF）。

根据香港税务局公布的规则，涉及的交易包括三类：
- 法币与加密资产兑换，例如用美元购买 BTC
- 加密资产之间兑换，例如 BTC 换成 USDT
- 以及部分加密资产转账，包括向外部钱包转移资产

符合条件的服务提供商需要收集用户姓名、税务居民身份、税务编号，以及不同资产的累计交易金额、数量和交易次数等资料。

即使用户没有提现到银行卡，只是在交易所买卖 BTC、ETH，或者将资产转入外部钱包，相关交易记录也可能被申报给税务机关。

🌟 什么样的人炒币需要缴税？
香港此次通过的是交易信息申报制度，没有新增针对加密货币交易的税种。 至于炒币收益是否需要缴税，可以分成三类情况。

第一类，内地税务居民。
根据内地《个人所得税法》，居民个人原则上需要就境内外应税所得纳税，其中财产转让所得适用 20% 的税率。不过，内地目前尚未针对个人加密货币交易收益出台统一、明确的征税细则，实际如何征税仍存在不确定性。

需要注意的是，即使通过境外交易所买卖加密货币，再把资金转入香港银行卡，也不会因此自动免除内地的纳税义务。

第二类，在香港进行长期投资的个人。
香港没有资本利得税，如果买入 BTC、ETH 等资产用于长期投资，之后出售获得的收益被认定为资本性质，通常不需要缴纳香港利得税。

即使偶尔进行交易，也不意味着一定要缴税，关键是投资行为是否具有经营性质。

第三类，在香港从事经营性交易的个人或机构。
如果高频交易、量化做市等活动构成在香港经营业务，并产生香港来源利润，就可能需要缴纳利得税。

符合两级制条件时，独资或合伙业务首 200 万港元应评税利润税率为 7.5%，公司为 8.25%；超过部分分别为 15% 和 16.5%。

🌟 从币安提现到香港卡，需要缴税吗？
这是普通用户最关心的问题。
从币安提现到香港银行卡，通常不会因为资金到账就产生额外税款。

举个例子，你在币安卖出 10 万 USDT，再通过法币渠道转入自己的香港银行卡。香港不会直接按照这笔到账金额征税，是否需要缴税，还要看资金来源、交易收益以及个人的税务居民身份。

对于长期生活在内地的用户，即使持有香港银行卡，仍可能属于内地税务居民，需要按照内地的相关税务规定处理加密资产收益。至于具体如何征税，目前仍未知。

此外，香港银行对加密资产相关资金的审核比较严格。用户可能需要提供交易记录、资金来源证明等材料，部分银行还会拒绝接收相关款项。这属于反洗钱及银行合规审查，与税务征收是两回事。

🌟 写在最后
目前，香港 CARF 主要覆盖符合香港关联条件的加密资产服务商，并非全球所有交易所。Binance、OKX、Bybit 等海外平台是否需要申报，还要看实际运营实体及适用规则。

对于不属于香港 CARF 申报范围的平台，用户原有的税务规则并未因这次香港修法发生变化。香港计划从 2028 年起与合作地区交换加密交易资料，但内地目前尚未公布首次 CARF 自动交换的具体时间表。

对普通用户来说，短期内交易和出金方式不会因为这次香港修法发生明显变化。

今天是我在Bytedance的Lastday～
谢谢字节圈的大家对我的祝福。
我重新介绍下自己，我是niki，马上快到了我27岁生日，也是我做后端开发的第四个年头，我做了一个非常大的决定，离开了大厂去startup尝试一种新人生。

过去几年，我逐渐熟悉了大公司的游戏规则，怎么扩大 scope、争取资源、证明技术价值，怎么把项目变成对团队和业务的贡献。我乐在其中，享受这份成就感，却也逐渐感到麻木。大厂不会死，即使是不赚钱、无聊的业务，只要能找到切入点去创新与协作，也能创造内部价值。

今年我慢慢的开始思考组织带来的认可和社会市场需要的价值差异在哪里。
我开始好奇如果离开这套评价体系，我能不能做出有价值的东西？

另外，AI。
不可否认，AI 已经在降低知识和软件工程的门槛，甚至未来 AI 也会逐渐改变 research 的方式。
所以当技术越来越容易获得，什么东西会变得更有价值？
过去，能够把产品做出来，本身就是一种竞争优势。而当所有人都具备这种能力时，找到真实的问题、理解用户、判断市场，以及把产品带给用户，就会变得更加重要。这些所有都会到一个问题GTM。
Uber、Owner都是很有趣的市场策略，在一个已有成熟玩家的行业里，如何找到切入点，改变用户习惯背后的某个关键环节，最终建立自己的市场。
但这不意味着技术不再重要。相反，AI 让我们有机会用更少的资源去解决过去不敢想象的问题。

从 2022 年开始，我们这一代软件工程师几乎完整经历了 LLM 如何一步步改变软件行业。每次看到新东西的时候都感到焦虑FOMO，但也让我感到兴奋。
过去积累的专业知识遭到了迅速贬值，但能尝试的事情也远超几年前。
不知道未来会变成什么样子，但我感觉与其努力守住自己已经掌握的知识，不如学习如何在不断变化的世界里持续创造价值。

我很喜欢那些大胆得近乎疯狂的想法。比如 Musk 对商业航天和Roadster。

上周一个朋友和我说：“我欣赏Musk但是又嫉妒他，为什么改变人类世界的是他，而不是我？”

听上去很ego但是有感觉很能共鸣，我也想改变世界，被时代记住。但是很天真，绝大多数人终其一生，都不会成为被历史记住的人。
所以我想如果做不到的话，我也希望自己能够站在技术发展的最前沿，见证人类社会的进步。

我并不认为创业比在大厂更有意义，也不认为冒险本身就值得赞美。

相比继续沿着一条已经相对熟悉的道路往前走，我更想知道，在一个充满不确定性的环境里，自己究竟能做成什么。
可能会失败，可能会发现很多判断都是错的，也可能几年以后重新回到大公司。
但我希望多年以后回头看，至少能吹自己曾经认真参与过这个时代，而不只是旁观。

人生是一件很有意思的事情，每个人都只有一次独一无二的经历。既然未来本来就无法被准确预测，那就保持好奇心、思考能力，以及重新做出选择的勇气。
焦虑是真实的，但也会带来机会，希望大家都能顺利活得精彩～

text:
Some things I learned working at Microsoft:

1/ large numbers everywhere. $100M ARR service isn't even a footnote on executive slide decks. Leadership time is too valuable, come back when you're $1B+. Msft ecosystem is so rich that $1B+ sales are common (it's ludicrous how much work goes into closing these). Azure has ~250 services, some are a few mil and stagnant, others in hypergrowth, some are cash cows, you see every quadrant of the growth-share matrix. Imagine the imperial navy with ships of vastly different sizes as far the eye can see

2/ more on immense scale-- the smallest of Azure services run on 10K+ VMs. Large services run on 1M+ (some maybe 10M+ VMs, idk). Msft is stamping one new datacenter into the ground every four days (!!!!), a bewildering rate. Demand is so high, even with all this buildout we're forever capacity constrained. Azure brings in $100B in revenue and is growing 40%+ annually (at this size!!) There are ~225K msft employees. You almost have to think in scientific notation, 10^4 is a tiny number here

3/ msft is totalitarian re serving the customer. It's counterintuitive to outsiders, but the warts in msft products fall out of this culture. For example, it would be easy to improve the Azure Portal. But in all my time working with customers and partners here, I haven't heard even one person complain about the portal UI. Msft invests $0.00 dollars in anything that doesn't serve the customer and is completely unapologetic about downstream implications of this mindset

4/ msft can reshape itself overnight (when it has the will). People argued whether we waited too long to adapt after Storm-0558/Midnight Blizzard hacks (with the benefit of hindsight, we definitely did). But once the leadership team privileged security, everyone's job changed in two weeks. LT tied every engineer's comp to security, centralized reporting of embedded security teams, every org reshuffled its roadmap. Within days everyone was pushing PRs with security fixes. I would have thought it inconceivable to mobilize 200K+ employees this fast

5/ Azure is complicated. Postgres depends on compute, networking, AKS (or EKS for you aws people), secrets, etc. AKS depends on compute, networking, some datastore (probably Cosmos but idk), a dozen other things. Cosmos depends on... you get the idea. When anything breaks, everything above can break too. Some construction crew accidentally cuts a fiber cable in Brazil South, or a dedicated hardware compression chip browns out in storage, or compute failure rate in west eu spikes for some reason, or a million other failure modes. Msft is relentless about improving this, idk exactly but fully loaded probably 50% of engineer time goes into resilience

6/ re lifers who work 20+ years here, SV sneers at this but I now see it differently. I was once on the bridge debugging some IO issue, we call storage, the guy diagnoses it in about a minute, we chitchat, turns out he built NT asyncio support. Or same story but with networking, the guy built NT tcp/ip stack. I used to have a boss here, we were bumping into some problem, she casually goes oh yeah, we hit that when I was working on .NET bytecode. The ex-DEC VAX/VMS database engineers built SQL Server, some are still here. I love bumping into these people

7/ I never *really* understood distribution until I got here. As an example, our team had a customer in Seoul w/ a deep performance problem. We had to fix it to unlock one of these giant contracts. We don't speak Korean, they don't speak English. Of course msft has specialists in Seoul who get to the customer site before you could even get on a plane. There is an office in every major city, a relationship with every major entity, legal experts in every jurisdiction. You can reach these ppl instantly. Claude tells me msft has ~180 offices in ~100 countries (!!) U.S. government has ~270 consulates in ~170 countries. So msft outposts aren't quite as vast as U.S. diplomatic network, but pretty vast

8/ in the 90s everyone was afraid of msft. The lore is that BillG was ruthless. He'd clone you, beat you via ecosystem/distribution strength, and moreover make the ecosystem stronger with the new product. I wasn't there to compare, but msft of today is ruthless about winning, has the will to adapt, and has the wherewithal to undertake colossal projects. Ppl see Teams bugs or whatever and completely misread the signals. Teams is less polished than Slack because msft doesn't care one iota about polish. It cares about winning, and is frighteningly good at it. Underestimate at your own risk

text:
I spent an afternoon building a program with Claude Code that reads facial expressions from a webcam. It all runs in the browser, no image leaves the laptop, and it costs nothing.

It uses Google's MediaPipe, which tracks 52 facial movements. From those I derive FACS Action Units (the individual muscles psychologists code) and combine them into 8 basic emotions and 12 subtler states: real vs polite smile, confusion, tiredness, micro-expressions under half a second.

Then I wanted to know how often it's actually right, so I ran it on 3,081 labeled photos from three research datasets.

On expressions posed in a lab it gets 60% right. On photos scraped from the web it drops to 26-32%. Random guessing would get 12-17%.

It almost always gets happiness and almost never disgust. Fear gets read as happiness, because bared teeth push the smile score up.

Learning the weights from the data instead of writing them by hand takes the web photos to 42-49%.

On a MacBook Air it uses about 250 MB of memory and roughly twice the power of playing a video.

The video is me testing it on myself, sped up 6x. Next step is putting the learned weights in and rerunning the test with a neutral-face calibration, which the photos didn't have.

let me briefly explain what's going on with @leapxyz, the new trading app

i've seen people mix up Solana, Solana Labs and Solana Foundation. that's where misleading takes like “don't build on Solana unless you want the team to build the same product” come from

• @solana - network.
• @solanalabs - company, one of the teams building on that network.
• @SolanaFndn - separate nonprofit supporting the network development.

Leap was built by the Dialect team, which Labs acquired. the Solana account also supported the announcement. in my opinion, good products deserve that support, but it doesn't mean “the chain itself” built them

i hope Leap gives us a trading app focused on users rather than extracting as much money from them as possible, like some others do

there are some encouraging signs: @aliquotchris is actively asking users what they'd like to see and inviting them to book time on Calendly to share feedback and suggestions

i think he'll read this tweet too, so leave your suggestions: what's missing from the trading apps you use, and what would make the experience better?

author: BinanceWallet
quoted_text:
⚠️ iOS Security Alert | Immediate System Update Required for iOS Users

Apple is urging iPhone/iPad users to update iOS immediately. Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) recently disclosed a critical iOS exploit chain known as “DarkSword,” affecting iOS 18.4 to 18.7.

This issue is not related to any exchange or wallet application, but is a system-level vulnerability in iOS.

Attackers may exploit this vulnerability when users visit compromised (but seemingly legitimate) websites. The exploit may be triggered automatically without any user interaction, allowing attackers to extract sensitive data, including crypto wallet information. The malware may also erase its traces after execution, making detection extremely difficult.

If your device is running iOS 18.4–18.7, you may be at risk.

Immediate Actions Recommended:
1. Update your iPhone/iPad to the latest iOS version immediately
2. Avoid clicking on unknown links or visiting untrusted websites
3. Review app permissions and disable any unnecessary access
4. Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) on all crypto-related accounts and ensure withdrawal whitelist is activated

We believe it’s important to share this security alert with all users and not just Binance users.

Security is the foundation of the entire ecosystem, and protecting user assets must come first.

text: 梨子真的太敬业了，辛苦所有币安朋友们，跟大家面基真开心！
author: 0xajc
quoted_text:
富国岛学习营结束了。来之前，我以为这几天是带着大家来学习。结果几天下来，我自己的本子上也记得满满的。

第一天，Jeff @taida88 给大家讲 Binance AI。他讲得很有画面感——同一个币安 App，刚入门的人打开，看到的是更简单的解释和提示；天天盯盘的人打开，看到的是更深的数据和市场背景。

后面几堂课，大家已经发了很多，我只说两点记得最深的。

一个来自 Binance Research 的分享：市场反应的，往往不是利率本身，而是大家的预期变得有多快。
另一个来自@AncoBinance 的钱包分享。钱包空投覆盖了 1199 万人，让我意识到，对很多人来说，币安钱包就是他们进入链上的第一道门。这道门容不容易迈进，比其他功能还重要。

最后一天，我们请老师们围坐在一起，挨个听大家的反馈。哪里用着不顺手、哪里还能改，都直接说出来。

听起来都是小细节，但每一条背后都是一个具体的人、一个具体的使用习惯。我也更理解 Jeff 说的「个性化了」。

以前的交易所，所有人打开看到的都是同一张行情表。以后，每个人看到的币安可能都不一样，但出发点是同一个——让更多人用得上、也看得懂金融工具。

我想这就是学习营最有意义的地方。产品做得再聪明，也得先听懂用的人。

当天晚上一姐@heyibinance 远程连线还提到一点，那就是用户的信任对我们来说是最贵的，币安能做的，是靠每天的经营和兑付，一点点把它累积起来。对我们来说，是一次次反馈能够落到实处，真的帮大家解决问题。

最后谢谢各位老师这几天的坦诚。币安一直说用户至上，我觉得它最真实的样子，就是像这几天这样，坐下来听你们说。很珍惜和大家相聚的时光，我们 #binanceblockchainweek 曼谷再见！

Getting laid off from OKX is an elite club filled with legends, that I am honored to have joined yesterday.

I was brought on to do DEX BD, where I was the #1 BD for volume and trader deals. After that team was re-org’d, I joined dex opps, focusing on AI integrations, and started a vibe-coding club with Solana Superteam USA.

After another re-org/re-focus (ADHD dream TBH)… 
 
I was next tasked with helping to expand OKX’s creator program, which I doubled in two weeks, created a bounty program that is now used by/ sought after by many teams, and got to work alongside some brilliant creatives to really help it become more personal. I know I worked w/ most of y’all reading this, and from the bottom of my heart, the lack of clarity around that program killed me more than you know, and I hate that X is how I have to say my formal goodbye. Please reach out to me on personal channels if I can do anything for you! 
 
I got to learn the ins and outs of a centralized exchange, throw events at the New York Stock exchange, and across the world as we entered new markets. I truly learned invaluable lessons, (and don’t worry I definitely preached self-custody daily… after all it is about mitigating risk & diversifying assets!) 
 
Speaking of risk, OKX’s compliance and special investigations teams are probably the most epic people I have ever met. I think working with them, & learning from them has been the highlight of my career. They made me realize the true value of a cex (something I NEVER thought I would say)

And throughout all of this, I had unlimited claude tokens & became resident vibe coder for all of my teams. Never once did I think I would be creating technology. What a time to be alive. 
 
Its time to return to my roots; decentralization, trading, education, & being in control of executing quickly & seeing projects through until the end. 
 
Hit me up if you are building something cool that needs someone who can wear many hats (though they will all be orange and furry)
 
But only if you eat, sleep, breathe it. Passion, conviction, & integrity are everything. 
 
Or work at a company with unlimited AI credits…

I wish I could tell you exactly what kind of role I’m most excited to jump into next, but as a human Swiss Army knife, I genuinely love doing it all.

text:
让美股 AI 概念股崩盘的女议员，到底什么来头？

她叫 Yassamin Ansari @RepYassAnsari ，34 岁，民主党籍联邦众议员，伊朗移民后代，也是美国国会首位伊朗裔民主党女性议员。毕业于斯坦福大学和剑桥大学，曾在联合国工作，担任过凤凰城市议员、副市长，2025 年进入美国国会。

但真正让科技行业关注她的，是她对 AI 的态度。

今年 9 月，她就参与联署 Bernie Sanders 和 Greg Casar 推动的《禁止人工超级智能法案》。

法案提出：

- 暂停训练计算量达到 10²⁵ 次运算的先进 AI 系统。
- 在联邦监管机构建立安全规则前，限制相关系统部署。
- 永久禁止超级人工智能。

这已经不是简单的要求科技公司加强安全测试，而是试图从研发阶段限制 AI 的发展边界。

当然，她并不能一个人决定美国 AI 政策。民主党内部对暂停研发的范围、期限和永久禁令仍存在分歧，法案还需要经过国会审议，并面对特朗普可能的否决。

但市场真正担心的，或许不是 Ansari 一个人，而是她所代表的政治信号：

美国 AI 产业过去最大的风险是技术竞争，现在可能还要加上一项：监管突然踩刹车。

当美国一边试图在 AI 竞赛中领先中国，一边又有人主张暂停本土先进 AI 研发，英伟达、AMD、微软、谷歌以及整个数据中心产业，都不得不重新计算政策风险。

这场 AI 竞赛，开始出现一个新问题：美国究竟是要继续加速，还是先给自己的 AI 踩刹车？

富国岛学习营结束了。来之前，我以为这几天是带着大家来学习。结果几天下来，我自己的本子上也记得满满的。

第一天，Jeff @taida88 给大家讲 Binance AI。他讲得很有画面感——同一个币安 App，刚入门的人打开，看到的是更简单的解释和提示；天天盯盘的人打开，看到的是更深的数据和市场背景。

后面几堂课，大家已经发了很多，我只说两点记得最深的。

一个来自 Binance Research 的分享：市场反应的，往往不是利率本身，而是大家的预期变得有多快。
另一个来自@AncoBinance 的钱包分享。钱包空投覆盖了 1199 万人，让我意识到，对很多人来说，币安钱包就是他们进入链上的第一道门。这道门容不容易迈进，比其他功能还重要。

最后一天，我们请老师们围坐在一起，挨个听大家的反馈。哪里用着不顺手、哪里还能改，都直接说出来。

听起来都是小细节，但每一条背后都是一个具体的人、一个具体的使用习惯。我也更理解 Jeff 说的「个性化了」。

以前的交易所，所有人打开看到的都是同一张行情表。以后，每个人看到的币安可能都不一样，但出发点是同一个——让更多人用得上、也看得懂金融工具。

我想这就是学习营最有意义的地方。产品做得再聪明，也得先听懂用的人。

当天晚上一姐@heyibinance 远程连线还提到一点，那就是用户的信任对我们来说是最贵的，币安能做的，是靠每天的经营和兑付，一点点把它累积起来。对我们来说，是一次次反馈能够落到实处，真的帮大家解决问题。

最后谢谢各位老师这几天的坦诚。币安一直说用户至上，我觉得它最真实的样子，就是像这几天这样，坐下来听你们说。很珍惜和大家相聚的时光，我们 #binanceblockchainweek 曼谷再见！

text:
这周开始做一些获客和补贴，也有不少新用户会产生疑问：为什么给的返现这么高，收益从哪来？

可能很少有创始人会公开披露自己的商业模式，正好简单写一篇科普帖子，拆解介绍一下运营一家Neobank（U卡平台）的收入和成本大概会是什么。

先说大家最感兴趣的U卡吧。

U卡一般分为三种模式：

1.直连发卡行，或者和有卡组会员资质的公司合作，需要自己申请一个独立的BIN, 经过卡组的合规审核，这个周期一般是6-12个月。对应的成本是每个月固定要给银行交一笔费用，从几千美金到十万美金都有，每家的政策不一样。发卡行决定了你的卡是哪个地区的，实际term怎么样，这个差异非常大。目前最优质的还是美国地区的发卡，结构通常是按照MCC返现，有些B端场景最高能到3%以上，但标准的还是在2%左右，C端的Bin通常在1-2%区间。发卡行会扣除一部分的手续费，剩下的分给U卡平台。外汇汇损也取决于发卡行的政策，市面标准通常是1%（如大家最常见的，Rain发行的U卡）。以这个方式合作，U卡平台要自己承担反洗钱和用户审核。

2.和Rain/Bridge等专门的发卡公司进行白标合作，他们有些自身就是发卡行，有些也是和发卡行合作，能快速缩短申请周期，一般3个月就可以上线。对应的他们也会收取一部分费用，可以理解为启动更快、初始成本更低、但是毛利更低的方案。以这个方式合作。这类公司会承担一些反洗钱和审核，也会定期筛查。

3.用一些大型的Fintech平台（卡台），以企业卡的方式发行，优点是更快，大部分给的返现会比较低，少部分因为有补贴甚至条件更好，缺点是相对没那么合规，不稳定。

综合下来，U卡这边最终能有的收入，在不额外加外汇费用的情况下，应该是在1-2%这个区间。Infini也是这个区间，因此我们基础返现是1.5%，前期小亏一点，后面会随着规模和渠道优化盈利一些。当然，大家常见的头部平台，基本都为了增长采取净补贴的烧钱获客方案，我们也不能避免，这部分我猜大家都是在月交易量 0.5-1%的补贴，当然早晚有一天会回归常态。

第二个是银行账户和法币出入金，能做这个业务基本都需要牌照了，给银行的固定费用和发卡差不多。

一般模式是，每个独立的子账户都收取一个月费（从1-3美金不等，我们现在为了获客是免费提供），然后还会有每笔交易的费用（银行一般会在支付通道上加，比如SWIFT/ACH等费用），各家差别也挺大的。除此之外，部分银行提供法币与稳定币的承兑服务，按照百分比收钱（通常在0.1%以内）。因为涉及到一来一回，所以如果头寸对冲的足够好，应该能把成本控制在0.05%以内，甚至更低）。这部分业务是不可能补贴的，否则会被撸死，并且还要承担反洗钱的成本和责任，因此行业常见的收费模式是0.2-0.3%，infini的定价也是这个范围，我们后续还会为大客户降低到0.1%。

再之后，各家的业务范围就不一样了。比如资管理财我们做的会更好，本质上还是因为有更好的套利策略，这个放在传统银行模式下就是贷款赚取利差，放在Crypto里常见的模式就是通过Defi/Cefi套利。这部分利润差别会很大，也会和流动性和行情有关，长期健康的商业模式应该是1-3%的利差收益，规模越大毛利越低（因为优质收益、安全稳定的策略容量有限，这是一个不可能三角）。

像我们的企业产品还有稳定币收单，收费是0.2-0.3%，成本是0.1%左右（因为自己承担了Gas归集成本和流动性占用成本。Tron会尤其高，新链相对好一些）

所以回到正题，为什么我们能有比较好的返现，一方面是因为不断在优化从发卡行拿到的比例（有些BIN应该能比常见的Rain要高一些），另一方面我们的资管Carry部分会拿来补贴，因此要求资沉。当然这两个加起来还是不一定能够cover的住，但其实能亏的也有限，都是经过精算的。当然希望未来能通过优秀的留存，以及其他业务的收入，维持一个长期稳定、有利润的商业模式。

最后大家关心的资产安全、透明等角度，自然都是很重要的事情，对于前者我比任何人都更操心，也踩过坑。所以infini提现会慢，因为自动化程度没那么高，现在这个被盗事件频出的年代，已经不能信任系统了，更复杂和臃肿的人工审核体系是短期最优解，现在各家交易所应该也都在跟进了，明显越来越严格，更贴近传统金融。这也是行业大的趋势，是我们在没法解决这种本质性问题前的被迫方案。

关于透明度，最终是一个平衡。一方面，更高的透明度会让用户更方便地验证，但同时也会让黑客更方便地验证。另一方面，传统审计其实是不能很好解决Crypto这种形式的，正如同交易所应该常见的也是用储备金证明，而不是靠审计公司的报告，只有合规资管是强制要求审计的，所以我们后面的合规资管产品会做。当然如储备金证明等还有一系列方案，也有很多优秀团队在做，我们当然也会采用，只不过一方面有成本，一方面产研有很多基建和功能要开发，所以是一个长期话题。

信任需要建立，需要沟通，其实最终所有解决方案都不是那个核心，因为所有证明都可以伪造，只是成本问题。核心还是分摊风险，我希望大家信任我们，愿意体验我们的产品，会争取更多的信任，但我也不希望大家把身家性命都交给我，我也背负不起。

分散资产、分摊风险，评估风险，是任何时代都绕不开的话题，更是对自己负责的唯一方法。我们不可能也不会尝试让每个人都信任，我们只能在各个方面每天都变好一点🫡

quoted_text:
hearing some chatter that anthropic is now lowering down to $1tn to get this IPO done. let me explain why this doesnt matter and its actually all over-

the entire existence of this company is based on a funding model that inherently has extreme asset liability mismatch. what that means is that just like the hyperscalers are diluting their equity fund capex, there is an expectation that anthropic will also have to do the same. ie it needs strong equity to perpetuate the scheme

but if you IPO at the wrong price (and dont get a pop which increasingly appears they wont be; spacex already below) then youre now in the death spiral that crypto investors should be very familiar with: its called the reflexivity trap of the confidence game. its the "ill bid FTT at $22 all day" or the "steady lads UST is $1" game, with all its lucid horrors. and here is the key insight- the confidence game exists at the service of the creditors. if there is no credit, there is simply no equity. and there is no credit, if there is no collateral

if the credit rating agencies are not going to give IG at $2tn, they are certaintly not going a better HY rating at $1tn. and there is no world in which anthropic can exist without credit because ~$1tn of commit, much of which is noncancellable, is a straight up negative equity pledge

yet there were two scenarios in which i was willing to concede anthropic could IPO: first 1) the improbable but possible was if the hyperscalers/chips oligopoly came to rescue and plug the hole, given their incestuous nature of revenue bookings and paper gains/losses at scale. but it is clear now that the market has spoken this will lead to a mutual death, and should not be attempted. or perversely even better, they are actually better off letting anthropic go to zero so they can acquire the pieces on the cheap which is the best nash equilibrium outcome, not just for the dominant player but for society at large. second 2) the us government can nationalize the company and collude with other sovereigns (like UAE, Saudi, Japan who are basically already the checks) to force its funding as a collective bargain. this gives you trillions, which is actually the most effective backstop to restore market confidence. the first edge case does require an IPO, but the second edge case here for which i believe there is still a good chance that this is the ultimate end game- will require a failed IPO to recapitalize at a normalized price for the consortium (and dont forget that openai front ran this investor group in anticipation of this dynamic to play out as a private co last month)

i believe the market is crapping out today because the market is recognizing it will not IPO. and actually, as ive said before, this is a very good thing. i might even imagine that the market could quickly rebound on the news of its IPO being delayed because it allows #2) to play out, as not only a national, but an international bailout. the US is more likely to tolerate, even relish, the taxes of foreginers to fund our domestic companies. that is the only end game that really matters, and the end game i am going to be excited to see

we'll see if this newly revamped washington can figure it out

这里简单说一下主要更新的几个功能：

▪️新增 Entropy 层级与预计返佣：可以选 T1～T4，面板显示预计返佣、扣返佣后的净损益和磨损

▪️新增浮盈止盈：持仓期间价差往有利方向走了一大段时，算上开平两边的手续费后仍然净赚，就提前平掉，再开下一轮
▪️新增择时开仓：程序会监控两边交易所的基础价差，会在对持仓方向有利的条件下开仓
▪️新增择时平仓：程序会监控两边交易所的基础价差，会在对持仓方向有利的条件下平仓

text:
On Fragmentation for Tokenized Equities:
I’d say tokenization doesn’t fix composability, and TradFi has the same problem: every broker holding is its own wrapper. The difference is TradFi has DTC underneath, so you can move between brokers 1:1 because they all point to the same share.

Tokenized stocks don’t have that layer yet. The closest fix is a unified DEX pool across issuers, something like Curve’s 3pool for DAI-USDC-USDT.
author: tomwanhh
quoted_text:
Tokenized equities are where stablecoins were in their early days.

The core problem: most tokenized stocks today are issued by companies that also run the exchange and the layer one. Each of these players has zero incentive to list or trade a competitor’s standard.

The result is ten competing standards and fragmented liquidity.

What the market needs is a neutral issuer, one that doesn’t own every layer of the stack.

Managing Director at UBS, Timothy Arcuri, on why the memory industry has fundamentally changed:

1. Unlike traditional memory which could last for years, HBM is now on an annual development cadence. Each new generation of AI processors requires a specific version of HBM, creating constant, direct connectivity between compute and memory producers. 

2. While logic is used for learning, valuable inference tokens are generated from memory banks, making memory inherently more valuable in an AI context.

3. Major hyperscalers are signing long-term agreements, often including multi-billion dollar prepayments, to secure supply. 

4. The production of HBM is physically more resource-intensive, as it consumes roughly four times the wafer capacity of non-HBM memory due to vertical device stacking. This effectively creates a supply-side anchor, where increased demand for AI compute further constrains available memory supply.

text:
《AI会打爆所有模拟经营类型的大学竞赛》

目前大多数大学生想要的无非是证书和荣誉，国家奖学金、保研加分都用得上。很多学校都有国家 A 类的竞赛目录，这种比赛会加分啥的，学创杯就是其中之一

学创杯里有个财务决策赛项，叫理财之道
这本质是一个模拟经营的小游戏：

系统给你一份初始资源，规则里把会计核算怎么算、各项数值怎么影响结果写得明明白白。一共四个季度，每个季度经营完出一个结果，你根据结果调整下一个季度的产线、生产量、广告、贷款。四个季度打完，系统给出最终分数

我读的是会计和金融，拿过全国的奖项
所以对这类比赛有点了解。最近我发现：

这种规则透明、结果可算的游戏
AI 现在已经能做到接近最优解

原因很简单：

规则是写死的，没有隐藏信息；
你可以让它模拟成千上万次，样本足够大，就知道每个阶段该做什么决策；
再根据对手的报价、场上局势做数据分析，这本来就是 AI 最擅长的事。

举个我自己的例子。有一套打法，大致节奏是这样的：

第一季度：长贷 20 万，买厂房和几条低端产线，招对应的工人和销售，原材料按订单量备货，广告平均分给低端。 第二季度：长贷 30 万，上高端产线，中端低端同时备料，广告往中端倾斜
第三季度：再贷一笔，融资租赁厂房，三档产品同时铺开第四季度：看每个组的平均单量，决定要不要扩产，广告三档同时加码。

几个小原则：报价基本报最高价；低端扩产看人均单量；贷款和广告随局势微调，打得好就多贷一点，被人压了就把广告降一点

注意：这是针对某一套模板的节奏。官方说明里，比赛模板在开赛前才由系统抽取，数据规则以现场公布为准，所以具体数字要重新算，不能照抄。但思路是通用的

这套逻辑，放进 AI 里反复推演，再让它自动执行、读取数据、回头修正，得出相对最优解

所以我的判断是：模拟经营这一类竞赛，要沦陷了。 当工具能把最优解算出来，比赛比的就是谁用最好的AI工具

最后：比赛请自己打噢，哈哈哈哈

text:
Today’s GPT-6 Cyber release is a meaningful step for defenders: stronger vulnerability research and better alignment. We’ve already been using GPT-6 Cyber alongside GPT-6 Astra with Daybreak to harden our own systems, finding weaknesses, validating their impact, and developing fixes.

Even after years @OpenAI, model capabilities continue to surprise me. One small example came from testing a prerelease version of GPT-6 Astra earlier this summer. We were examining tools used across our research infrastructure and one of our research infra leads, Michael Dalton, was looking into some low risk areas like a math task grader that used SymPy, a mathematics library, to check answers.

In an offline test, the submitted answer used characters that looked like ordinary letters to get past the grader’s checks. It caused the grader to run a shell command that printed “4242”, while still returning the expected result, 1/2. The grader marked the answer correct. A valid math answer had become a way to run code inside the grader - diagram below.

This is the kind of vulnerability that can be very hard for a human to find, even with a fuzzer. It takes connecting how input validation and evaluation interact, constructing an input that passes the checks but triggers unintended behavior, and recognizing the failure even when the final answer is correct. Models can reason across those pieces and help uncover classes of vulnerabilities that are difficult to spot when reviewing components in isolation.

That’s why it’s important for more defenders to use models with Daybreak to find and fix vulnerabilities in their own systems. Whether it’s a potentially internet-melting bug like PHP2Shell or a subtle but important issue like this grader bug, finding it before an attacker does gives defenders time to act.

Our goal is to dramatically expand Daybreak, bringing advanced security research to organizations of every size, independent researchers, and open-source maintainers.

We’re also expanding Daybreak Blue alpha access for GPT‑6 Astra to more organizations and individual security researchers - let us know if you’re interested:
https://t.co/0PpjMDDZJc

为啥周四美股开盘后大跌了？不是中期大选利好吗？为啥 Bitcoin 也跌了？？

😂我晚上开始码字到现在还没有一个小时就出现大跌了，Bitcoin 都已经跌了超过 6% 了，这种情况下原罪大概率是出在美股身上，果然英伟达、AMD 和数据中心相关股票都在下跌，也就是科技股和 AI 都在下跌。

主要的原因就是民主党获胜，等等，不是说民主党获胜是利好吗？你 TMD 昨天还说是利好，怎么今天就是利空了？好坏坏话怎么都你一个人说的！！

先别打，这个逻辑是这样的。

昨天是因为民主党获得了胜利，控制了国会，尤其是参议院民主党领袖舒默都表示要结束美国和伊朗的战争了，这个利好确实带动了市场的上涨，甚至是 bitcoin:native ，这是没错的。

但就像昨天有小伙伴说的一样，这不是利好吗？为啥科技股在下跌，科技股昨天和今天下跌的原因都是一样的！主要原因就是因为数据中心建设的不确定性增加。

实际上民主党在得州、佐治亚州等数据中心建设较集中的地区取得胜利，部分地方民众此前就反对数据中心扩张，担心用电、用水和电费上涨。投资者担心，未来部分项目可能面临更严格审批或暂停建设。如果数据中心建得慢，芯片、服务器和算力供应商的订单增长也可能受到影响。

说人话，民主党没有那么激进，所以在民主党主要获选的地区可能就为了选票而降低对 AI 数据中心的支持，而且现在本身市场就担心 AI 的扩张带来了资本开支的增加，结果科技股的投资者就开始担心，出现了抛售。

这是第一个主要原因，其次就是油价又开始回升了，主要是市场昨天买入的是情绪，今天卖出的是情绪落地，所以我是在早晨看到油价反弹的时候就直接清空了做空的仓位，如果不算资金费率的是小赚，算了资金费率仍然是亏损的，但我觉得只要伊朗有明确的信号，我就在做空就行了。

上一轮七月就是因为觉得还能跌硬生生的从 80% 的利润变成了超过 100% 的亏损，和头疼的资金费率，所以这次就更果断了。

而在 bitcoin:native 我还是判断错了，虽然我知道 AI 会跌，油价上涨了，但是白天就已经是这样了，但白天 BTC 没啥动静啊，我就觉得 BTC 问题不大，结果到时间就买入抄底了，结果就成这样了，但我觉得现在买入的问题仍然不会很大，我在继续做空油价的时候，BTC 的价格就应该回来了。

但 AI 和半导体，我给小伙伴的建议就是不要着急抄底。
