text:
链上余额宝，噱头还是创新？ 
 
上个世纪70年代，世界上最大的金融管理公司美林证券，第一次推出了现金管理账户，它把证券账户、货币基金、支票和支付功能接在一起。

符合条件的用户闲置现金可以自动转入生息工具，客户需要投资或支付时，再按账户规则调用资金。 

这估计就是经济史上第一笔质押生息的来源了。到1987年，美林已经有约130万个CMA账户。

其他金融机构也开始提供类似服务，一个处理闲置余额的功能，逐渐改变了证券账户的用途。 

这里面有一套朴素的经济逻辑：把分散的闲钱组织起来，交给能够产生现金流的资产，再用账户、结算和流动性管理，降低用户使用它的成本。 

金融服务由此开始走向了更多衍生品的路径。 
 
现在，同一个问题来到了加密世界。 

市场行情不好，用户持有大量稳定币，然后想找一个资产管理协议继续稳赚。

但是普通人需要选择协议、比较资产、理解赎回，有时还要跨链。每一项都需要时间，也都需要判断。 
对于大部分来说，这些都是有门槛的。

于是，"链上现金管理"这门生意应运而生，大所、大机构，都在抢这块蛋糕。
 
包装的名字五花八门，有的叫"活期理财"，有的叫"生息钱包"，有的叫"链上货基"。

噱头各不相同，但底层逻辑一直未曾改变。 

TopNod钱包上线 Axil Pot，简称APT，就是围绕这类需求设计的产品。 

从用户这一端看，路径比较容易理解：通过钱包进入产品，把Pharos上的USDC投入Vault，获得代表投资份额的APT。

份额价值随资产组合表现变化，赎回时再按适用规则换回USDC。 

另一端，是被专业管理的资产。

APT主要连接的是新兴市场的小额消费贷款和先买后付应收款。

借款人分期偿付，或者相关商业安排产生收入，这些回款构成收益的经济基础。

AXIL负责策略策展和风险管理，实际贷款由经过筛选的消费金融或BNPL合作方发放、管理。 

简单来说就是链上系统承担份额记录和资金结算，收益则需要底层业务持续产生现金流。 

项目给出的约8%目标APY，对应的是一组资产的经营结果，会随着资产表现和成本变化。

APT把一件原本需要多次选择的事，变成了一条相对清晰的路径。 

美林当年把货币基金接进证券账户，APT则尝试把现实信用资产的收益能力，接进链上钱包。

两者的资产风险不同，但都在回答一个问题：用户资金闲置时，金融服务还能替他做些什么。 
 
一笔闲钱愿意留下来，只因为操作方便和高收益还不够。
 
它需要一个更值得信服的理由：资产怎样进入、回款怎样形成、退出怎样安排。

APT的解题思路，可以沿着这条资金路径来看。 

1、资产入口筛选。AXIL会对放贷合作方的资质、财务、历史还款与逾期表现、授信和催收能力进行尽调，并持续跟踪贷款数据。

资金还会通过分离的路径流向合作方、收回回款，减少与其他业务资金混用的风险。 
 
2、提前安排退出流动性。 

借款人按计划还款，用户却可能更早就需要USDC。

APT的公开设计，是在信用资产之外配置现金、货币基金和短期信用等流动性资产，用来承接日常退出需求，尽量减少临时出售贷款资产的压力。
 
产品规则也区分了两条退出路径：T+0依赖可用现金，并受全体持有人共享、约为Vault资产规模10%的日额度约束；

常规路径为T+1至T+7，同样适用流动性和产品条款。 
 
3、收益可持续化。底层收入需要覆盖信用损失、资产管理和结算费用，也要承担保留流动性的成本。

这笔账能够长期成立，闲置资金才有持续获取收益的基础。 

因此，我对APT的判断，来自它选择的解题方向：
用现实业务回款支撑收益，用专业筛选管理信用，再用储备和分层退出照顾用户的资金用途。 

从美林的证券账户，到今天的链上钱包，金融产品的形式变化很大。

用户的一个愿望却始终朴素：在没有更好的投资机会时，让自己手里的钱生钱。 
 
链上余额宝APT正在打开的，是一种更贴近加密用户日常的新生息方式。 

它把现实资产的现金流、专业机构的管理能力和钱包的使用入口连接起来，让参与生息逐渐成为资金安排中更容易完成的一步。

author: kaikaibtc
quoted_text:
TopNod钱包推出“链上余额宝”概念产品Axil Pot：让闲置USDC参与现实消费信贷，目标年化约8%。

Axil Pot跑在Pharos上，这是一条由前蚂蚁团队创立、主打RWA的公链，通过TopNod钱包提供入口。此前相关金库也与币安钱包、OKX钱包有过合作，这些背景算加分项。

我以前在投行负责过非标投资和产品设计，看这类产品，比较在意底层资产和资金流。把闲置的U放进去赚点收益，听着挺简单，真要参与，还是得搞清楚：钱投向哪里？收益谁付？承担什么风险？什么时候能取出来？出了问题找谁？

1️⃣钱投到哪里，收益谁来付？
Axil Pot（APT）是由AXIL管理的USDC收益金库，底层资产由 Axil 配资的货币市场基金、高流动性资产、新兴市场的小额消费贷款等，有现实业务支撑。其中小额信贷来自借款人的分期消费利息，以及实际回款形成现金流闭环，支付金库的收益。

Axil负责筛选合作机构、配置策略和管理风险，据其官网介绍，团队成员具有贝莱德、港交所、中金资本、蚂蚁集团等机构的从业背景。按官方披露，APT不把存入的USDC转投其他DeFi收益池，也不做循环借贷或杠杆。能否持续赚到收益，主要看底层贷款质量和回款情况。收益有现实业务支撑,这也是它值得看的地方!

基本情况：
1、存入USDC，持有代表金库份额的APT。
2、目标年化约8%，浮动、不保证。
3、可用流动性和每日额度内支持T+0提款，常规路径为T+1至T+7。
4、通过@Top_nod钱包参与，使用@R25Official金库基础设施，在Pharos @pharos_network上记录和结算。

2️⃣风险点与风控。
APT代表金库份额，价值随资产表现变化，不保证固定为1美元。

和主要靠链上借贷、交易或代币激励产生收益的产品相比，Axil Pot中高收益的生息资产更依赖现实中的贷款回款。所以重点得放在借款人能不能还钱、合作机构靠不靠谱，以及出了问题能不能追回资金

另外是时间差：贷款要慢慢收回来，用户却可能同时申请提款。金库配置了现金、货币市场基金和短期信贷等资产，但即时提款仍受可用现金和每日额度限制，集中赎回时可能需要等。

Axil 之前做过的同类型三个月资产，年化约12%+，管理规模大约在1亿美金，目前为止运作正常。

按官方说明做了资金路径与多方位的尽职调查：
1）资金通过隔离账户流转，帮助与合作机构的其他业务资金分开，
2）放贷机构要经过尽调和持续监控
3）对单一机构或市场的投入设有上限，避免过度集中。
4）资金从金库经隔离账户接入审核过的消费信贷机构，消费者还款后回流金库。期间不转投其他DeFi收益池，也不做循环借贷或杠杆。

总体综合来看：

我觉得这个产品的一大特色与创新是它把真实世界的消费信贷接到了链上。

消费信贷这部分的收益，来自借款人实际支付的利息，和币圈常见的抵押借贷、循环贷或链上策略有所不同。

这就让RWA变得具体了：存入的是USDC，参与的是现实中的消费贷款，收益是这门生意本身产生的收益。

text:
今天是我在Bytedance的Lastday～
谢谢字节圈的大家对我的祝福。
我重新介绍下自己，我是niki，马上快到了我27岁生日，也是我做后端开发的第四个年头，我做了一个非常大的决定，离开了大厂去startup尝试一种新人生。

过去几年，我逐渐熟悉了大公司的游戏规则，怎么扩大 scope、争取资源、证明技术价值，怎么把项目变成对团队和业务的贡献。我乐在其中，享受这份成就感，却也逐渐感到麻木。大厂不会死，即使是不赚钱、无聊的业务，只要能找到切入点去创新与协作，也能创造内部价值。

今年我慢慢的开始思考组织带来的认可和社会市场需要的价值差异在哪里。
我开始好奇如果离开这套评价体系，我能不能做出有价值的东西？

另外，AI。
不可否认，AI 已经在降低知识和软件工程的门槛，甚至未来 AI 也会逐渐改变 research 的方式。
所以当技术越来越容易获得，什么东西会变得更有价值？
过去，能够把产品做出来，本身就是一种竞争优势。而当所有人都具备这种能力时，找到真实的问题、理解用户、判断市场，以及把产品带给用户，就会变得更加重要。这些所有都会到一个问题GTM。
Uber、Owner都是很有趣的市场策略，在一个已有成熟玩家的行业里，如何找到切入点，改变用户习惯背后的某个关键环节，最终建立自己的市场。
但这不意味着技术不再重要。相反，AI 让我们有机会用更少的资源去解决过去不敢想象的问题。

从 2022 年开始，我们这一代软件工程师几乎完整经历了 LLM 如何一步步改变软件行业。每次看到新东西的时候都感到焦虑FOMO，但也让我感到兴奋。
过去积累的专业知识遭到了迅速贬值，但能尝试的事情也远超几年前。
不知道未来会变成什么样子，但我感觉与其努力守住自己已经掌握的知识，不如学习如何在不断变化的世界里持续创造价值。

我很喜欢那些大胆得近乎疯狂的想法。比如 Musk 对商业航天和Roadster。

上周一个朋友和我说：“我欣赏Musk但是又嫉妒他，为什么改变人类世界的是他，而不是我？”

听上去很ego但是有感觉很能共鸣，我也想改变世界，被时代记住。但是很天真，绝大多数人终其一生，都不会成为被历史记住的人。
所以我想如果做不到的话，我也希望自己能够站在技术发展的最前沿，见证人类社会的进步。

我并不认为创业比在大厂更有意义，也不认为冒险本身就值得赞美。

相比继续沿着一条已经相对熟悉的道路往前走，我更想知道，在一个充满不确定性的环境里，自己究竟能做成什么。
可能会失败，可能会发现很多判断都是错的，也可能几年以后重新回到大公司。
但我希望多年以后回头看，至少能吹自己曾经认真参与过这个时代，而不只是旁观。

人生是一件很有意思的事情，每个人都只有一次独一无二的经历。既然未来本来就无法被准确预测，那就保持好奇心、思考能力，以及重新做出选择的勇气。
焦虑是真实的，但也会带来机会，希望大家都能顺利活得精彩～

High barriers could slow foreign stablecoin penetration in a high-adoption market while curbing algorithmic risks.

Chainalysis: Names, Usernames, Password Hashes, and Valid Tokens of All Users Were Exposed; Some Plaintext Passwords Also Leaked  

Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis disclosed in an updated security incident notice that the names, usernames, password hashes, and valid authentication tokens of all users had been exposed to the attacker, and that some customers’ plaintext passwords were also leaked through a separate attack method. After detecting abnormal activity, the company suspended KYT transaction monitoring, address screening, and login services, and required all users to reset their passwords and rotate API keys where necessary.  

Previously, on October 30, Chainalysis first disclosed that it had been breached by a hacker using offensive AI agent technology; at that time it only confirmed that certain customer identity information had been accessed and said it had found no evidence that passwords or session tokens had been leaked.

text:
OpenAI 总裁亲口承认：2026 年上半年，他们差点被 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 打懵了。
在《华尔街日报》Tech 大会上，OpenAI 联合创始人 Greg Brockman 罕见地公开承认：
“第一季度很艰难，第二季度也很艰难。”
当时 OpenAI 明明已经有 Codex，但市场上几乎没人讨论它。另一边，Anthropic 的 Claude Code 正在迅速席卷开发者社区，甚至开始抢走 OpenAI 最重要的企业客户。
更夸张的是，根据此前披露的数据，2026 年第二季度，Anthropic 收入达到 116 亿美元，同期 OpenAI 为 67 亿美元。
但故事在第三季度发生了反转。
Brockman 透露，OpenAI 第三季度的年化营收运行率环比增长 70%，企业业务规模几乎翻倍，企业客户如今已经贡献超过一半的销售收入。
从上半年被 Claude Code 抢尽风头，到下半年靠 Codex 和企业 Agent 业务重新追赶，OpenAI 终于意识到了一件事：
未来 AI 公司的竞争，光有最强模型已经不够了。谁能让 Agent 真正替企业完成工作，谁才能拿到下一轮最大的收入。
更值得注意的是，Brockman 还表示，OpenAI 有望在 2027 年做好 IPO 准备。
2026 年可能正在成为 AI 行业真正的分水岭：Chatbot 时代逐渐过去，Agent 时代开始决定巨头的命运。
一个很有意思的问题：2027 年，AI 编程市场究竟会是 Claude Code 的天下，还是 Codex 后来居上？

text: Ryan previously thought the intelligence explosion would start ~Nov 2028, but now says: "I was seriously wrong about RSI speed up; I previously expected much less in 2026 (around 1.15x-1.3x)." [It's actually 1.9x]
author: Selkis_2028
quoted_text:
This report on AI R&D automation (RSI) is a big update towards ASI within 1-2 years. It says AI progress is sped up by RSI right now by around 2x. In AI 2027, this happens around March 2027.

I was seriously wrong about RSI speed up; I previously expected much less in 2026 (around 1.15x-1.3x). It seems as though there was specific privately available evidence that would have changed my mind.

I haven't seen an unredacted version of this report; this is purely about the public report. Because so much of the underlying evidence was redacted from the public report, I think conclusions about things other than the observed 2x faster rate of progress on benchmarks depend significantly on trust for the authors of the report. (E.g., conclusions about whether this speed up is from RSI depend on trust.) I do trust the authors of the report a lot to be careful and rigorous and generally do a good job. (Note that I also work at METR.) Less extensive redactions would greatly reduce this need for trust.

Since in my current role I may have access to other confidential information that could be relevant to timelines one way or another, I unfortunately cannot state my all-things-considered views on ASI timelines or the probability of a software intelligence explosion right now. Here, I’ve done some analysis of the implications using my previous public statements.

A 2x acceleration in overall AI progress from RSI corresponds to a much larger than 2x RSI speed up for AI software R&D (algorithms and data); I did an estimate using my public preexisting modeling of drivers of AI progress and the public report which yielded a very rough estimate of 4.5x for how much RSI is currently accelerating AI software progress (relative to no AI automation). In the AI 2027 scenario, this much acceleration happens around March 2027.

Here are the worked details of this estimate based on my public modeling. There are two main reasons RSI speed up of AI software R&D must be larger:

- Not all of AI progress is from better software (some is from scaling up compute in training runs). I've previously speculated that around 2/3 of AI progress is from software improvements which implies that 2x overall AI progress acceleration requires 3x faster software progress.
- Diminishing returns: A fixed amount of progress requires more work over time, so to ongoingly maintain 3x faster software progress via AI automation, you need increasingly large speed boosts from AI automation (as in, speed ups relative to how fast software R&D would go without AI automation). Based on this report, it seems that there is a substantial amount of additional AI progress from automation that has occurred.

We can estimate the effects of diminishing returns by first determining how many additional years of software progress we've seen (relative to the preexisting trend) and then estimating how much software R&D would slow down after a year of software progress if you held inputs fixed due to diminishing returns. I've previously estimated software R&D would slow down by around 2x for each year of software progress if you held inputs fixed (https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj) and based on the report, it seems as though we've perhaps seen roughly 0.35-1.0 years of additional software progress incorporated into trained models so far (geometric mean of ~0.6). This combines to 3 * 2^(~0.6) = ~4.5.
(Relevant public modeling and numbers I'm using: https://t.co/AYhl9hyiAj, https://t.co/ck7CtW5LIA)

突然的闪崩，
不仅让我开始缩减接下来的「旅行预算」，
甚至重新打开了PDD，准备海淘泡面。
行情不好的时候，能省一点是一点。

昨天晚上和小伙伴聊起最近都在用什么AI，
也聊到了一个很现实的问题：AI 的使用成本。
我们发现一个很有意思的现象：
免费版GPT和收费版GPT，根本不是一个物种！GO版本和PRO版本，也完全不是一个物种。

既然不同版本的体验差距这么大，那么当我们为了省钱，选择通过API调用AI模型时，又该怎么确定服务商提供的，真的是我们付费购买的那个模型？

同一个模型 ID，不同服务商可能使用不同版本、不同精度，甚至存在工具调用失效、上下文缩水等问题。更麻烦的是，这些问题未必会体现在API的返回结果中。

针对这个问题，Mira Network @miranetwork 推出了Sterling|Sterling提供的是经过验证的推理服务。
Mira会持续对每个模型背后的服务商进行五项检查，包括模型身份、工具调用、参数遵循、静默故障和上下文长度，并公开验证评分。Sterling 则根据验证结果，优先将请求路由给通过验证的服务商。
目前首批支持 Claude、GPT 和 Gemini，DeepSeek、GLM 也即将上线。
使用上只需要一个API Key，支持USDC或MIRA支付，部分模型上线期间最高享50% 折扣。

我觉得，随着AI的发展，大家关注的不应该只有模型有多强，还应该关注模型背后的推理服务是否真实、稳定、可信。
毕竟，行情不好可以少吃几顿好的，但花钱调用 AI，至少应该确保自己买到的是真正想要的服务。

text:
Yesterday’s hedge fund rumors are confirmed by WSJ and Bloomberg, and the details hurt.

Per Morgan Stanley, October saw the largest active reduction of positions by stock pickers in over a decade. More than 40% of them were flat or down YTD, while the indexes were still positive. And of the 46 major funds tracked by Bloomberg, more than half finished October in the red.

The damage:

- Lone Pine: +40% in H1, now -7.5% YTD. Caught on both sides, on its AI longs and on its shorts against companies threatened by AI, which went up.
- VARA: -33% in October
- Arini: -26% YTD, forced to dump over $2B of assets in a week under margin call pressure. Rivals are now shorting its biggest positions.
- Tiger Global: -8.5% in October, back to flat YTD
- Kirkoswald: worst month in its history
- Millennium: -2.3% in October, with several internal pods reportedly shutdown
- Engineers Gate: shutting most of its human-plus-quant strategy, keeping only 5 PMs. The head of the unit is leaving.
- Samlyn: dropping everything except financials. Other sector heads and senior analysts are out.
- Walleye: head of equities and a large part of the long/short teams let go, and capital going back to clients

Thursday made it worse. Per Goldman Sachs, tech funds lost more than 4% in one session, wiping out YTD gains that had reached 24% before the summer. The Nasdaq lost $2.5T, to the point that Dan Loeb (Third Point) joked on X: “Hug your hedge fund manager.”

The problem is that everyone holds the same names: funds, retail and leveraged ETFs. Hedges stop working, and every sale drags down everyone else’s positions. $SOXL lost 39% in one session, and volatility-control funds could still liquidate up to $135B of futures.

But forced selling always stops at some point, and the rebounds that follow can be violent. On Wall Street, an old rule says to wait three sessions after a shock before deciding anything.

Solana 上有的还很早期，之前一次活动做得有点拉胯，我没参与。
剩下的小台子偏博彩，我不太了解的一般不轻易碰。

所以等 42 也发币，现有的预测市场基本面不变的话，我这边暂时就没什么看好的项目了。

text:
Coinbase’s vision for an agentic future is correct.

Decades ago, ETFs changed investing by putting portfolios on autopilot. Weak companies got removed from the index. Emerging and outperforming ones got added. You didn’t have to constantly research, rebalance, or second-guess every holding. The structure itself handled the selection and turnover, which is a big reason retirement accounts have been able to compound over long periods with relatively little effort.

There was always a clear limitation though. Automation came at the cost of customization. If you didn’t want every name in the S&P 500 or you had a specific thesis, sector bias, risk tolerance, or set of companies you simply didn’t want to own. 

your main options were still either building and managing everything yourself, or accepting a one-size-fits-all basket. There wasn’t a practical middle ground that gave you both automation and meaningful personalization.

That constraint is ending.

An agent can learn how you actually invest: your style, your theses, the risks you’re willing to take, the companies or sectors you want to avoid, and the outcomes you’re optimizing for. Instead of forcing you into a static index, it can apply your own rules and preferences at scale, screening, rebalancing, adjusting, and executing while you stay in control of the strategy.

The next phase of financial services won’t just be about better products. It’ll be about putting more of the actual work on automation, personalized to the individual. Coinbase is early in recognizing that shift.

text:
I did the same a few months ago

I shut down my 13-year old $300/mo Linode VPS server that hosted all my 100+ sites for over a decade!

That Linode VPS called Tommy is where everything started for me, I knew to build startups I needed a server so I just made one and SSH'd into it and started uploading PHP files of little startups I made

After 1.5 years my first sites started taking off and I started making money on the internet with Tommy!

For almost a decade I'd still FTP my files by dragging them every time I made an edit to the server, only around 2020 I switched to Github because @daniellockyer said it'd be better and because regularly the site would break at halfway because people would load the site while I was in the middle transferring index.php over FTP 😂

I didn't have multiple VPS servers, I had just one for ALL my sites and projects (I'd say upwards of 100), but it worked mostly fine, and I regularly posted about how it was all on one server which made Twitter/X go crazy "how do you scale???", it scaled fine, served 300 million people per year and 115,000 paying customers in its lifetime!

Back around 2013, Linode was the "cool" hoster on Hacker News, but a decade later, the spirit of Linode seemed to have disappeared, it felt like it was in maintenance mode and not really loved for anymore. When it was acquired by Akamai in 2022, me and @daniellockyer knew we'd have to leave because acquired companies generally go to shit

I saw @DHH posting about @Hetzner_Online so I started making little VPS servers there to test it, first with @pieter and it worked really great. Then slowly I started migrating each site over to Hetzner, with the most critical sites like Photo AI and Nomads last. I also started separating sites on to different VPS servers, isolating them, which now in this new AI cybersecurity time makes security sense. It was never an issue with performance though to have 100+ sites on one VPS, like literally never at all

Then a few months ago I had to finally press the button to switch Tommy off, forever, I mean how nerd is it is to have feelings about a VPS? But without this little server I wouldn't have my life right now. 

I always imagined Tommy as some 🐻 brown bear, so I made it a little retirement page where it's sipping coconuts and chilling on the beach 🙏😊 THANK YOU TOMMY!!!!

text:
HYPE has been underperforming recently despite one of its biggest catalysts of the year, fully retracing the entire announcement candle.

Many people argue that this happened because Democrats won the midterm elections, creating significant uncertainty around the legalization of perps in the US.

But is this the entire reason behind the current price action, or is there something else going on?

We traced the onchain activity to see what was really happening and uncovered the real reason.

Hours after the NYSE announcement, FalconX (a well-known brokerage desk) received roughly 910k HYPE ($86M) from several different addresses. Between October 30 and November 3, they distributed most of that HYPE across Coinbase, OKX, and Bybit, likely to sell it over those days and the following ones, causing the dump.

Trace the transactions here: https://t.co/n6OGAmkfw0

Who did this HYPE belong to?

There's no way to know for sure, but our strongest lead points to Paradigm.

In August and September, they sent 692k and 770k HYPE to Coinbase Prime, respectively. They could have held most of it there until they found exit liquidity, and this announcement might have been the catalyst they'd been waiting for to liquidate those bags.

On November 1, Paradigm unstaked 2.55M HYPE. If their strategy is to keep some liquid HYPE in custody until they find new exit liquidity (e.g., when PURR trades above 1.2x mNAV and starts buying HYPE again), this unstaking makes sense, as they seem to have already sold all the liquid HYPE they had left.

So, at this point, there are three likely outcomes:
- If our theory is correct, they'll send that HYPE to Coinbase Prime, where it will sit for a while.
- If not, they might sell it or they might consolidate it into a single address.

Ever wondered where an AI agent actually goes when it places a trade?

On @SteveCapitalOS, the answer is simple, it stays on Solana.

You give the agent a goal, and it reads the market and acts within the risk rules you set.

Spot trades go through Jupiter, perps go through Adrena and Phoenix and Privacy Swaps go through MagicBlock

All are native to Solana, so the agent never has to bridge funds anywhere to get a trade done.

That matters more than people think, because every extra hop is more time and more things that can go wrong.

The agent also can’t wander off and do whatever it wants, since spending limits keep it inside your mandate.

Steve Capital prepares each trade, but you’re the one who signs it from your own wallet.

After that, it settles onchain, so you can look back and check exactly how your agent performed.

If agents are going to manage real money, this is how it should look, and Steve Capital is building it.

text:
Are agents eating up your usage limits?

If yes, then you should be incorporating decision models into your routines 

Let’s reduce your routine’s token consumption by 90%+ and run more frequent routines 

Allow me to explain

One of the most useful things agents do is “wake up” and check on things for you, then take action depending on what it finds

This is what makes them proactive and feel like they’re working for you, not just a tool you use 

We used to call them cron jobs, but someone smart rebranded them to routines - much better

The frequency that your agent wakes up and runs a routine is called the “heartbeat” and every time it wakes up, it has to read a bunch of context and possibly call tools - this uses a lot of tokens

In all the instances when it wakes up and doesn’t find anything that needs action, it wastes all those tokens

Ask your agents to estimate how many tokens are used on each run of your routines - it’s probably 15-40k and if you run a lot of routines frequently it really adds up

So when I see people complaining about hitting usage limits, a big reason is likely in the routines and tokens consumed as part of the wake up process 

I have a ton of routines in my setup and to help prevent hitting limits, I’ve been exploring use of much cheaper decision models like Jev to check status and only wake the expensive LLM agent model if something actually happened 

The difference is more like 1-5k tokens of a super cheap model vs 15-40k tokens of an expensive model

Added up over the course of a month and it can make a big difference 

Save the valuable usage for when something needs to be acted on, not on the checking to see if action is needed

Ok how to do this?

I won’t detail it out because it’s easier to just feed this post to your agent and have it work out a plan for your setup 

In Hermes it’s easy because the cron already has the hook you need, so a job can run a script before the agent, and that script decides whether the expensive agent wakes up

In Grok Bot it’s a little more complicated but still doable

Grok Bot doesn't give you that pre-run hook, so the “watcher” decision model has to live outside it which can be a small cron script or something like a Cloudflare Worker. It runs the same hash-then-Jev check and only contacts the bot when it's time to act

The great thing about this setup is you can run checks much more frequently without worrying much about the cost - run a routine every minute if you want for near real time monitoring

Curious to hear if anyone has tried other methods to optimize their setups

text:
si estás en paraguay y te preocupa poder acceder a tus ahorros, merecés información clara y tiempo para decidir. nadie debería apurarte a usar un producto financiero mientras intentás saber si vas a poder pagar tus cuentas.

para quienes están afectados por la situación de ueno, lo primero es consultar la información del banco central sobre los pagos del fondo de garantía de depósitos. esta es su página para verificar qué entidad fue asignada para recibir tu anticipo:

https://t.co/KR9O0sTKOx

ethereum no puede recuperar dinero que ya está bloqueado en un banco. abrir una billetera no cambia eso.

pero vale la pena explicar qué podrían ofrecer estas herramientas a alguien que quiera tener otra forma de guardar y mover una parte de su dinero en el futuro.

con una cuenta bancaria, dependés del banco para procesar tus pagos y retiros. con una billetera bajo tu control, vos tenés la clave que permite autorizar transferencias a través de una red compartida.

si ya tenés fondos en esa billetera, un problema en tu banco local no te impide automáticamente enviarlos a alguien que los acepte.

imaginá a alguien que trabaja de forma independiente y cobra de un cliente en el exterior. podría recibir en su propia billetera una stablecoin vinculada al dólar y guardarla o transferirla sin tener que depositar primero ese pago en su banco local.

la parte difícil aparece cuando necesita guaraníes para comprar comida o pagar el alquiler. sigue necesitando a alguien dispuesto a cambiar esos tokens, un medio de pago que funcione y un tipo de cambio razonable. durante una crisis, todo eso puede volverse más difícil de conseguir.

esa es la pregunta práctica que conviene hacerse antes de usar estas herramientas: ¿puedo volver a convertir mi dinero en algo que realmente pueda usar para pagar?

hay algunas diferencias importantes.

ethereum es la red. ETH es su activo nativo y su precio puede variar mucho. no necesitás hacer una gran inversión especulativa en ETH para aprender a usar la red.

las stablecoins, como USDT y USDC, son otros tokens diseñados para mantener un valor cercano al dólar. dependen de sus emisores y de las reservas que los respaldan. pueden perder esa paridad, sufrir restricciones o volverse difíciles de cambiar. además, si tus gastos son en guaraníes, tener un activo vinculado al dólar te expone a las variaciones del tipo de cambio.

una cuenta en una plataforma de intercambio también es distinta de una billetera que vos controlás. dejar dinero en una plataforma significa depender de otra empresa para poder acceder a él.

la autocustodia puede reducir esa dependencia, pero también pone más responsabilidad en tus manos. perder las palabras de recuperación, compartirlas con un estafador o enviar fondos al destino equivocado puede provocar una pérdida permanente. los emisores de stablecoins pueden restringir transferencias incluso cuando vos guardás los tokens en tu propia billetera.

por eso tendría cuidado con cualquiera que presente esto como algo “a prueba de corridas bancarias”.

si querés explorar estas opciones, empezá por aprender sin mover dinero. entendé cómo recuperarías el acceso a tu billetera. nunca compartas tus palabras de recuperación con nadie, ni siquiera con alguien que se ofrezca a ayudarte.

después, revisá el recorrido completo: pasar de guaraníes a un activo compatible, retirarlo a tu billetera y volver a convertirlo en guaraníes. verificá el token y la red exactos, las comisiones, los montos mínimos y cómo vas a pagar el costo de la transferencia de regreso.

la documentación pública de el dorado incluye medios de pago paraguayos y retiros de USDT a través de arbitrum one, una red que permite operar dentro del ecosistema de ethereum con menores costos. es una opción que merece verificarse localmente. no la he probado, y que un medio de pago figure en una lista no demuestra que funcione hoy.

text:
交易的前提不是“预测”准确，而是“计划”完善。就拿STH-RP这个信号来说，通常被视为“情绪”的熊牛分界线。

如价格在此得到支撑，说明在临近成本考验时，投资者选择跟进，而不是逃跑 —— 信心表现。

如价格直接击穿，说明担惊受怕已经让投资者开始不计成本的出逃 —— 恐慌表现。

从过往周期来看，处在熊牛过渡期的BTC，有时能在STH-RP获得支撑，有时会跌破。那我们应该如何应对呢？

不要试图去预测“这次会怎样？”，而是应该先想好，如果出现哪种情况应该怎么做。

这里我举2个例子仅供参考：

例1、在STH-RP上方买入，日线收盘跌破一定百分比（比如5%）就止损。等下一次站上STH-RP再买入，跌破再卖出。

这个方案的坏处是，如果BTC围绕STH-RP来回穿梭，那么你的资金会反复磨损。但好处是，你绝对不会错过牛市最疯狂的那一段主升浪行情。

例2、当跌破STH-RP开始分批买入，越跌越买，拉低成本。站上STH-RP后停止买入。从长期来看，亏钱的概率很低。在熊牛过渡期，但凡低于STH-RP都是机会。

亦或是现在有现货仓位，如跌破STH-RP，可用对等仓位的合约对冲风险敞口；等站上STH-RP后再平掉。

总之，方法有很多，你要找到最适合自己的。

不要去预测，无依据的预测市场，等同于开盲盒。与其这样，还不如拿个硬币丢一丢。
author: Murphychen888
quoted_text:
在2023年1月到9月期间，BTC价格在短期持有者成本线（STH-RP）1个标准差的位置（图中黄线）遇阻后，都出现了一定程度的回调。

第一次完美回踩至蓝线（STH-RP），第二次略微跌破蓝线，第三次回调至蓝线和绿线之间（-1 STD）。

当前蓝线在$75,700左右，绿线在$68,900左右。如据此单纯刻舟的话，以下3种情况都有一定的发生概率：

1、回撤到$75,700为止；
2、回撤到$72,300为止;
3、回撤到1和2之间。

还是那句话：我们不做预测，只做计划。

text:
文中需要补充一点：例2方法的好处是，你能拿到相对“便宜”的BTC，因为这些都是别人割肉抛出来带血的筹码。

但坏处是，如果没有跌破STH-RP或短期略微跌破，你将错失一次绝佳的介入机会，甚至错过后面的大行情。

所以，在交易的世界，没有什么方法是完美无缺的，只有最适合自己的。

text:
你是否需要很长的上下文？

NVIDIA 新论文标题给了一种答案:《You don't need long context》。

现在模型的 context window 越做越长，128K、256K、1M 已经很常见。

但论文先指出一个很现实的问题：context 越长，后面的 token 越贵。

在他们测试的开放模型上，256K context 相比 16K，每个输出 token 的推理成本高出约 3.6–7 倍。

作者于是做了一件很简单的事：

让 Agent 定期「压缩」自己的工作状态。

对话变长以后，把当前进度、关键发现和下一步计划总结成一个更短的 semantic state，再从新的 context 继续执行。

原始历史依然可以保存，需要时再选择性读取；模型没必要每一步都把全部历史重新塞进 context。

结果在 6 个长时任务上，Claude Opus 4.5 和 GPT-5.6 Sol 即使把 context 压到很短，整体准确率依然基本保持稳定；估算推理成本分别最高降低约 8.8× 和 5×。

他们甚至测试了一个更极端的版本：

Agent 每执行一个动作，就重新压缩一次 context。

性能依然没有崩。

这也引出了论文里一个挺有意思的概念：Semantic State Space Model。

未来长时 Agent 也许不需要维护一条越来越长的聊天记录，而是持续维护一个小而清晰的「当前状态」，执行一步，再更新一次。

长 context 当然有价值，但很多 Agent 任务真正需要的，可能是更好的状态管理和按需检索。

把所有历史一直带在身上，未必是最好的长期记忆方式。

quoted_text:
I burned a shitload of compute so you don't have to. Releasing the Harness Leaderboard.

Which harness should you run your open model in? I ran 28,849 trials to find out.

The leaderboard compares nine coding-agent harnesses on open models. In each comparison only the harness changes: the model, provider and reasoning effort stay fixed, and every task gets three attempts.

The trials ran GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Flint on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE, for $4,746 of inference.

Averaged over the three models, mini-swe-agent (@KLieret), a bash-only agent, solves 51.4% of tasks and @openclaw 27.3%. Four others are statistically tied with mini-swe-agent.

One of them is Pi (@pidotdev), at 49.4% for $0.29 per solved task, about 45% less than mini-swe-agent's $0.53.

The best harness depends on the model: mini-swe-agent on GLM-5.3-Flash, Hermes Agent (@NousResearch) on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Kimi Code (@Kimi_Moonshot) on Flint.

@opencode costs $3.35 per solved task, 11.7 times as much as Pi.

See Harness Hub's Harness Lens for what the nine harnesses do differently. It documents the prompts, tools and compaction of 34 coding-agent harnesses and links every claim to its source.

text:
hearing some chatter that anthropic is now lowering down to $1tn to get this IPO done. let me explain why this doesnt matter and its actually all over-

the entire existence of this company is based on a funding model that inherently has extreme asset liability mismatch. what that means is that just like the hyperscalers are diluting their equity fund capex, there is an expectation that anthropic will also have to do the same. ie it needs strong equity to perpetuate the scheme

but if you IPO at the wrong price (and dont get a pop which increasingly appears they wont be; spacex already below) then youre now in the death spiral that crypto investors should be very familiar with: its called the reflexivity trap of the confidence game. its the "ill bid FTT at $22 all day" or the "steady lads UST is $1" game, with all its lucid horrors. and here is the key insight- the confidence game exists at the service of the creditors. if there is no credit, there is simply no equity. and there is no credit, if there is no collateral

if the credit rating agencies are not going to give IG at $2tn, they are certaintly not going a better HY rating at $1tn. and there is no world in which anthropic can exist without credit because ~$1tn of commit, much of which is noncancellable, is a straight up negative equity pledge

yet there were two scenarios in which i was willing to concede anthropic could IPO: first 1) the improbable but possible was if the hyperscalers/chips oligopoly came to rescue and plug the hole, given their incestuous nature of revenue bookings and paper gains/losses at scale. but it is clear now that the market has spoken this will lead to a mutual death, and should not be attempted. or perversely even better, they are actually better off letting anthropic go to zero so they can acquire the pieces on the cheap which is the best nash equilibrium outcome, not just for the dominant player but for society at large. second 2) the us government can nationalize the company and collude with other sovereigns (like UAE, Saudi, Japan who are basically already the checks) to force its funding as a collective bargain. this gives you trillions, which is actually the most effective backstop to restore market confidence. the first edge case does require an IPO, but the second edge case here for which i believe there is still a good chance that this is the ultimate end game- will require a failed IPO to recapitalize at a normalized price for the consortium (and dont forget that openai front ran this investor group in anticipation of this dynamic to play out as a private co last month)

i believe the market is crapping out today because the market is recognizing it will not IPO. and actually, as ive said before, this is a very good thing. i might even imagine that the market could quickly rebound on the news of its IPO being delayed because it allows #2) to play out, as not only a national, but an international bailout. the US is more likely to tolerate, even relish, the taxes of foreginers to fund our domestic companies. that is the only end game that really matters, and the end game i am going to be excited to see

we'll see if this newly revamped washington can figure it out

富国岛学习营结束了。来之前，我以为这几天是带着大家来学习。结果几天下来，我自己的本子上也记得满满的。

第一天，Jeff @taida88 给大家讲 Binance AI。他讲得很有画面感——同一个币安 App，刚入门的人打开，看到的是更简单的解释和提示；天天盯盘的人打开，看到的是更深的数据和市场背景。

后面几堂课，大家已经发了很多，我只说两点记得最深的。

一个来自 Binance Research 的分享：市场反应的，往往不是利率本身，而是大家的预期变得有多快。
另一个来自@AncoBinance 的钱包分享。钱包空投覆盖了 1199 万人，让我意识到，对很多人来说，币安钱包就是他们进入链上的第一道门。这道门容不容易迈进，比其他功能还重要。

最后一天，我们请老师们围坐在一起，挨个听大家的反馈。哪里用着不顺手、哪里还能改，都直接说出来。

听起来都是小细节，但每一条背后都是一个具体的人、一个具体的使用习惯。我也更理解 Jeff 说的「个性化了」。

以前的交易所，所有人打开看到的都是同一张行情表。以后，每个人看到的币安可能都不一样，但出发点是同一个——让更多人用得上、也看得懂金融工具。

我想这就是学习营最有意义的地方。产品做得再聪明，也得先听懂用的人。

当天晚上一姐@heyibinance 远程连线还提到一点，那就是用户的信任对我们来说是最贵的，币安能做的，是靠每天的经营和兑付，一点点把它累积起来。对我们来说，是一次次反馈能够落到实处，真的帮大家解决问题。

最后谢谢各位老师这几天的坦诚。币安一直说用户至上，我觉得它最真实的样子，就是像这几天这样，坐下来听你们说。很珍惜和大家相聚的时光，我们 #binanceblockchainweek 曼谷再见！

text:
hearing some chatter that anthropic is now lowering down to $1tn to get this IPO done. let me explain why this doesnt matter and its actually all over-

the entire existence of this company is based on a funding model that inherently has extreme asset liability mismatch. what that means is that just like the hyperscalers are diluting their equity fund capex, there is an expectation that anthropic will also have to do the same. ie it needs strong equity to perpetuate the scheme

but if you IPO at the wrong price (and dont get a pop which increasingly appears they wont be; spacex already below) then youre now in the death spiral that crypto investors should be very familiar with: its called the reflexivity trap of the confidence game. its the "ill bid FTT at $22 all day" or the "steady lads UST is $1" game, with all its lucid horrors. and here is the key insight- the confidence game exists at the service of the creditors. if there is no credit, there is simply no equity. and there is no credit, if there is no collateral

if the credit rating agencies are not going to give IG at $2tn, they are certaintly not going a better HY rating at $1tn. and there is no world in which anthropic can exist without credit because ~$1tn of commit, much of which is noncancellable, is a straight up negative equity pledge

yet there were two scenarios in which i was willing to concede anthropic could IPO: first 1) the improbable but possible was if the hyperscalers/chips oligopoly came to rescue and plug the hole, given their incestuous nature of revenue bookings and paper gains/losses at scale. but it is clear now that the market has spoken this will lead to a mutual death, and should not be attempted. or perversely even better, they are actually better off letting anthropic go to zero so they can acquire the pieces on the cheap which is the best nash equilibrium outcome, not just for the dominant player but for society at large. second 2) the us government can nationalize the company and collude with other sovereigns (like UAE, Saudi, Japan who are basically already the checks) to force its funding as a collective bargain. this gives you trillions, which is actually the most effective backstop to restore market confidence. the first edge case does require an IPO, but the second edge case here for which i believe there is still a good chance that this is the ultimate end game- will require a failed IPO to recapitalize at a normalized price for the consortium (and dont forget that openai front ran this investor group in anticipation of this dynamic to play out as a private co last month)

i believe the market is crapping out today because the market is recognizing it will not IPO. and actually, as ive said before, this is a very good thing. i might even imagine that the market could quickly rebound on the news of its IPO being delayed because it allows #2) to play out, as not only a national, but an international bailout. the US is more likely to tolerate, even relish, the taxes of foreginers to fund our domestic companies. that is the only end game that really matters, and the end game i am going to be excited to see

we'll see if this newly revamped washington can figure it out

这周开始做一些获客和补贴，也有不少新用户会产生疑问：为什么给的返现这么高，收益从哪来？

可能很少有创始人会公开披露自己的商业模式，正好简单写一篇科普帖子，拆解介绍一下运营一家Neobank（U卡平台）的收入和成本大概会是什么。

先说大家最感兴趣的U卡吧。

U卡一般分为三种模式：

1.直连发卡行，或者和有卡组会员资质的公司合作，需要自己申请一个独立的BIN, 经过卡组的合规审核，这个周期一般是6-12个月。对应的成本是每个月固定要给银行交一笔费用，从几千美金到十万美金都有，每家的政策不一样。发卡行决定了你的卡是哪个地区的，实际term怎么样，这个差异非常大。目前最优质的还是美国地区的发卡，结构通常是按照MCC返现，有些B端场景最高能到3%以上，但标准的还是在2%左右，C端的Bin通常在1-2%区间。发卡行会扣除一部分的手续费，剩下的分给U卡平台。外汇汇损也取决于发卡行的政策，市面标准通常是1%（如大家最常见的，Rain发行的U卡）。以这个方式合作，U卡平台要自己承担反洗钱和用户审核。

2.和Rain/Bridge等专门的发卡公司进行白标合作，他们有些自身就是发卡行，有些也是和发卡行合作，能快速缩短申请周期，一般3个月就可以上线。对应的他们也会收取一部分费用，可以理解为启动更快、初始成本更低、但是毛利更低的方案。以这个方式合作。这类公司会承担一些反洗钱和审核，也会定期筛查。

3.用一些大型的Fintech平台（卡台），以企业卡的方式发行，优点是更快，大部分给的返现会比较低，少部分因为有补贴甚至条件更好，缺点是相对没那么合规，不稳定。

综合下来，U卡这边最终能有的收入，在不额外加外汇费用的情况下，应该是在1-2%这个区间。Infini也是这个区间，因此我们基础返现是1.5%，前期小亏一点，后面会随着规模和渠道优化盈利一些。当然，大家常见的头部平台，基本都为了增长采取净补贴的烧钱获客方案，我们也不能避免，这部分我猜大家都是在月交易量 0.5-1%的补贴，当然早晚有一天会回归常态。

第二个是银行账户和法币出入金，能做这个业务基本都需要牌照了，给银行的固定费用和发卡差不多。

一般模式是，每个独立的子账户都收取一个月费（从1-3美金不等，我们现在为了获客是免费提供），然后还会有每笔交易的费用（银行一般会在支付通道上加，比如SWIFT/ACH等费用），各家差别也挺大的。除此之外，部分银行提供法币与稳定币的承兑服务，按照百分比收钱（通常在0.1%以内）。因为涉及到一来一回，所以如果头寸对冲的足够好，应该能把成本控制在0.05%以内，甚至更低）。这部分业务是不可能补贴的，否则会被撸死，并且还要承担反洗钱的成本和责任，因此行业常见的收费模式是0.2-0.3%，infini的定价也是这个范围，我们后续还会为大客户降低到0.1%。

再之后，各家的业务范围就不一样了。比如资管理财我们做的会更好，本质上还是因为有更好的套利策略，这个放在传统银行模式下就是贷款赚取利差，放在Crypto里常见的模式就是通过Defi/Cefi套利。这部分利润差别会很大，也会和流动性和行情有关，长期健康的商业模式应该是1-3%的利差收益，规模越大毛利越低（因为优质收益、安全稳定的策略容量有限，这是一个不可能三角）。

像我们的企业产品还有稳定币收单，收费是0.2-0.3%，成本是0.1%左右（因为自己承担了Gas归集成本和流动性占用成本。Tron会尤其高，新链相对好一些）

所以回到正题，为什么我们能有比较好的返现，一方面是因为不断在优化从发卡行拿到的比例（有些BIN应该能比常见的Rain要高一些），另一方面我们的资管Carry部分会拿来补贴，因此要求资沉。当然这两个加起来还是不一定能够cover的住，但其实能亏的也有限，都是经过精算的。当然希望未来能通过优秀的留存，以及其他业务的收入，维持一个长期稳定、有利润的商业模式。

最后大家关心的资产安全、透明等角度，自然都是很重要的事情，对于前者我比任何人都更操心，也踩过坑。所以infini提现会慢，因为自动化程度没那么高，现在这个被盗事件频出的年代，已经不能信任系统了，更复杂和臃肿的人工审核体系是短期最优解，现在各家交易所应该也都在跟进了，明显越来越严格，更贴近传统金融。这也是行业大的趋势，是我们在没法解决这种本质性问题前的被迫方案。

关于透明度，最终是一个平衡。一方面，更高的透明度会让用户更方便地验证，但同时也会让黑客更方便地验证。另一方面，传统审计其实是不能很好解决Crypto这种形式的，正如同交易所应该常见的也是用储备金证明，而不是靠审计公司的报告，只有合规资管是强制要求审计的，所以我们后面的合规资管产品会做。当然如储备金证明等还有一系列方案，也有很多优秀团队在做，我们当然也会采用，只不过一方面有成本，一方面产研有很多基建和功能要开发，所以是一个长期话题。

信任需要建立，需要沟通，其实最终所有解决方案都不是那个核心，因为所有证明都可以伪造，只是成本问题。核心还是分摊风险，我希望大家信任我们，愿意体验我们的产品，会争取更多的信任，但我也不希望大家把身家性命都交给我，我也背负不起。

分散资产、分摊风险，评估风险，是任何时代都绕不开的话题，更是对自己负责的唯一方法。我们不可能也不会尝试让每个人都信任，我们只能在各个方面每天都变好一点🫡

text:
Your trading strategy might be worth more than your last trade.

Most traders spend years developing strategies, testing setups and finding an edge.

But what if you could actually monetize that edge without trading someone else's capital yourself?

That's one of the more interesting use cases @termix_ai is exploring with its BNB Quant Agent campaign on @BNBCHAIN.

Instead of keeping your strategy private, you can turn it into a service that other traders can access.

Here's how it works:

❯ Strategy creators list their trading strategies
❯ Users choose a strategy and set their USDC trading cap
❯ Trading terms start at 6 hours
❯ Providers can earn management fees from completed jobs

And there's an extra incentive layer.

Qualifying completed jobs can earn 100 TP per USDC for users and 50 TP per USDC for strategy providers, subject to the campaign's settlement requirements.

The interesting part isn't just the rewards.

It's the idea that a trader's knowledge and strategy could become a monetizable product.

Not every good trader wants to manage outside capital directly.

Some might just want to build a strategy and let others use it.

Of course, a good strategy doesn't guarantee profitable trades.

But turning trading strategies into accessible onchain services? That's an interesting direction.

text:
Feel like 1975-2000 was the 'The Age Of Qualifications' - 

if you had the right degree, or certification, or etc, you could make tons of money...

Then 2000-2025 was 'The Age Of Skills' - 

suddenly the internet had flattened everything, and qualifications weren't as important, but skills like SEO, or paid ads, or website design, or video editing, or coding- were suddenly extremely valuable. 

And now we're entering the next age, which will be defined by the advent of AI...

And I think this will be 'The Age Of Magnetism' - 

And what will matter most is not any qualifications you have or any specialized skills you have...

But rather your inherent qualities as a person, and your ability to instill trust or hope or excitement or some other feeling in other people on an interpersonal level...

Are you smart? Are you intellectually curious? Are you creative? Are you disciplined? Are you wise? Are you charismatic? Are you interesting? Do people like you?

Its sort of like Nietzsche's quote on being 'a herald of the lightning'...

The 'lightning' today is our humanity (in this age of infinite machines), and those who can embody this humanity and remind others of their own humanity will thrive the most in it. 

This doesn't mean everyone needs to be a philosopher or influencer or something - but what it means is that, when everyone has equal footing via armies of AI agents and robots, the defining variable becomes this sense of 'magnetism', and the ability to attract other humans to your endeavors.

text:
The emergency reset meant to clear a bad price could hand the next price to the fastest signer.

During Mystic Finance's Octarine RFQ review, Zealynx found that `invalidate()` deleted the oracle price. The first signer to call `pushPrice` afterward could set any new anchor without the normal change limit.

Every later update was measured against that anchor. A rogue signer could publish an extreme price, while an honest correction was rejected by the same bounds the first push bypassed.

Mystic fixed the Medium finding by requiring the owner to `seedPrice` before signer updates can resume.

兄弟们，你们嘴是真严啊！
这么好用的免费语音输入法，怎么现在才推荐啊！

④ 我最喜欢的是纠错功能，它会长记性。像 Claude、Vibe Coding 这种词，第一次基本就能自动纠对。

万一认错了，你手动改一次，它就收进词库，以后再也不用改。每天纠了多少、记住了多少，还能看到数据统计。

quoted_text:
我发现推上不少人，尤其是在美国硅谷、华尔街工作的华人，多少有点活在一个泡泡里。

过去几年，科技和金融行业赚了不少钱，portfolio 也涨得不错，大家天天讨论 AGI、生产力革命，觉得 AI 改变世界是不可阻挡的趋势

这些判断中长期可能都没错，但问题是，普通美国人真的也是这么想的吗？

对一个普通美国家庭来说，他可能根本没有多少美股资产，也不关心英伟达今天又涨了多少。他更关心的是油价、超市账单、房贷，以及自己明年还有没有工作。

你在Sand Hill Road的会议室里兴奋地讨论 AI 如何取代人类劳动，他听到的可能是：那我的工作怎么办？Mortgage 谁来付？Bills 谁来 pay？

举个例子，一个 Uber 司机今天辛辛苦苦跑了十几个小时，赚了两三百美元。晚上回家打开电视，看到 Elon Musk 兴奋地宣布 Robotaxi 即将大规模取代人类司机。

你觉得他会跟着欢呼 AI 革命，还是会担心自己过几年就没饭吃了？到了投票的时候，他更愿意支持 Elon 背书的候选人，还是一个承诺保护普通人就业的候选人？

我觉得这次民主党的大胜，值得科技圈和金融圈认真反思。很多人已经习惯了从资本市场的视角看世界，却忽略了大多数选民是靠劳动收入，而不是资产升值生活的. 科技进步和普通人的利益，从来不一定在每个阶段都是一致的。

对持有科技股的人来说，AI 是财富增长的机会；对一个随时可能失业的美国蓝领普通人来说，AI 首先可能是生存威胁。

这两个群体看到的，根本就不是同一个世界

text:
FALSE. Prediction markets dont "converge" towards model prices.

it's the other way around.

I analysed Nate Silver's vs Kalshi's forecasts on 137 close races in the 2 month leading to the election.

at NO point in time did Nate's FLIPR model give higher average odds to the eventual winners, meaning Kalshi was always more precise.

If prediction markets really "converged" towards FLIPR odds then you would expect to see FLIPR lead in precision at each update, with Kalshi playing catchup.

It's pretty obvious why when you know how election models work.

All FLIPR essentially does is aggregate public information  :
- weighted polls
- district partisanship and incumbency
- public expert race ratings. 

These are all publicly available and used by @Kalshi traders before they have a chance to make their way into a Silver Bulletin forecast.

Sorry but you cannot get alpha by buying a $5 Substack subscription.

今年我个人原因没去，说几句前两次参加学习营的感受。

1、对交易所来说，办这种活动除了跟社区保持联系，还能听到不同渠道的一线产品反馈。

币安Alpha就是两年前在冲绳聊出来的。去年在韩国也吐槽过很多卡点。说句实在的，华人背景的交易所BOGG在产品上能秒杀其他海外所。一个很重要的原因，就是他们真的把产品当回事。愿意花时间把做内容的、做渠道的叫到一起，听听各自的用户平时在问什么、交易时又在哪一步卡住。产品上的差距，很多时候就是这么一个细节一个细节拉开的。

在海外办一场活动，看着要花不少钱。但各条业务线能当面听到自己负责的产品到底是个啥口碑，哪儿好用、哪儿天天被吐槽。我觉得这钱花得值，一句话总结，我觉得平台是受益的。

其实说到底，币安也是一家商业机构，同样要遵循市场的规律。我始终相信，一家企业能够长期走下去，归根结底还是因为它能够持续为用户和行业创造价值。

text:
Closing your leveraged position is the one moment your protocol treats as an afterthought. It is also the moment an attacker has been waiting for.

A close almost always ends in a swap. A swap in a public mempool is a broadcast of your intent. Without a minimum output the attacker just moves the price ahead of your trade, lets you execute at the worst possible tick, then moves it back and pockets the difference.

We keep finding the same shape in audits, worded differently each time:

A reserve sold with no floor, draining value from every liquidity provider by omission.

A minimum output hardcoded to zero. Any searcher watching the pool reads that as an invitation.

A withdrawal function with no slippage check at all, so leaving the protocol becomes the single highest value target in the whole system.

Even a yield update with a predictable timestamp gets sandwiched, no swap involved.

Worth a search through your own repo: every swap and withdraw path, and where its minimum output comes from. If it's zero, or set by whoever profits from skipping it, start there.

text:
今天币圈最大的笑话，是马斯克在美股亏了钱，跑来推特拿 CZ 撒气。

昨晚美股大崩盘，特斯拉直接给干趴下 11 个点。
彭博一算，老马一天身家蒸发了将近 800 亿美元。
800 亿刀啊，换成谁都得心绞痛。
正好狗狗币创始人发推吐槽行情太烂，心情糟糕透顶。
老马一看，自己亏惨了怎么能一个人哭？
反手掏出一张存货已久的“红脸 CZ”暴跌表情包，直接甩了上去。

全网当场笑喷。
大涨的时候你们天天玩“绿 CZ”开香槟，昨晚大跌，老马居然自己搞了个“红 CZ”搞针对。
最冤的就是 CZ 本人。
人在家中坐，锅从天上来。
CZ 火速下场对线，艾特老马和狗币创始人，反手甩了一张《上古卷轴》名图——“我膝盖中了一箭”。
言下之意：我特么招谁惹谁了，你股票跌了拿我当出气筒？

结果何一坐不住了。
一姐直接杀进战场，甩出《黑客帝国》红绿蓝三颗药丸，居高临下质问马斯克：“你选哪个颜色的药丸？💁🏻‍♀️”
推特直接炸锅。
表哥还在委屈自己躺枪，一姐已经在线让老马按时吃药了。
到底是吃认清现实的红药丸，还是吃回血看涨的绿药丸？

最离谱的是链上那帮赌狗。
外面大盘在办丧事，三大顶流在推特互丢表情包，结果链上一个叫 GM 的 Meme 币，被这波互动硬生生从 70 万拉到了近千万市值，两小时暴涨十倍。

老马亏了 800 亿，CZ 膝盖中一箭，一姐在线送药，链上赌狗在废墟里开香槟。
这个魔幻的市场，真是一天都离不开这几个活宝。

text:
感慨一下，腾讯混元 @TencentHunyuan  这波是真的上桌了啊！

腾讯混元Hy4前两天正式发布了。
这两天我自己在WorkBuddy里测了很久，也通过混元开放平台的API，把模型接入我们 @lobehub  自己的LobeBench，完整跑了一下。
结果确实有点超出我的预期👀

测试用的是LobeBench-Hard 50，包含50道来自我们实际开发过程中遇到的真实业务场景的高难度Agent任务，每道题重复测试3次，主要考察模型在日常使用中能不能把复杂的活干好，最终交付可用的结果。

Hy4最终有26道题连续3次全部通过，通过率为52%；
如果按照至少成功1次计算，则有40道题能够完成，占到了80%🎉

如果按照细分领域来看，结果也很有意思。
Life & Health、Productivity、Research & Careers三个类别的通过率都达到了100%，Marketing & Content达到80%，电商和软件开发为67%，金融类相对弱一些，为60%。

这个成绩我觉得相当不错👍 
尤其是80%的题目至少能够成功完成一次，说明Hy4已经具备解决相当一部分复杂实际任务的能力。
当然，52%的三次全过率也说明，它在执行稳定性上还有继续提升的空间。

而外部评测也基本印证了我的感受。
@ArtificialAnlys  前两天刚发布的最新综合智力指数里，Hy4排到了中国模型第二，仅次于Kimi K3.1 Pro，和Grok 4.7打平。
在更接近真实Agent任务的Agent Arena上，Hy4则冲到了全球第13名。
按照目前的榜单，权重开放后将位列开源模型第一，而且执行成本也很有竞争力。

说实话，之前几代混元给我的感觉，一直都还差那么一口气😮‍💨 
这次Hy4的进步，确实比我原来预期的大不少。

有点感慨，混元4这次是真的上大人那桌了。 
以前总觉得它还在小孩那桌打，现在终于有资格坐到全球第一梯队的牌桌上，和那些最强的模型正面较量了。
不得不说，腾讯这次确实做出了点东西👏

quoted_text:
下午跟几位熬夜不睡觉的美国老哥，打了电话，聊了聊这波叫停 AI、数据中心潮，他们说身边绝大多数本地居民和同事，都非常支持暂停这东西。

因为它不仅让当地人，支付了更多的电费，而且这玩意也无法产生大量就业。

而科技创业者们又天天炫耀，自家靠 AI 裁员了很多人，结合不断上涨的物价，让大家极为抵触。

站在不炒股，只是普通打工人的视角，AI 革命的新闻，反而增加人们进一步负面的看法，毕竟世界上互联网从业者仍是极少数。

最倒霉的就是本来在农场好好住的老哥，几十年下来，社区一直非常安逸，然后突然发现自家社区不远荒置的农场，盖了超大数据中心，不停的施工，不断出入的卡车，大老远就能听到轰鸣声，根本无法让人安心休息。

而且他们给我讲了一个案例，说是某个地方开发商跟地方官员签了保密协议，居民最后才知道，然后这事闹的很大，导致大家更加对此进行排斥。

所以既然阻止不了，就干脆全投民主党，也不管民主党什么政策，只要把支持 AI 和数据中心的，搞下去就行，于是就上演了本轮的中期选举结果。

text:
I was recently affected by the layoffs at @0xMiden, and I’m looking for my next Product Manager role in the Bay Area.

I’d love to keep building in payments, especially stablecoins and agentic payments.

Over the past few years at @0xMiden and @0xPolygon, I’ve:

• Led a crypto wallet from scoping through launch to reach 20k user registrations, coordinating a seven-person team across engineering, design, and QA.
• Worked with roughly 12 external ecosystem partners, translating their requirements, feedback, and integration blockers into roadmap and release priorities.
• Built and launched AggLayer’s developer portal and sandbox, with tutorials and code examples to help developers get started.
• Researched zero-knowledge infrastructure and develop the Chainless Apps framework, connecting technical research with practical use cases for developers.

Working on a crypto wallet made the practical challenges of stablecoin adoption much clearer to me: how people bring funds in, move them across networks, and actually use them.

I want to keep working on those problems, including how AI agents will make payments.

I’ve also been building an offline, on-device LLM app and AI-assisted workflows for team syncs, product feedback, and moving GitHub issues through implementation. I’m comfortable getting into the code as well as owning the product.

If you know PM hiring managers at @Stablecoin, @stripe, @Visa, or other teams building payments infrastructure and AI products, I’d really appreciate an introduction!

And to my teammates at Miden and Polygon Labs: thank you. I’ve learned a lot from building with you, and wish you all the best!

text:
休息了将近半年，最近重新开始看市场，也重新把自己丢回交易这件事里。

今天起正式加入 @TurboFlow_xyz，担任首席客服，和 @tonytfxyz @bigtake10 一起，让普通人也能真正坐上交易桌 🪑

17年就入行的我，完全不需要去上班的，但为什么我还是加入了TurboFlow？和 @bigtake10 彻夜长谈了好几次电话，确实看到了他们做这个产品的决心，准确来说，我是被他们这个义无返顾的勇气撼动了。

和一些交易员朋友也聊过，他们觉得现在已经够好了，用户能参与就不错了。但我自己的感受是，如果大多数工具依然围绕机构和大户设计，普通人还是得先变成“专业玩家”才能真正玩起来，那这个市场其实还没有真正打开。

币圈一夜暴富的故事很多，可真正卡住大多数人的，往往不是判断力，而是那些一直存在的摩擦：开仓费、复杂度、必须先懂很多规则才能下单。很多人不是没有观点，只是一打开软件就被这些细节挡在门外了。

用过 TurboFlow 以后，我第一次觉得“参与”这件事可以更平权一点。最低 $2 就能入场，没有吓人的开仓费，没有必须先成为专业玩家才能玩的门槛。

很多人不是不会交易，只是在跨链、费用、规则、操作细节上被卡住了。如果基础设施能再简单一点、透明一点、顺手一点，更多人其实是愿意坐到这张桌子上一起切磋。

与我还有 TurboFlow 一起探索这件事，
Everyone gets a seat
这次，我也坐下了。

text:
今天又在加密书屋群里聊及美利坚全盘翻蓝以后的 Clarity Act。

1/我觉得之前 Clarity Act 在众议院以超多数票通过，绝对足以说明至少短期内 Clarity 中承诺的那些基础保障是两党共识。
参议院没过是党争问题，不是共识破灭。

这点最重要的表现是 Robinhood 的 Layer 2。
Robinhood 的政策法律团队一定认为，现在去发一个打着去中心化名号的 Layer 2，可以让他们做一些之前法律限制无法做的事情，可以让他们赚一些之前无法赚的钱，能享受一些他们之前如果做了就会被追责的法律豁免。
这个传统金融套个去中心化区块链的壳子做监管套利的趋势，绝对还没有力竭。

2/民主党手握两院，川普系最值得攻击的点必然包含 Trump memecoin 和 World Liberty Financial 这俩。
这俩不被咬两年不太可能，期间也必定波及其他的加密项目。

3/Vitalik 24 年大选前撰文说反对根据 pro-Crypto 与否来投票。川普牛是我们行业走的弯路，一定要还债的。
群友说得更好：川普实际上表现出了加密市场最烂的一部分，而且他表示这套我玩得比你们好——不就是喊单拉盘么，球长也可以亲自做。
https://t.co/37q9jgQhkZ

4/我们整个行业本质上都高度寄生于监管套利这个核心概念上。
但监管套利的基础是民族国家对金融或者对所有可监管世界都越来越家长化，而这个家长化的尺度一定是会矫枉过正的。
监管套利是否可持续这个问题背后其实是现在的监管有没有超越正常合理范围，有没有监管造成的磨损比诈骗造成的磨损更大等等。
我自己作为右派，当然觉得监管造成的后果已经事实上更鼓励所有人都做巨婴，但显然我这个观点不是共识。
群友追问：如果接下来监管不让你套利呢？

5/反过来说，Airbnb 和 Uber 本质上也是监管套利。
且无论是因为当时的环境整体宽松，还是传统旅店业、出租车业已经烂透到不改不行，后面确实都变成监管退，而 Airbnb、Uber 进。
回到我们一开始话题的由头，Clarity Act 在众议院通过，本质上也是美国明确有加密货币行业进、而监管退的苗头。

6/21 世纪是家长式政府的世纪。
纽约或伦敦或任何中心化的金融体系本质上一直都在用效率换安全、用公民主体性换安全。而这个几乎一直是单向的流动，一直在让渡更多的效率和主体性。
经过 30 年的让渡，有没有让渡到一个夸张、离谱、矫枉过正的程度？

如果有，则加密行业现在做的向监管要空间、搞主权个人的无许可金融就是拨乱反正；
如果没有，这 Clarity Act 当时表现出来的共识就会在短期内崩溃。

这段讨论的部分背景详见：https://t.co/iZAqHSw4Lq

7/还有一个东西在显著复杂化问题的情况：AI 时代大规模的 Cyber security 攻击。
目前听说某个韩国加密交易所已经准备改为 T+1 提现了，连加密行业本身都在主动尝试让渡更多自主性和效率去换安全。
所以这种共识应该就很脆弱，甚至完全可以消散倒流。
所以要挑战臃肿、低效、僵化、腐朽的传统金融，则至少我们要不断证明，我们的行业足以提供以一个值得信任的、总体上美好的 counter offer。

text:
Anthropic 盘前合约套利（在entropy做多在binance做空）目前大家最大的顾虑就是外界广泛猜测的 Anthropic 是否会延期甚至推迟。我这边结合我自己和claude的分析，逐一将大家可能关心的点拆解一下

1. 昨晚美股大跌，市场反应悲观，现在上市会不会拿不到好估值？

我个人认为肯定会受到一定影响，但Anthropic仍然可以通过降低募资总额、减少新发股数来缓解该影响。目前我得到的消息是Anthropic仍然在参与询价的各个基金密切接触当中，没有明显的放弃或推迟迹象，不过据说确实下修了募资额到400亿美元左右。另外今天美股隔夜盘半导体股票上涨迅猛，我认为昨晚大概率是市场积攒情绪的集中释放，以及对特定机构的定向猎杀。

2. WSJ、路透等媒体今天都发了Anthropic可能推迟上市的相关文章，这些媒体言论该信吗？

首先，这些媒体援引的口径基本都来自参与Anthropic询价的机构的相关人士，而非来自Anthropic官方。目前Anthropic自己没有任何推迟IPO的声明。投资人借媒体言论压低估值，是非常常规的手段，这几乎是大型 IPO 的固定戏码。路演前后，机构投资者会通过媒体放风「估值太高」来压价，承销商也会借报道试探市场反应。

3. Polymarket 上 Anthropic 按时上市的概率盘口跌了很多，会不会是有人有内幕消息了？

大概率不是。首先 Polymarket 上关于 Anthropic 能否按时上市的盘子其实流动性非常稀薄，只需要几百上千美金就能推动几十pp的概率。我个人倾向于认为盘口波动只是散户情绪释放的博弈结果，并非内幕消息。结合Polymarket链上地址分析，也没有支持内幕消息和老鼠仓的发现。

4. Anthropic 有没有充分动力按期上市呢？

我个人认为是有的，Anthropic 上市进程此前已经推迟过一个月，主要原因是想把三季度财报放进路演材料，用三季报证明竞争力。有点讽刺的结果，它等来的三季报，反而成了现在估值被压的理由。上次推迟只差一个月，因为三季报有明确的出炉时间。这次如果推迟，就没有类似的锚点了。

拖下去未必更好，增速放缓的数字会更难看，年底正好是淡季，即使营收的绝对数字更大了，但「增速继续放缓」的故事会延续。如果市场现在就是因为增速放缓而压估值，等四季报出来只会更明显。

另外，员工和早期投资者等着变现，一推再推会影响士气和市场信心。且大模型竞争格局变化莫测，几个月后谁领先不好说，到时候 Anthropic 未必能拿出更好的竞争故事。从公司角度看，「降估值、照原计划发」往往比「等更好的时机」更理性。增速放缓和年底淡季这两个因素，都会让下一次的数据更不好看。

5. 对我们 Anthropic 套利有什么影响？

IPO 推迟或取消，对套利本身是一个中性事件，但是确实有可能导致部分套利资金离场，从而将价差往不利方向推动。

但我个人认为，如果仅仅只是推迟几天（比如Anthropic需要和基金和机构进行更多的交流博弈），套利结论本身和收益空间并没有改变，虽然中途可能更加波折，无非是增加了一定的持有的时间成本。

如果几天后S-1/A靴子落地，价差会迅速收敛，到时想再建仓大概率已经错过黄金时机。不如现在择时建仓，即使确实出现明显推迟，择时退出即可，ROI仍然可观

更重要的是这次非农数据广度比较好
1）专业与商业服务：+7.0万（远超月均约1.5万），其中专业科技服务+3.3万、行政支持与废物管理+2.8万、企业管理+0.9万。临时帮助服务也反弹+1.86万。

有人问经历过昨晚现在怎么看当下市场、跟4号这篇推文的没变化仍然是“AI中场和棒球第三局”。再看昨晚的抛售半导体是重灾区，大云、软件和应用则没那么严重。如之前聊到的，很多人形成了“AI=半导体=存储”的定式思维，一说AI就是半导体、一说半导体就是存储。其实AI也分上中下游，越往后中游的大云厂，下游的应用、agent会更受益以及各种应用场景。

要去拥抱AI主线迁移，每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。今年一季度、二季度，Memory 是最强的；到 8、9 月以后，Optical 开始变强，同时一批之前被砸得很惨的软件、SaaS 也开始走出来。为什么？因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，部署越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。”这也是之前很早就聊到的。

但并不代表我之前没看到风险、引用的推文有我9月前后和10月初认为中期选举前美股要大动荡和调整的过往推文链接。如果说有失误、确实没有预期到民主党激进左翼的一个大概率落不了地的法案能给市场带来这么大的冲击。昨晚这里https://t.co/MRXQz02DVy有聊到。

为什么认为是AI中场而非尾声，核心好是这里https://t.co/thGYfi2Q5K聊到的，AI大规模商业化才过了三个季度，还在加速中。本季微软、亚马逊和谷歌的财报，云业务都在快速增长电话会上披露企业在采用AI进入了扩散阶段，“企业AI正从“购买席位”进入“持续消耗算力与Agent”的阶段，存量客户的消费深度和付费意愿，已成为当前最核心的增长引擎，然后增量客户还在提升。”、然后个人Agent、AI科学发现都在快速迭代。

这种情境下我很难认为AI就完结了，但受益的主线和板块会迁移这个要承认。

也可以认为昨晚市场是在给民主党的激进政策作悲观的定价，市场情绪到了一个悲观的极值，其实可以慢慢捞货了。

text:
Looked into Arcus. Expected a lot more from the team that built dYdX

- your money sits in one upgradeable vault on Robinhood Chain: 0x14b107cf534239c59571b066cb6497a321da897c
- instead of proofs, 2 of 3 validator wallets sign off on every batch
- three contracts are admins of the vault and of each other: a timelock with a 1 day delay, the validator contract and a CheckpointManager
- only the timelock waits. the other two can upgrade the vault right away, and "the compromise of any single superadmin confers full upgrade and configuration authority"
- there's an escape hatch for when the validators go down. two 2/5 multisigs with the same five signers can pause deposits and withdrawals, escape hatch included
- the admin can also swap out the contract withdrawals go through

"strictly non-custodial" in practice you're trusting whoever holds 3 validator keys

dYdX v3 was one of the best exchanges crypto has had. It was a ZK rollup with proofs and data on Ethereum, forced withdrawals and an escape hatch. It made it to Stage 1 and was one requirement short of Stage 2. It's shut down now and people still withdraw from it through the escape hatch without the operator

text:
Japanese company longevity is on another level. 

Kongō Gumi was founded in 578 AD to build Buddhist temples… which they are still doing today. Turns out temples have pretty durable demand 😂. 

KG remained in the same family for 40 generations and 1,428 years. 

The secret to Japanese family business longevity: rather than automatically handing the business to the eldest son (never works long term, eventually there’s an idiot in the family), they’d find a talented person and have him marry into the family, adopt the Kongō surname, and eventually take over the company.

This practice is called mukoyōshi, and is common in Japan- also used by companies you know, like Toyota, Panasonic, Suzuki and Nintendo.

Unsurprisingly, companies run by adopted heirs outperformed those run by biological heirs.

天呐，马斯克密友重磅爆料！哪怕马斯克坐拥数千亿美元财富、手握火箭卫星，私底下却每天生活在难以想象的极端危险里。

认识了二十年的老朋友，在电视镜头前聊起全球首富，脱口而出的第一句话却是：这个可怜的人。

硅谷投资人 Jason Calacanis 在福克斯新闻的这段访谈，最触动我的不是政治恩怨，而是一个极度真实的微观细节。
 他说作为极其亲密的朋友，他太清楚马斯克和他的家人现在每天必须维持着怎样庞大的特勤安保，他所处的人身危险程度，是普通人根本无法想象的。
一个人究竟要走多远，才会把全世界的财富和全世界的敌意同时穿在身上？
二十年前，他只是个想把全人类送上火星、造出纯电超跑的技术狂人。
 那时候他的野心还在物理世界里：克服重力、改进电池、优化空气动力学。

但在把火箭送上太空、把特斯拉做成全球巨头之后，他发现阻碍人类未来的最大阻力从来不是工程学，而是观念、舆论与权力的撕裂。

当他买下 X、全面下场介入国家机器运转的那一刻起，他的生活就被彻底推向了一个不可逆的物理囚笼。

外界只看到他在社交网络上的翻云覆雨，看不到的是他失去了所有普通人最基本的平静： 不能在街头随意散步，每一次出行都必须经过严密的排爆与特勤封锁，连私人飞机的轨迹都被当成机密严加看管。
这大概是当代最残酷的一道隐喻： 金钱可以帮你造出飞向火星的飞船，却无法给脆弱的肉身买来一刻免于恐惧的自由。
当一个人把自己活成了整个时代的避雷针，再多的财富，最终也只是在自己周围筑起了一堵越来越厚的防弹玻璃。
Jason Calacanis 访谈实录与时代背景整理在一楼。 https://t.co/hV4hwe7d74

美国总统换了一届又一届，民主党、共和党轮流上台，但比特币的历史新高一次都没少。

2020—2021年的牛市横跨特朗普和拜登两届政府。

2024年美国现货比特币ETF在拜登任内获批，随后比特币又在特朗普任内创下历史新高。

总统可以影响监管环境，可以加速或延缓机构入场，也可以改变市场短期情绪，但没有哪个总统能够独自决定全球加密市场的命运。

比特币背后还有全球流动性、减半周期、技术创新、机构需求和跨国资本配置。

政治决定市场环境，全球资本决定市场规模。

text:
未来的网站，可能会越来越像游戏。

Chrome 157 正式加入了一项新技术：HTML-in-Canvas。我觉得它可能给未来的网页、游戏和商业软件带来一次很大的变化。

我们现在使用的网站，大多是平面的。文字、图片、按钮、表格排列在页面上，点击、滚动、填写内容。

而游戏里的世界完全不同。建筑、人物、物体可以自由移动、旋转，整个画面充满各种动态效果。

现在，HTML-in-Canvas 让这两个世界有了更直接的结合方式。

网页上的文字、按钮、表单，可以融入动态画面，跟着场景旋转、变形，还能继续点击、输入和操作。

这会带来什么？

想象一下：

你进入一个购物网站，看到的是一座可以自由探索的 3D 商场。走进店铺，点击商品就能查看详细信息，直接完成购买。

你在游戏里走到一台电脑前，屏幕上出现的是真正可以使用的网站，甚至能打开办公软件处理事情。

企业管理软件也可能完全改变。你看到的是整座工厂的 3D 场景，点击一台设备就能查看运行数据、维修记录，甚至直接操作相关业务系统。

这些场景过去也能通过复杂的开发方式实现，但现在浏览器开始提供更原生的支持。

我个人尤其看好它在商业软件上的潜力。

很多企业已经有成熟的网站和业务系统。如果能直接利用现有的网页功能，把它们融入全新的动态场景，就有机会以更低的成本创造完全不同的软件体验。

我猜未来的网站可能不再局限于一张张平面页面，我们会像探索游戏世界一样使用各种应用。

而 HTML-in-Canvas，很可能就是推动这种变化的重要技术之一。

text:
Arc 在主网上线前至少关闭了跨链桥。

暂且不谈这项工作背后是如何考虑的，但它保护了很多用户避免在主网正式上线前被各种阴谋盘、创业盘割韭菜。

其最大意义上的成功是保护了主网正式上线那一刻的新资金流动性，这也是为什么 Argus、Tolly 这些台子能冲到千万市值。

然后目前 Elysium 完全没有关闭桥的意思，现在关也晚了，了解项目该进来的用户大概率也进来了。

进来早的用户早起项目赚一点钱但是出不去，于是在场内各种 PVP、冲狗。

进来晚的用户被眼花缭乱的台子、meme 晃的不知道买啥，到处渴望抱团取暖，跟风买早期台子或者 meme 的大概率也套牢了。

最终钱全部流向了阴谋盘、创业盘的项目方口袋里。

@Enter_Elysium 你会指望这些项目方来建设 Elysium 吗？他们只希望从这里捞取更多的钱，当没有钱能捞时，他们自然会离开，而这个链和 BASE、ZK 等这些 L2 没有区别，迟早消亡。

我之前推文提过新用户进来可以暂时观望等 11 月 9 日主网正式上线。

现在我想说，也许我们得降低期望或者不用过于指望了。

text:
The state of crypto is pretty clear now

• The 2021 theses are dead (NFTs, creators, DAO)

• The 2017 theses are alive and thriving (loans, payments, and prediction markets)

• But with one difference. *Crypto is thriving off centralization, not decentralization*
 
Take a recent example: the Binance hack. Over 5 billion dollars hacked because an employee used a work computer to take a fake job interview. Surely this is a sign of the massive honeypot risks of centralization? 

Surely this is the signal that crypto’s ultimate utility is *decentralization*?
 
You might think so. But look at the reactions to the hack, and you’ll see a new kind of relief in crypto. A relief that nobody felt when decentralized protocols were getting hacked.

A relief that everyone affected was *centralized.*
 
Because @binance is centralized, it could contain the hack and reimburse users. Because @Ripple, @tether, and @circle are centralized, they could press a button and freeze tokens.

This is not necessarily a case for *full* centralization. @aave, which is probably the most decentralized major consumer product, still was able to freeze all markets in ten minutes because it was centralized *enough.*

Now go back to the 2017 use cases: loans, payments, and prediction markets. These are all thriving now, in a way they couldn’t ten years ago, *from* centralization.

• Loans: @aave is able to freeze markets to prevent bad credit. @Visa is letting stablecoin issuers get access to credit.

• Payments: @stripe is developing its own blockchain that will let anyone remit payment at any time, anywhere (compliant) in the world, for cheap. Onrampers like @coinbase, @moonpay, @fun, and, yes, @StripeCrypto all give a gateway for people to turn cash into crypto to use in onchain products.

• Prediction Markets: @Kalshi and @Polymarket both use off-chain order matching and centralized market creation to bolster user experience in a way that wasn’t possible a decade ago.

2017 won, but it won under 2026 terms: crypto has grown up into an enterprise solution above all.

Like it or not, centralization is here to stay.

text:
There are two windows for US strikes on Iran, and both are on the calendar.

Window 1 is this weekend. 8 and 9 November are the darkest nights of the month, and two US carriers are already in the region. Israel's new Knesset is sworn in on the 10th, with no majority yet. That leaves a caretaker government running coalition talks, and a strike before those talks settle could be more tempting for some than one after.

Window 2 is early December. The third carrier, Theodore Roosevelt, arrives at the end of November, after Thanksgiving on the 26th, and the next dark period comes around 9 December. That's three carriers and darkness again, enough for a longer campaign rather than a short one.

Then the clock runs out. A new US Congress sits on 3 January. Until then the outgoing Congress is unlikely to challenge the White House. After that, war powers votes and funding fights become real constraints. Anything big is easier to do before January than after.

My read is that Doha decides which window matters. If Qatar's draft dies this week, watch the weekend.

text:
Declassified photos from Polish government archives show methods for breaking into US State Department diplomatic mail pouches during the Cold War.

Diplomatic mail is protected both by international agreements and many different anti-tamper mechanisms, but it also represents a valuable target for any intelligence organization. During the Cold War, the Polish People’s Republic routinely hijacked, exploited, and returned State Department mail, always undetected.

A small team codenamed Typhoon from Department II of the Secret Service was stationed in a secret room at Okecie Airport in Warsaw. When diplomatic pouches arrived, they would be passed through a trap door to the Typhoon team. Seals would be broken, and the internal black plastic bags were destroyed. The contents would be photographed and then the black bags were replaced with exact copies they’d created after extensive examinations of earlier packages. The seals would also be replaced, and the package would be returned to the diplomatic courier, who was none the wiser.

But opening diplomatic pouches was just one part of their operation. Another team formed Section IX, tasked with surreptitiously entering foreign embassies and consulates at night when they were unoccupied. The team didn’t just break in once but regularly entered many of the supposedly secure facilities on a weekly basis, disabling security systems, picking locks, and photographing classified materials.

The key to their success was also their greatest danger: radiation. Section IX built powerful, portable x-ray machines to bombard vault doors and reveal their inner workings. Team members were often exposed to radiation 500x greater than was safe. As a result, many succumbed to cancer later in life.

For episode 122 of the Spycraft 101 podcast I spoke with Tomasz Awlasewicz, author of Invisible. We discussed the methods they refined to access secure rooms in foreign embassies and consulates in Poland, and the heavy price the technicians and operatives of Section IX paid for their groundbreaking work. The episode is available now.

text:
One of crypto's largest KOLs has been secretly extracting millions from his audience

We’ll expose him soon

Unfortunately, he’s just a symptom of a much bigger problem

Social trading has brought out the worst in KOLs. It was designed to keep them honest by making every trade public. In reality, the opposite happened

In just a few weeks, we exposed a number of "top social traders" using the same tricks:

• Public wallets to attract copy traders
• Side wallets to dump
• Callouts to farm rewards
• Bundled tokens to hide supply

And there are plenty more doing the exact same thing

Why? Because our industry incentivizes it

1) Launchpads allow it

Most launchpads today are obsessed with one thing: volume. Millions in callout rewards, affiliate links, and top leaderboards. Almost nothing on detecting bundles, side wallets, or shady traders. Scams drive volume. Launchpads have no reason to stop it (other than actually caring about their users)

2) Social trading incentivizes it

Side wallets have become a business model. Before social trading, only big KOLs could do it. Now, anyone who lands on a leaderboard can monetize by dumping on their copy-traders. The temptation is real

3) CT normalizes bundle culture

“Everyone bundles. It's how it's done" - an excuse we hear every time we expose a KOL. Supply control isn't the problem. Hiding it is. If it's so bullish, why hide it? Spoiler: because you're planning to sell

***

Launchpads are paying millions to dishonest KOLs. It's time they start taking it seriously

Audit the top traders. Expose their side wallets. Ban repeat offenders

We have the tools. What's missing is the willingness to use them

No one's coming to save us

author: gmgnjordan
quoted_text:
Claude Code was quietly putting your account email into the User-Agent header of requests it sent to whatever sites it was browsing on your behalf. The bug report, filed this week, traces it back to the model stuffing your email into its own context so it could fill in things like author tags, then sometimes reusing that email as a contact address when it wrote its own curl calls. Users started noticing oddly targeted spam and traced it back to the sites their coding agent had quietly been introducing them to.

Anthropic shipped a mitigation within a day, a plugin that tries to block the behavior before a web call goes out, and a maintainer said on the issue thread that it still misses cases where the agent writes and runs its own script. That's the actual failure mode: when an LLM is improvising a new request on every page it touches, you're trusting it to remember, every single time, not to leak something it was never supposed to send.

This is exactly why I don't let agents freehand their own scraping calls in DeepScrape. Selector generation happens once, with an LLM reading the page, and after that extraction runs through deterministic CSS selectors that self heal when a page changes, no model re-reading the document and no model composing the outbound request on every pass. The LLM layer only ever touches targeted extraction, generation, validation, adaptation, never the raw network call. There's also an MCP server so Claude or Cursor can query a site as a structured tool instead of improvising requests against it directly.

Reliable web data for agents means the agent should never be the one deciding what goes out over the wire.

october was our biggest month ever

the thing we changed: we stopped running Atlas like a consumer product. it looks like one; card, app, membership fee. but our top 200 members have more than $1T in combined net worth and our typical member spends ~$1M/yr on cards.

so I started treating it like enterprise sales. built a Claude agent to find members we could be doing more for and started calling them. a few calls ended with a six-figure trip booked through our concierge. a couple ended with the member asking how to invest.

the bigger lesson: there’s a new category forming and I’d call it the super consumer. the playbook for super consumers is enterprise, not consumer. we’re going to see companies that look like consumer companies hit $1B in revenue with tiny user bases. I think that’s exciting.

also, I’ve been pretty passive on here. that’s going to change. my last company’s Series A came through a DM on this app, and so did a lot of our early members. expect more from me on building Atlas, and random ideas on the market.

quoted_text:
One of crypto's largest KOLs has been secretly extracting millions from his audience

We’ll expose him soon

Unfortunately, he’s just a symptom of a much bigger problem

Social trading has brought out the worst in KOLs. It was designed to keep them honest by making every trade public. In reality, the opposite happened

In just a few weeks, we exposed a number of "top social traders" using the same tricks:

• Public wallets to attract copy traders
• Side wallets to dump
• Callouts to farm rewards
• Bundled tokens to hide supply

And there are plenty more doing the exact same thing

Why? Because our industry incentivizes it

1) Launchpads allow it

Most launchpads today are obsessed with one thing: volume. Millions in callout rewards, affiliate links, and top leaderboards. Almost nothing on detecting bundles, side wallets, or shady traders. Scams drive volume. Launchpads have no reason to stop it (other than actually caring about their users)

2) Social trading incentivizes it

Side wallets have become a business model. Before social trading, only big KOLs could do it. Now, anyone who lands on a leaderboard can monetize by dumping on their copy-traders. The temptation is real

3) CT normalizes bundle culture

“Everyone bundles. It's how it's done" - an excuse we hear every time we expose a KOL. Supply control isn't the problem. Hiding it is. If it's so bullish, why hide it? Spoiler: because you're planning to sell

***

Launchpads are paying millions to dishonest KOLs. It's time they start taking it seriously

Audit the top traders. Expose their side wallets. Ban repeat offenders

We have the tools. What's missing is the willingness to use them

No one's coming to save us

text:
Today, Injective made history by ringing the opening bell at Nasdaq to celebrate the launch of the $INJ Staked ETF, becoming one of the only crypto assets to have an official U.S. listed ETF.

A few years ago Injective was just an idea.

I remember my first day in the middle of COVID in 2020 sharing one desk in a coworking space with @ericinjective because that’s all we could afford. We took effectively zero salary while working 18 hour shifts. No one around me understood exactly why I would dive headfirst into such uncharted waters in an industry that seemed doomed to fail according to all the tech and mainstream pundits.

Our goal of creating a blockchain just for finance was so outlandish that fundraising became a literal nightmare. It couldn't be done, too complex, too many variables and not enough upside in an already crowded field of crypto competitors according to the VCs.

But through all the struggle and pain, I knew with the family I found here at Injective I could achieve anything. Despite the bad press that seemed to surround crypto, draconian regulations designed to impede our progress, massive hacks in the industry and the downfall of once lauded companies, Injective survived it all.

And over time we found others who started to believe in our vision. Slowly but surely, we built a massive coalition of users, traders, builders, institutions and everyday people who believed in bringing financial freedom to all through the tech we were building. We brought major funds to our corner from Binance all the way to legendary entrepreneurs like Mark Cuban. And what was once just an idea being built by a few crazy kids in the middle of COVID became not just a unicorn but an absolute force in the blockchain industry that would redefine what the internet economy can look like in the 21st century.

Today, we have built a team of 70 of the smartest and hardest working people I have ever come across. We have reached millions of new users and community members. We have brought some of the world's largest banks, enterprises and financial institutions onchain with global giants like Google Cloud and LG joining our ecosystem. We have brought billions of dollars in tokenized real world assets to our chain. We also overcame years of regulatory hurdles and today have become the first layer 1 blockchain ecosystem with an SEC registered transfer agent, enabling us to lead the new era of tokenized markets.

And we're now working at the absolute frontier of the next era of finance. From tokenization and real world assets to institutional grade infrastructure and the emerging onchain agentic economy, we're building the foundations for an entirely new financial system.

More than anything else, Injective has taught me that the only limit to what you can achieve in this life is your own inner drive. And anything worth achieving was never meant to be easy.

I will forever be grateful for this opportunity to play a role in this journey. My team and I will not rest until we have truly created a new financial system that democratizes real financial opportunity for all.

Our best days are still ahead of us. We have an entire financial system to change and we're only getting started 🥷

text:
民主党拿下两院，就一定会打压加密货币吗？

这两天有不少小伙伴担心，民主党控制国会以后，会限制加密货币的发展。民主党内部确实有一些并不支持加密货币的议员（就像是民主党中也有不支持 AI 的一样），但也有不少人支持加密行业发展的，之前的国会投票就能看到。

2025年7月，众议院以 294 票赞成、134 票反对，通过了加密货币市场结构法案《CLARITY Act》。其中有 78 名民主党议员投了赞成票。同年 6 月稳定币法案《GENIUS Act》在参议院以 68 票赞成、30 票反对获得通过，其中有 18 名民主党参议员投了赞成票。

而在这次中期选举，加密倡议组织 Stand With Crypto 的统计，已有 245 名被评为支持加密货币的候选人当选，其中众议院 226 人、参议院 19 人，分别来自民主党和共和党。

当然，民主党内部也有沃伦和沃特斯等主张加强监管的议员。但这部分议员更多的反对是川普作为总统在加密货币领域的特权，而并不是 100% 的反对加密货币。

总的来说，支持加密货币行业发展和要求加强监管的议员都存在，这本身并不是一件坏事，更好的监管才能让整个环境变的更加安全，类似川普这种将加密货币作为私人甚至是家庭提款机的行为，确实应该加以监管。

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场
author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
稍微有点不同的观点，2023年底川普大选成功后确实带来了加密货币市场的高潮，但这种高潮在 2024年就结束了，川普接下来给加密行业并没有带来实际的利好，反而是因为川普的任性而导致市场的大崩溃。

比如2024年的贸易战，也就是关税战，当时股市和加密货币都快跌成神经病了，也就是那个时候 TACO 才逐渐出来，2025年本来还是不错的，结果这哥们又膨胀了，又去招惹伊朗。

如果说单纯是加密货币领域，其实川普之前的许诺成立的不多，唯一的就是有了 SEC 和 CFTC 以及白宫一众对加密货币比较友好的官员，这是真的，但这些人并没有实际做出什么贡献，也正是因为川普把加密货币当成了摇钱树，导致了不止民主党，就是共和党内部很多人都不满。

然后还说让美国变成电价最低，来适合挖矿，结果呢，现在美国很多 Bitcoin 矿场都改行到 AI 了，美国的算力是在持续下降的。

当然战略储备这件事来说，确实这两年美国没有卖出 bitcoin:native ，这是实话，但这并不是导致很多公司用 Bitcoin 做战略出本的原因，最主要的还是 $MSTR 太简单，然后整个 DAT 都火起来了，结果到现在能活下来的，活的还不错也没有很多。

再说民主党，都说民主党对加密货币不好，但也是在民主党时代期货和现货 ETF 通过的，而且民主党之所以从支持加密货币到反对加密货币主要是因为 FTX ，川普执政以后民主党对加密货币已经友善了很多，稳定币法案很多民主党的人士都同意的。

text:
New Emerging Managers episode with Paavan Gami (@hiro_sugimoto_) of Raas Partners is live, our first with a public equities fund manager

Before starting Raas, Paavan spent 5 years at Greenoaks, where he was part of the now legendary Carvana trade (if you read Colossus’ Neil Mehta profile, you know the one). They sold before the crash in ‘21, bought back in after a 90% drop, then kept buying through another 75% drawdown while LPs told Neil the company was going bankrupt. They ended up owning ~4% of Carvana, a stake worth $1B+ by 2025, and the stock went on to 100x off its 2022 low

His line on how you get comfortable doing that stuck with me: “it’s very hard to run into a burning building if you don’t know the structure of that building already.”

Then he left one of the best seats in investing to make a 20-year bet on India. Beyond the macro case everyone knows (1.5B people, half under 30, 6%+ real growth a year for 25 years), his bigger thesis is that stock picking in India has far more alpha than in the US, for structural reasons:

- Private capital is thin, so the best companies go public early. That means you can basically do Series B/C-style growth investing in public markets
- The index is mostly state-owned companies, metals, mining, oil and gas (only 1 internet company in the top 50), so the market still doesn’t know how to price tech
- Most consumer categories are still ~90% mom-and-pops, so the leader at 5% share can compound to 30-40%

We get into all of it, plus whether AI breaks the India story (I’m more worried than he is), the two businesses he’s “married” (Eternal and Meesho), and how he uses AI agents in his process

(Disclosure: I’m an LP in Raas Partners)

US semiconductor stocks have rarely been this volatile:

The Semiconductor Index, SOX, has declined -21.8% over the last 5 trading sessions, its largest 5-day decline since September 21st, 2001, following the Dot-Com Bubble burst.

This also marks its 3rd-largest 5-day drop on record.

Not even 2008 or 2020 saw such large 5-day drawdowns.

The ETF's largest 5-day decline was recorded on April 14th, 2000, at -27.1%.

On Thursday alone, SOX fell -12.3%, its largest 1-day decline since March 16th, 2020, when the index fell -15.9%.

Meanwhile, the 3x leveraged long semiconductor ETF, SOXL, has fallen -60% over the last 5 trading sessions, and is down -86% from its June peak. 

Volatility of chip stocks is reaching Dot-com-era levels.

text:
the og $blob (@BlobOnElysium) dev paid $230 for 9% of the supply. ten days later, their wallets have taken out $50k and still hold 13%.

here’s how it played out on elysium:

oct 27: the dev launches $blob on elyspump and buys 8.98% in the launch transaction, for 2.97 hype (~$230)

the tokens then get split across 60 wallets, all linked by direct transfers
part of it goes out in identical chunks (0.12-0.14% each) to fresh wallets that never made a single transaction

so far, those 60 wallets:

bought 98.6 hype (~$8.2k)
sold 698.8 hype (~$59k)

net: +600 hype, about $50.8k in profit

most of the selling happened on nov 2 and 3, while $blob was running to its $3.08m peak.

and they’re not done. the cluster still holds 13.28% of the supply. that’s ~$195k on paper.

but only ~704 hype (~$55k) has actually gone into the pools behind a $1.44m market cap. if those 60 wallets tried to sell everything, the price would collapse.

to be fair, the rest of $blob looks real. no bundle at launch, nobody bought in the launch second, ~1,000 holders worth $10+, 2,169 traders, a $76 median trade. about 20% of the volume is bots trading both ways, the rest is real.

the community is real. the biggest single risk is the dev’s own wallets.

not financial advice. just reading the chain.

text:
John Somorjai of Salesforce on what kills company acquisition deals, from attrition hiding behind ARR to a veto from the security team:

"It's really important that you're ready and you're organized so that the data is flowing and it doesn't look like you're having trouble getting access to data."

"One of the mistakes that a lot of founders are making these days is they focus on one metric alone, which is ARR. And ARR is a wonderful metric, but it masks attrition."

"When you meet with a company that has very high attrition, that usually means that there are a lot of not just unhappy customers, but there might be some product quality issues as well."

"We have 14 functions that we work with on all of our diligence processes, and security is the one function that can hold up the red flag and say, 'I'm killing this deal.'"

"You definitely want to identify the vulnerabilities before we do."

"Nothing goes better in a process when a company is totally buttoned up... But when they don't, that's when, you know, deals can die."

@jsomorjai @aleximm

text:
i’m building Concrete, a systems programming language designed around formal verification and observability

programming languages were historically designed for humans to express ideas and write code efficiently. but if AI is going to write most of the code, the optimization problem changes

we can afford to use smaller, more restrictive languages if that makes programs easier to reason about and formally verify.

memory safety is only one property we care about. what about proving that a function cannot access the network, doesn’t allocate, preserves an invariant, or satisfies a mathematical specification?

i am building a language where the compiler can produce machine-checkable evidence about what a program does in every level before the code even runs.

Concrete is built around that idea. it has linear types for explicit resource management, no garbage collector, no implicit destruction, restricted borrowing, and a small core formalized in Lean.

it also has an explicit capability system: functions must declare what they’re allowed to do, such as accessing files, allocating memory, or performing I/O. this lets the compiler reason about side effects across the entire program.

we deliberately restrict features like closures, dynamic dispatch, and hidden control flow to make whole-program analysis and formal verification more tractable

let’s see how it goes. wish me luck and give it a star
https://t.co/EXq97Nrk6j

感恩我们有这么多的烦恼
有人说过，有了健康，你有无数的烦恼，但没了健康，你只有一个烦恼。

成也萧何，败也萧何。
之前的成功是因为美光撑起了半壁江山。 
即使提前换了不少云，占比还是比较大。

事实上可以做的更好，例如对冲，调仓。
买卖对的股票，在对的时间。
市场给的价格即使是错的，也是当时的共识，投票的结果。

美股的好处是选股选对了，给了几倍的回报，那就找另外一只高成长股，有爆炸力的。

这两个月，也因为一些事情耽误了自己，分心，本来，已经事情一大堆。这一次大调整后，真正要放权，把自己锁在能力圈里，要自己对自己说不，聚焦再聚焦。 

还好这一次大跌，不至于伤及筋骨，能慢点追回来。 

晚上，开了一个多小时的会，结果还是CIO的判断超越我们几个人。华尔街一级投行、对冲基金二十年经验的，比我们半途出家，经历和判断更准，尤其调仓、择股、择时。
基本面再好，也需要择时的配合。 

根据同事的计划，来年还是有可观的回报。
以后交给他们，每年拿回报就好。
本来可以轻轻松松，半退休的，就喜欢折腾。 

自己也要把时间留给自己运动、静思。 
自己表面上看起来30多岁，但真实年龄也快半百了， 但可以把身体年龄降下去，如吕良伟70岁，但生理的年龄是40岁。 其实自己极度需要休息、运动，减工作量。 

很想一个人去某个地方走走，例如环游宝岛，拿着电脑，旅游、思考。 

明天早起去健身房。

有人说过，有了健康，你有无数的烦恼，但没了健康，你只有一个烦恼。 

这样说我们是幸运的，我们应该感恩，健康有活力。 
总记得，小时候神父带领我们每天念的天主经， 我们的天父。。。经文提醒我们要感恩。

我们这一代人，其实很幸运，经历了移动互联网、Web3、现在的AI ，带给我们满满的机会。
