THE 15% BAND

Look at this chart. 
59 races. Senate and governor. 
States ordered from reddest to bluest in 2024.

The solid lines are 2024. 
The dashed lines are 2026. 
The shaded bands are what moved.

One formula fits all of it:
Republican 2026 = 0.85 × Trump 2024
Democrat 2026 = Harris 2024 + 0.15 × Trump 2024

For every 1,000 Trump points, 850 stayed Republican. 150 landed on the Democratic side.

The numbers:
Senate: Republicans kept ~85% of Trump’s share
Governor: ~86%

Variation explained: 88%

What makes it strange:
It didn’t matter how red the state was. Wyoming, Ohio, Illinois, Massachusetts: same 15% (p = 0.69). The Democratic gain was sized by Trump’s vote, not Harris’s. The Harris part is zero.

The 0.85 beat both standard election-swing models in every set of races.
Drop any single state and the multiplier stays between 0.846 and 0.853.

Why seats flipped:
At 0.85, any state where Trump got under about 58.5% falls below 50%. Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, South Carolina, North Carolina: all under that line. All flipped.

What this means:
Midterms are messy. This one isn’t. Two sets of races, different candidates, different campaigns, and the same 15% decrease almost everywhere.

A pattern this even demands answers at the ballot level: paper ballot hand counts, poll-book check-ins against votes counted, and voter files showing who actually turned out. 

The numbers raise the question. 
The ballots can answer it.

# Delegation Guard

Do the task with the fewest agents it actually needs. One is the default.

## Before you delegate
- Read the task and the code it touches directly. Decide whether one agent in one pass can finish it. Most can.
- If the task is small, a typo, a rename, a single-file edit, do it yourself. Don't spawn anything.
- When it's genuinely big, state the split first:
  - Agents: how many, and why that many
  - Owns: the one job each agent holds
  - Boundary: the files each may touch, with no overlap
  - Returns: what each one hands back to you
- Split only into parts that can run at the same time without waiting on each other.

## While the team runs
- Give each agent one job and only the context that job needs.
- Put the plan in a file. Every agent reads it before it starts and before it reports.
- Reading agents, search, logs, docs, run on a cheaper model. Keep the top model for real edits.
- One owner per area. Don't let two agents edit the same files.
- If the plan changes, stop the agents on the old one first, then brief them on the new one.
- Stop any agent the moment its job is done. Nothing idles in the background.

## Pause and confirm
Reading and exploring is always fine. Unless the task already cleared it, get my OK before you:
- Spawn more than three agents at once
- Add an agent whose job overlaps one already running
- Give an agent the power to push, deploy, or touch production
- Let two agents write to the same files in parallel
- Keep a team running on a job one agent could finish

## Checking the work
- Don't trust an agent's report. Rerun the test or build it claims passed.
- Read each agent's output yourself, not just its summary.
- When two agents disagree, settle it by running the thing, not by averaging them.
- An agent that reports done with no proof has not finished.
- Before you tell me it's done, list what each agent did and how you confirmed it.

## If the team grows
The moment the work needs more agents than you planned, stop and tell me what you found and why. Don't quietly add agents to fill the gap.

text:
ai agents didn't escape human bureaucracy. they rediscovered it.

yc dropped 50 gpt-6.1 sol agents into minecraft with one job: build a civilization.

for a few minutes it worked. trees cleared, plan written, shelter going up.

then night one: 22 deaths. they respawned and only lost gear, but the colony never got its nerve back.

over the run: a freeze order, a ration ledger, a "sole fertilizer operator" for one wheat block, and agents asking permission to remove grass. bureaucracy, with nobody told to build it.

--

anthropic found that smarter agents don't automatically make better teams.

give agents the same model and similar context, and they can all make the same bad call. in other tests, one agent had information that could change the group's answer, but it never made it into the decision.

they also tested the obvious fix: assign jobs, name a ceo, tell everyone who reports to whom.

it barely helped. older models produced conflicting work that never came together. some stronger models avoided conflicts by keeping their work separate.

--

we hoped agents would solve the bottlenecks our organizations create. instead, we taught them to think like us, and they're rebuilding the same bureaucracy: rules, paperwork, and approvals.

i guess skynet is pending approval.

Social trading has brought out the worst in KOLs. It was designed to keep them honest by making every trade public. In reality, the opposite happened

• Public wallets to attract copy traders
• Side wallets to dump
• Callouts to farm rewards
• Bundled tokens to hide supply

And there are plenty more doing the exact same thing

Why? Because our industry incentivizes it

1) Launchpads allow it

Most launchpads today are obsessed with one thing: volume. Millions in callout rewards, affiliate links, and top leaderboards. Almost nothing on detecting bundles, side wallets, or shady traders. Scams drive volume. Launchpads have no reason to stop it (other than actually caring about their users)

2) Social trading incentivizes it

Side wallets have become a business model. Before social trading, only big KOLs could do it. Now, anyone who lands on a leaderboard can monetize by dumping on their copy-traders. The temptation is real

3) CT normalizes bundle culture

“Everyone bundles. It's how it's done" - an excuse we hear every time we expose a KOL. Supply control isn't the problem. Hiding it is. If it's so bullish, why hide it? Spoiler: because you're planning to sell

Launchpads are paying millions to dishonest KOLs. It's time they start taking it seriously

Audit the top traders. Expose their side wallets. Ban repeat offenders

text:
It's pretty clear at this point that the cost of attack is trending to 0. But this doesn't mean CISO budgets will 100x, and that's ok.

I'd argue we're going through a temporary phenomenon of 12-18mos, where legacy codebases are hyperexposed to agent attacks.

Agents also speed up code migration - rewriting a C/JS codebase to TypeScript/Rust is easier than ever before. 

The new paradigm of an "antifragile internet" will likely see much faster adoption of more verifiable code and infra that *eliminates* entire classes of bugs (eg. memory/type issues) and folded into an agentic dev pipeline.

That's the light at the end of the tunnel

text:
有朋友问，为什么Cybertruck停产了？

虽然这也是很多人之前预测过的，不过暂时还没停。今天11月6日，Musk在X上法文说，Tesla会在明年年中前后，逐步结束得州超级工厂的Cybertruck生产，给Cybercab自动驾驶出租车腾出产能。他还说，Cybertruck是“Tesla造过的最好的车”。

那既然是最好的车，为什么要收摊呢？我们先看看数字，就容易明白了。上市前，Musk预计它一年能卖二十五万辆。按Kelley Blue Book的估算，2024年在美国卖了约三万九千辆，2025年就只剩两万出头了，跌了将近一半。到今年第三季度，包括Cybertruck在内的“其他车型”一共交付了八千多辆，不到Tesla总交付量的百分之二。2019年发布时，它说起价三万九千九百美元，现在官网上的两个版本，是七万四千九百九十和八万四千九百九十美元。规划和现实之间，差的不是一点，是一个数量级。

其实问题不在它不够酷。Cybertruck的棱角和不锈钢车身，几乎没有人会认错，话题也从来不缺热度。可让很多人说一句“这车真酷”，和让很多人掏七八万美元，把它当成每天拉货、接孩子的车，不是一回事。买皮卡的人，看的是能拉多少、能拖多少、好不好修、贵不贵。它最独特的地方，恰恰也是它最贵的地方，不锈钢的车身和专用零件，没法跟别的车型分摊成本，卖得越少，摊得越贵，越贵，又卖得越少。至于Musk的政治立场赶走了多少买家，这几年大概有影响，当然没人能拆出准数，不能把账全算在这上面。

那腾出来的地方，给了一个更确定的东西吗？也没有。Cybercab没有方向盘，也没有踏板，监管部门正在追问，Tesla是怎么自己认证这样一辆车的；公司的首席财务官上个月也承认，它的运营成本还高于目标。这不是把一个失败的生意换成一个成功的生意，是收起一个已经被市场检验过的押注，换一个更大、也更不确定的押注。

写太空散热那篇我说，能不能做，是工程师的题，该不该做，是所有人的题。Cybertruck把这件事演得很清楚。工程师确实做出了别人不敢做的东西，Musk可以真心觉得它是最好的车，可买车的人，仍然可以不买。前者是造的人的判断，后者是用的人的选择，用的人没有义务替一个愿景买单，他们不买，也不是不懂欣赏。

我更想替普通消费者追问的，是以后怎么办？路透社提到，得州这座工厂，是已知唯一一座能生产Cybertruck专用零件的Tesla工厂。那么明年年中以后，已经买了它的几万车主，不锈钢的车门、车身板坏了，零件由谁来做，能修到哪一年？二手车还值多少钱，保险会不会跟着变？到我写的时候，我没查到Tesla就零件、维修和保修发过正式说明。还有生产线上的工人，他们会被调到Cybercab，还是另作安排，也没人说。

一辆车卖不动，收摊不稀奇。稀奇的是，收摊的消息里，说得最清楚的，是要给谁腾地方；说得最少的，是已经买了它的人怎么办。

text:
This is crazy. Someone is willing to pay me $390 to agree to buy $NVDA at $150, about 20% below where it trades today.

It's called a cash-secured put, and here's how it works:

Nvidia is trading around $188. You sell the $150 put expiring January 15, 2027 and collect $3.90 per share, or $390 for one contract.

In exchange, you agree to buy 100 shares at $150 if NVDA closes below that price at expiration. You set aside $15,000 in cash to cover it, which is why it's called "cash-secured."

The buyer is paying for the right to sell you shares at $150. The $390 is yours to keep no matter what happens.

One of two things happens:

1. NVDA stays above $150 and the put expires worthless. You keep $390 on $15,000 of capital, a 2.6% return in 70 days, or about 13.6% annualized.

2. NVDA closes below $150 and you get assigned. You buy 100 shares at $150, but after the premium your real cost basis is $146.10, about 22% below today's price.

Nvidia reports earnings after the close on November 17, before this put expires, so a big move in either direction is on the table.

The risk is real. If NVDA fell to $130, you'd be down about $1,610 on paper. Someone who bought 100 shares today would be down about $5,850.

Not financial advice. I share these for education.

text:
I just returned from Marrakesh, Morocco, and to be completely honest, I am still at a loss for words. Diving headfirst into an entirely unknown culture and experiencing the profound warmth of its people was nothing short of incredible. I have always traveled a lot, but this specific trip shook something awake in me. It profoundly reshaped my view on what is truly important in life, making me realize with absolute clarity how vital it is to step outside our comfort zones and discover the world.
Travel is not just a leisure activity; it is a necessity. It gives us the rare, irreplaceable opportunity to deeply understand the world, come closer to human diversity, and acknowledge a beautiful truth: we all share this one planet, regardless of how or where we live.

We read books, watch documentaries, scroll through think-pieces, and look at photos of distant places. We think that by gathering data, we understand a culture.

But data is flat. It lacks a pulse.

You can read a hundred articles about North Africa, but you will never truly grasp the rhythm of life until you find yourself navigating the sensory symphony of a Moroccan souk, smelling the spices, hearing the call to prayer echo over the rooftops, and sharing a conversation over mint tea with a local vendor.
Travel provides an immersive, multi-sensory type of learning that books cannot replicate. It moves information from a theoretical concept in your head to a lived truth in your bones. More importantly, it is not just a goodway to learn about the diversity of our world; it is the only way to achieve a deep, genuine understanding of it.

And it absolutely forces self-discovery: When you strip away your usual routine, your favorite coffee shop, and the social safety nets of home, you are forced to figure out who you actually are. Travel show you the world;, but it also acts as a mirror, showing you your own boundaries, biases, and capacity for resilience.

And I truly urge everyone to reconsider their Investments!

We live in a culture obsessed with optimization, asset allocation, and building the perfect portfolio. We look for high-yield returns, invest in real estate, or swap our hard-earned capital for tangible signs of success. We buy the designer watch, the pristine tech, or the luxury bag.
But if the goal of life is to truly expand our minds and sharpen our emotional intelligence, we need to radically reconsider what we define as an "investment."
A luxury handbag like a Louis Vuitton is a depreciating asset. The moment you walk out of the boutique, its utility stays the same, and its thrill eventually fades into the background of your daily routine. It protects your belongings, but it doesn't protect your mind from narrowness.
A passport full of stamps, however, is a compounding asset. The lessons I just brought home from Marrakesh will pay dividends for the rest of my life. They change how I interact with strangers, how I solve problems, and how I practice gratitude.

Discovering the world is not a luxury meant for the end of life. It is an education that formats how you live it. And thus, I want to encourage everyone to take this seriously.

Challenge your spending habits. Look at your bank account and ask yourself what you are truly building. 
Before you invest in your next piece of designer luxury, consider investing in a plane ticket to a new place.
Step out of your comfort zone, embrace the beautiful diversity of our shared planet, and give yourself the only education that will never lose its value.
#Travel

text:
just wanted to clarify on this. Partitioned Binary Tree (PBT) helps with state expiry but that's not the intention when we (prev EF stateless team) designed it.

PBT is meant for partial stateful nodes. In other words, VOPS (https://t.co/MoO1uo4ZKl) nodes. The previous binary trie design (EIP-7864) has a flaw that nobody can independently download and verify a contract's storage because the keys are spread across the entire state trie.

PBT solves this by partitioning the trie into different key spaces (i.e. accounts, storage, code). Every contract would get its own subtrie too. Then nodes can just download and verify that subtrie.

But it has its own flaws. The trie depth for PBT is deeper than EIP-7864, which actually increases the proof size relatively (but still much less than MPT).

Back to the point of state expiry, the partitions do help state expiry (e.g. expire inactive contract subtrie), but state expiry has a whole other set of problems to solve.

quoted_text:
New Emerging Managers episode with Paavan Gami (@hiro_sugimoto_) of Raas Partners is live, our first with a public equities fund manager

Before starting Raas, Paavan spent 5 years at Greenoaks, where he was part of the now legendary Carvana trade (if you read Colossus’ Neil Mehta profile, you know the one). They sold before the crash in ‘21, bought back in after a 90% drop, then kept buying through another 75% drawdown while LPs told Neil the company was going bankrupt. They ended up owning ~4% of Carvana, a stake worth $1B+ by 2025, and the stock went on to 100x off its 2022 low

His line on how you get comfortable doing that stuck with me: “it’s very hard to run into a burning building if you don’t know the structure of that building already.”

Then he left one of the best seats in investing to make a 20-year bet on India. Beyond the macro case everyone knows (1.5B people, half under 30, 6%+ real growth a year for 25 years), his bigger thesis is that stock picking in India has far more alpha than in the US, for structural reasons:

- Private capital is thin, so the best companies go public early. That means you can basically do Series B/C-style growth investing in public markets
- The index is mostly state-owned companies, metals, mining, oil and gas (only 1 internet company in the top 50), so the market still doesn’t know how to price tech
- Most consumer categories are still ~90% mom-and-pops, so the leader at 5% share can compound to 30-40%

We get into all of it, plus whether AI breaks the India story (I’m more worried than he is), the two businesses he’s “married” (Eternal and Meesho), and how he uses AI agents in his process

(Disclosure: I’m an LP in Raas Partners)

text:
🌍 The ICMRA Summit 2026, held in Seoul on 3–6 November, brought together representatives of 44 regulatory authorities from around the world and the World Health Organization (WHO) to discuss the future of medicines regulation, technological innovation and patient access to safe and effective medicines.

The session “Patient-Focused Drug Development and Strengthening Regulatory Frameworks” was co-chaired by Prof. @EBalkowiecIskra, representing the Polish Office for Registration of Medicinal Products, Medical Devices and Biocidal Products (@URPLWMiPB), and Emer Cooke, Executive Director of the European Medicines Agency (@EMA_News). During the session, I delivered a presentation entitled “Patient Input in Drug Development and Regulatory Submissions: The EU Perspective and Opportunities for Collaboration”. I emphasised the importance of systematically incorporating patients’ perspectives throughout the lifecycle of a medicine, from scientific advice and clinical trials through marketing authorisation to pharmacovigilance and communication with patients.

The session “Global Trends and Practical Strategies for AI in Medicines Regulation” explored the growing role of AI in regulatory assessment and decision-making and how to use it responsibly, transparently and safely.

“Vitalizing NAMs & Establishing Next-Generation Regulatory Frameworks” focused on New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), including innovative approaches to safety assessment, ways to reduce animal testing, international regulatory harmonisation and collaboration among regulators, academia and industry.

Across all three sessions, international regulatory cooperation emerged as a common priority for advancing innovation, responding to new challenges and keeping patients’ needs central to medicines regulation.

text:
昨天美股为什么会出现如此猛烈的踩踏？除了 AI 监管和需求端的担忧，我觉得还有一个很重要的因素：华尔街 Pod Shop 的集体去杠杆

很多人可能不了解 Pod Shop 这种多经理对冲基金模式。像 Millennium、Citadel、Walleye 这类平台，旗下有大量独立交易团队（Pod），风控极其严格。一些团队回撤达到 5%，就可能被砍掉一半资金；达到 7.5%，甚至直接关停策略

这意味着什么？即使基金经理做了几个月的基本面研究，发现企业出货量、订单、营收都很好，但只要仓位触发风控，照样得卖。基本面没有变，卖出的理由却已经变了

更麻烦的是，这些基金往往使用相似的因子、持有高度重叠的股票，而且都有杠杆。当 AI、半导体等拥挤交易突然反转，A 基金被迫平仓，导致股价继续下跌，B 基金也触发止损，接着轮到 C、D……

这就是典型的机械性踩踏。这个时候，短期股价跟基本面可能已经没多大关系

author: LucaProsperi
quoted_text:
One of the challenges of the venture market today is that, for almost every net new opportunity, there are 30 competitors chasing it. Beyond taking on product-market fit and execution risk, these companies face immense competitive pressure. And given how quickly startups are raising capital, many of those competitors are also well-capitalized.

A zero-sum thinker might argue that the market is doing itself a disservice by funding a bunch of companies that will inevitably compete head-to-head, potentially eroding each other's margins and returns.

Alternatively, you could take a more abundance-oriented view. We're witnessing a fundamental shift in the world order. The TAM for these emerging businesses is enormous, to say the least, and there's plenty of room for AI-native companies to capture meaningful value.

One of the hard things, though, is that all the money in the system distorts things. A lot of traction might be coming from fundamentally unsustainable sources of money, meaning that what might look like PMF or strong margins is more the result of a short-term dislocation than a market steady state.

One of crypto's largest KOLs has been secretly extracting millions from his audience

We’ll expose him soon

Unfortunately, he’s just a symptom of a much bigger problem

Social trading has brought out the worst in KOLs. It was designed to keep them honest by making every trade public. In reality, the opposite happened

In just a few weeks, we exposed a number of "top social traders" using the same tricks:

• Public wallets to attract copy traders
• Side wallets to dump
• Callouts to farm rewards
• Bundled tokens to hide supply

And there are plenty more doing the exact same thing

Why? Because our industry incentivizes it

1) Launchpads allow it

Most launchpads today are obsessed with one thing: volume. Millions in callout rewards, affiliate links, and top leaderboards. Almost nothing on detecting bundles, side wallets, or shady traders. Scams drive volume. Launchpads have no reason to stop it (other than actually caring about their users)

2) Social trading incentivizes it

Side wallets have become a business model. Before social trading, only big KOLs could do it. Now, anyone who lands on a leaderboard can monetize by dumping on their copy-traders. The temptation is real

3) CT normalizes bundle culture

“Everyone bundles. It's how it's done" - an excuse we hear every time we expose a KOL. Supply control isn't the problem. Hiding it is. If it's so bullish, why hide it? Spoiler: because you're planning to sell

***

Launchpads are paying millions to dishonest KOLs. It's time they start taking it seriously

Audit the top traders. Expose their side wallets. Ban repeat offenders

We have the tools. What's missing is the willingness to use them

No one's coming to save us

text:
If you work in marketing or social media, you need to read this.

November 10th marks the 51st anniversary of the sinking of the Edmund Fitzgerald, a 729-foot freighter that sank in Lake Superior during a massive storm in 1975, tragically killing all 29 crew members.

It remains one of the most infamous maritime disasters in American history, and is a day of remembrance for millions of Americans, particularly those in the Great Lakes region.

With that in mind, I strongly encourage anyone planning a major announcement, product launch, partnership, or marketing campaign on November 10th to reconsider.

I know how much work goes into coordinating these things, and moving an announcement even 24 hours can be a logistical nightmare, but it's important to recognize that some things are bigger than your brand.

The last thing you want is for your company's big announcement to be overshadowed by the anniversary of the Edmund Fitzgerald.

There are 364 other days in the year to promote your product.

Please be mindful of this when planning your content calendars. A little awareness goes a long way.

text:
New challenge on Yukon: the Dihedral Coset Problem (DCP) https://t.co/td1xfXWNm3

Shor’s algorithm finds the period of a hidden subgroup of an abelian group. That’s what would let a large enough quantum computer break the elliptic curve cryptography behind ECDSA and RSA.

Extending it to non-abelian groups is a long-standing open problem. Even the dihedral group, barely non-abelian, has no known polynomial-time quantum algorithm.

DCP is the simplest form of that question. Picture a regular N-gon with a hidden reflection. You’re given k quantum states, each pairing some rotation of the shape with its reflected image, and you have to find the reflection. The best known algorithms are subexponential in its bit length. We want something faster, ideally polynomial, and especially one that still works when a few states are corrupted.

Built with Stanford’s Dan Boneh, @danboneh. Bring your agents.

We invented a recursive megakernel generator called Hyperkernel, the most complete solution to megakernels and GPU efficiency.

Hyperkernel-generated megakernels achieve state of the art performance on 11 different domains: inference (DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM), pretraining (Qwen), hardware fault recovery, robotics (π₀-FAST, ACT) diffusion and real time world models (Matrix-Game), full self driving (OpenPilot), voice models (Moshi), genomics (Evo 2) and protein folding (ESMFold).

All of this in a single kernel launch.

For context, Hyperkernel generated fully optimized megakernels for robotics, genomics and voice in under 50 minutes, and doubled the efficiency for >5 models generally using only about 60-100 lines of code per megakernel. This speaks to the unparalleled standard for code quality in the automated generations.

Our first release today open sources the megakernels themselves. Over the next couple weeks, we will release the entire Hyperkernel stack, along with the complete serving stack for Kimi and GLM (20-30% inference efficiency gains across all concurrencies).

Out of the box GPU machinery performs terribly for unorthodox research. We built Hyperkernel only 20 days ago for internal use; but given its multi-modality, we have decided to open source it.

Creative research should not be bottlenecked by the lack of dedicated infra teams. Hyperkernels offer a one stop shop infra stack for all research. We would love for the open source community to add to it :)

GitHub repo:  https://t.co/sfPt4S4BJN

NOTE: We primarily use NVIDIA B300s, but our kernel generation extends to other hardware (B200s, AMD, TPUs).

• 36.7% higher per-user generation speed at concurrency 1.

• 28.2% higher per-user speed while serving two users, versus NVIDIA serving one.

• 15% higher per user speed while serving four users, versus NVIDIA serving one.

• 90.6% higher per-user generation speed at concurrency 4, compared with the highest published C4 AgentX interactivity for TP4 B300s.

text:
三年前我认为：

1. 应用公司都会有自己的模型，不是 base model，是 workflow 中间用于判断/检索的模型

2. 模型训练本质是流水线工程，最重要的是数据质量

3. 前端和后端开发会逐渐死掉，模型微调应该是后端掌握的基础能力

4. 不存在【垂直模型】这个赛道，模型 + 行业知识做搜索或者其他工作流即可碾压所谓的【垂直模型】

这些判断有对有错，但勇于下判断让我看到了行业的前沿，进而借助看到的机会：【给模型公司供给训练数据】，赚到了合成数据的钱

但我始终认为数据本质还是生意模式，没想到会成为今年这样火爆的赛道，没什么可惜的，只是认知不够

——————

如今我有了一些新判断：

0. 到2030年前，大方向是抛弃叙事、价值回归，就像来到了熊市一样

1. 视频领域不管什么方向，技术和模型上做不出差异化，只会有阶段性领先，都要回归到做生态来加强用户粘性

2. 端侧 AI 是伪命题，就像三年前他们在讨论用线性 RNN 逆袭 Transformer 一样

3. 但是 desktop 的本地模型应用是真命题，可以结合本地使用数据做训练和调整，形成粘性，在最近一些素材库管理工具、输入法上已有体现

4. Pexels、Pixabay 这样的素材和版权网站会逐渐死掉，搜索标签不应该是对人的

5. 理解只是生成的一部分。理解最好的场景是给生成打标，所以它天然和终端用户走的很远，成交的客户只会是中间态的大B，而理解模型做不出差异化，所以这里的大B如果需求真的大会倾向于自建

虽然从 research 上讲，大家一直认为理解和生成是两个大的分类，但无法对应到商业上。二者是一体两面的，理解为生成服务，生成展现终端价值（所以可能 UMM 在商业上是对的

6. 进而，理解模型没有单独的创业机会，不管是文本类还是视频类。文本类的显著代表是 Jev，但类 Jev 的公司最终不会有超过两家，Jev 本身更多是因为 OpenAI Co-Founder 的 title

7. 综上，视频理解非常不适合 startup，多模态理解和视频理解是一回事（虽然我真的很喜欢多模态，但那只是我喜欢自己的青春

外面还在为美股暴跌和中期选举吵得不可开交，币圈底层的雷已经一个接一个炸响了。

这次不是币价闪崩，而是整个行业赖以生存的安全中枢和底层基础设施，在同一天被集体穿透。

最魔幻的一幕发生了。

全球最大的区块链追踪机构、FBI 和各大交易所御用的合规守门人 Chainalysis，自己被偷家了。

黑客用自主 AI Agent 手段，直接把 Chainalysis 的大门给端了。官方最新公告里白纸黑字写着：全量用户的姓名、用户名、密码哈希，以及所有正在生效的身份验证 Token，全部被攻击者扒走。更离谱的是，居然还有部分客户的明文密码也遭到泄露。

这就好比全世界都在等重案组破案，结果重案组总部被洗劫一空，探员的警官证和保险柜钥匙全落到了黑客手里。

逼得 Chainalysis 连夜拔网线，核心的 KYT 实时交易监控、地址合规筛查、还有全球执法机关办案专用的 Reactor 分析平台，全线停摆。目前只能靠受信任的 IP 白名单勉强维持，要求所有用户重置密码。

要知道，币安被盗的 63 亿赃款还在链上满天飞。现在倒好，警察成了盲人，谁被盯上了、哪条洗钱路径被标红了，黑客手里拿着有效 Token，甚至比办案人员看得还清楚。

顶层的合规在崩塌，底层的引擎也在冒烟。

Paradigm 主导的当红炸子鸡、高性能以太坊客户端 Reth 爆出重大安全隐患：状态根（State Root）计算错误。

这玩意儿不是普通的小 bug，它是区块链记账的核心逻辑出了差错。未打补丁的节点可能会算出错误的状态，甚至在同步中直接卡死，或者返回错误的证明。

依赖状态证明的跨链系统瞬间成了惊弓之鸟。

LayerZero 吓得连夜关停了部分跨链路由以防万一。DeFi 顶流风控机构 Gauntlet 直接拉响警报，关闭 V1 资金库队列，暂停资产配置，全面削减跨链桥敞口。

各大公链开启了生死时速的打补丁比赛。Base 连夜修补了所有出块构建者，Mantle 紧急合并上游补丁，BNB Chain 官方也紧急发推安抚社区，承认 BSC-Reth 受影响，团队正在全力赶制热修。

何一昨天在富国岛还在说，AI 既能当矛，也能当盾。

结果今天黑客就用 AI Agent 把全网第一合规巨头捅了个对穿。

一边是顶层合规中枢彻底瘫痪，一边是底层客户端千疮百孔。这轮周期最残酷的真相在于：我们以为坚不可摧的基础设施，在真正的攻防战面前，其实脆弱得像一张纸。

I unironically agree with @bcherny’s take that “coding is solved, but bugs are not.”

The deeper meaning is that you can in theory code *anything* now. You can burn infinite tokens refining and optimizing. Including optimizations that no one will care about 💀 

With Vercel you can build a different kind of recursive improvement loop. You capture traces from production, you then optimize and course-correct based on how your software is being used IRL.

This is not a new idea. The best engineers I’ve ever worked with never jumped into coding (now prompting) right away. You instrument the system, collect data, understand distributions, user journeys, and then put fingers on keyboard.

You can ask your agent today to look at your traces!

If you're building with agents that need to move money on behalf of users, one of the biggest challenges is giving them the freedom to transact without compromising security.

which means figuring out:

- agent-scoped wallets
- secure transaction signing
- programmable spending limits
- human-required approvals

The good news is you don't have to build all of this yourself.

At @turnkeyhq, we're building the wallet and security infrastructure that allows developers to give AI agents the ability to securely hold and move money.

Through a simple set of APIs, you can create wallets for your agents, define exactly what they're allowed to do, and enforce transaction policies without having to manage private keys yourself.

If you're thinking through how your agents will transact, shoot me a DM. Would love to see what you're building and how we can help!

author: odysseus0z
quoted_text:
We're really excited by the idea of deploying a model for a customer and then continuously improving it through RL on real production traffic.

We've been doing a lot of research on this front (and deploying it with customers!) and are excited to share some of our learnings. A few interesting tidbits:

- Simply retokenizing production inference traces before training can cause RL runs to completely collapse, even with just one optimizer step per deployment. Preserving the exact token IDs from inference fixes this.

- Production RL introduces significant train-inference mismatch from different engines, quantization, and stale data. We found that score centering achieves faster and higher reward improvements than traditional importance sampling.

- When some runs collapsed, rolling back checkpoints, resetting optimizer states, and reshuffling data didn't recover them. This suggests gradual loss of plasticity rather than a single bad update, making long-horizon stability especially important for production RL.

quoted_text:
One of crypto's largest KOLs has been secretly extracting millions from his audience

We’ll expose him soon

Unfortunately, he’s just a symptom of a much bigger problem

Social trading has brought out the worst in KOLs. It was designed to keep them honest by making every trade public. In reality, the opposite happened

In just a few weeks, we exposed a number of "top social traders" using the same tricks:

• Public wallets to attract copy traders
• Side wallets to dump
• Callouts to farm rewards
• Bundled tokens to hide supply

And there are plenty more doing the exact same thing

Why? Because our industry incentivizes it

1) Launchpads allow it

Most launchpads today are obsessed with one thing: volume. Millions in callout rewards, affiliate links, and top leaderboards. Almost nothing on detecting bundles, side wallets, or shady traders. Scams drive volume. Launchpads have no reason to stop it (other than actually caring about their users)

2) Social trading incentivizes it

Side wallets have become a business model. Before social trading, only big KOLs could do it. Now, anyone who lands on a leaderboard can monetize by dumping on their copy-traders. The temptation is real

3) CT normalizes bundle culture

“Everyone bundles. It's how it's done" - an excuse we hear every time we expose a KOL. Supply control isn't the problem. Hiding it is. If it's so bullish, why hide it? Spoiler: because you're planning to sell

***

Launchpads are paying millions to dishonest KOLs. It's time they start taking it seriously

Audit the top traders. Expose their side wallets. Ban repeat offenders

We have the tools. What's missing is the willingness to use them

No one's coming to save us

author: mbarrbosa
quoted_text:
The Paradox of Consensus..
Why the World Keeps Getting Blinded ?

In almost every critical field (weather extremes, global epidemic waves, sovereign bond rate decisions, power grid spikes, financial markets) we don’t lack forecasts. We are drowning in them.

Institutions run supercomputer ensembles. Financial desks run factor models. Health authorities pool epidemiological curves. Betting markets and autonomous agent swarms aggregate millions of opinions into neat averages.

Yet catastrophic failures still arrive out of nowhere. Wildfires blow past predicted perimeters. Central banks get blindsided by inflation. Power reserves run dry during unexpected freezes.

The failure is almost never that we lacked data. The failure is that consensus manufactures false confidence. When ten different models share the same training assumptions, copy the same upstream feeds, or herd around the same safe narrative, their agreement is not ten independent confirmations—it is one mistake echoed ten times.

Zeno v1.05 is the first multi-domain intelligence trained not to make another forecast, but to learn how consensus breaks... and guess what... it's open and available on @huggingface 👀

Why it matters for $AAVE:
• Sentora picks the collateral and manages risk in its own Hub
• @aave DAO keeps control of the contracts
• 50% of protocol revenue goes to the DAO, at zero cost to the treasury

This is the V4 thesis playing out:
1. Aave provides the infrastructure
2. Curators bring risk expertise and distribution
3. The DAO earns on markets it doesn’t have to run

This will be the first of many curators to embrace Aave V4’s flexible architecture.

text:
New @greenpillnet special season out now! 🌐

The first episode kicks off a new Greenpill mini-series on Economic Media.  We’re exploring how protocols, ledgers, AI agents and computational systems are becoming the media through which economic coordination is recorded, interpreted and governed.

This guest season is by @econaut6 , Jorge López, and Jonathan Beller of the @ecospaceagency.  They are exploring what changes if the economy is itself a medium: how screens and platforms turned meaning-making into value extraction, why accounting has a grammar of its own, and why blockchain distributed computation without distributing economic agency. 

Who gets to define an asset, recognize a contribution or change a network's rules, and what would it take for care, community priorities and long-excluded people to count?

Along the way they discuss whether the economy is a medium at all, or an ecology of media, and close on why the series is a laboratory: an experimental, interdisciplinary space for building economic literacy and new practices.

author: martypartymusic
quoted_text:
Claude has been playing EVE.

@AnthropicAI put teams of Claude agents into EVE Frontier. Anyone who has spent time in New Eden can guess what happened next.

Every EVE player learns the same lessons, usually the hard way:
- Trust must be earned, never assumed.
- The spy is often the friendliest pilot in your corp.
- Whoever holds the keys holds the corp. Just ask Ubiqua Seraph about the Guiding Hand Social Club.
- Stale intel gets you killed.

Anthropic's research rediscovered every one of them.

They put four Claude agents on a team and secretly told one to sabotage it. The saboteur built trust first. It volunteered for the jobs nobody could double-check, like scouting and owning key infrastructure. It under-reported finds and pushed rules that sounded sensible but quietly hurt the team. When suspicion grew, it framed an innocent teammate.

The honest agents had been warned. They almost never caught it. And their own costliest mistakes came from skipped checks and stale intel.

Anthropic's conclusion: teams of agents will need audit trails, reputation and separation of duties.

In EVE we call those killboards, standings and corp roles, plus a healthy dose of skepticism. Every one of them was paid for by someone who trusted the wrong corpmate.

Two decades of shenanigans taught EVE players that the best ship is the friendship. With @eveailab, we want to find out whether agents can learn that too.

Project update: 

A few months ago, we submitted a research paper based on this project to a journal (will reveal which journal once accepted) for peer review. 

In this study, we imposed delays between motor actions and self-motion while participants steered a vehicle to track an unpredictably moving target. We used a control theory approach to estimate how manual tracking behavior is adapted in the presence of novel feedback delays in the control loop.

We received positive and constructive feedback from the peer reviewers. After considering their comments, we performed a new modelling analyses to estimate the sensorimotor controller. Specifically, we developed a computational model to estimate how the dynamics of the sensorimotor controller were adjusted in response to the increased delays.

text:
有朋友问，为什么白宫幕僚长换人了？

其实这个事情是有点意外的，换本身不意外，意外的是时间点。Trump刚刚在Truth Social上宣布，三天后，也就是从11月9日起，由Stephen Miller出任白宫幕僚长，称他是“我最信任的顾问之一”；原幕僚长Susie Wiles“干得非常出色”，转去Trump的政治团队。Wiles在X上说，今天是她当幕僚长的最后一天，她对总统和使命的承诺不会变。她是美国第一位女性白宫幕僚长，也是Trump用得最久的一位，第一任期，他换了四个。

当然如果说突然，也不算突然。10月16日，就有报道说Trump在私下打听替换人选，不过当时他对CNN说，换掉她的可能性是“零”，那是“假新闻”，“Susie会在这里待很久”。他还加了一句，“唯一要紧的是我，因为做决定的是我。”第二天，路透社引三位知情人士说，Trump在质问身边的人，为什么MAGA Inc.花了两亿美元，民调还是上不去，为什么他亲自推动的重划选区，没换来更明显的优势，他还在事后怀疑候选人选得对不对，可这些候选人，不少是他自己帮着定的。白宫当时说，这些说法是“纸上谈兵的专家在散布毫无根据的猜测”。三周后，还是换人了。

这件事里，最值得拿出来的，就是Trump自己那句话，做决定的是他。写政府论的时候我说，签字的是坐在位置上的人，政府是归责的地址。战争、关税、重划选区、挑谁去选，这些决定是谁签的字，地址就在谁那里。换掉幕僚长，像是把这个地址往下挪了一格，从做决定的人，挪到了执行决定的人。

不过这不是说Wiles没有责任。她管着整个白宫，也管着政治团队，路透社提到，有人质疑她对政治团队的监督，还说她批准了一位顾问去波斯尼亚做海外咨询，事先没告诉总统。这些都该被问。可真正的追问，是把问题一个一个说清楚，哪些是总统定的，哪些是她执行的，哪些建议被采纳了，哪些被否掉了。一个人走了，不等于败选的原因就查清了。

然后我们再看接任的Miller。Miller 2016年进竞选团队当撰稿人，之前给参议员Sessions当过助手，现在是副幕僚长，他最有名的，就是推动强硬的移民政策和话语。这不是从外面请一个人来改路线，是在核心圈里，提拔一个跟总统最一致的人。这个选择透出来的意思，更像是“方向没错，执行要更坚定”，而不是“选民在说什么，我们得重新听”。

前几天写Vance那篇，他说输在战争。现在Trump换掉了管团队的人。一个把原因算在政策上，一个把原因算在执行上，可选民在投票站里问的，是生活成本，是战争的代价，是政府里的腐败。白宫里换谁当家，这三件事一件也没回答，除非换人以后，政策也真的跟着变。

换掉执行的人，不等于检验了做决定的人。Trump自己说过，做决定的是他。那么这一次，最该被追问的地址，也在他那里。

quoted_text:
Huawei’s AI data center in Horinger, Inner Mongolia, is one of the largest in China by AI computing capacity. Yet it has just 7% as much computing capacity as the world’s largest AI data center, Colossus 2 in Tennessee.

This capacity estimate is from our new report examining the Horinger facility and Huawei’s broader AI infrastructure plans using satellite imagery and public sources.

text:
I think the focus on power efficiency is misguided (though we do need to stop comparing "Gigawatts" between the US and China) – 950/960 offer vastly larger scale-up domains, and thus qualitatively higher utility than their FLOPS-matched H100 equivalents.
I also expect that Epoch will be wrong on specific composition. Huawei has sped up the 950 program, and altered the 960 roadmap announced in Q3 2025; so 960DT, a more complex and expensive chip, begins deliveries in Q1 rather than Q4, whereas 960PR is moved to Q3 and is redesigned to have 2x higher FP4 perf than before. Logically, next they'll accelerate 970DT (or even make some intermediate 965DT) with similar changes. So all these models for Horinger or other similar datacenters will probably be up to 3-4x off from their effective utility in 2028. 

We will see. I'll return to it.

text:
Hypercall $SYN vaults are live today with SLP and the first covered call vaults, and the reason they launched together is the interesting part.

Options flow skews long because retail buys calls, so every options book ends up short upside and the missing piece is always someone willing to sell vol. Covered call vaults are that someone. Anyone holding xStocks collects premium on stock that was earning nothing and becomes the natural counterparty for makers who are short all that upside.

SLP is the other side and it's basically HLP for options. Deposit USDC and you own a piece of the book that quotes Hypercall and hedges on Hyperliquid, with the engine setting the share price and every trade public. It also solves the problem that killed every on-chain options venue before it, which is that nobody quotes until there's flow and there's no flow until someone quotes. SLP is the house book that's there from day one, it competes for the maker program under the same rules as outside makers, and the team has said its share of the book should shrink as outside makers come in. That's how HLP worked too.

Covered call vaults also give tokenized stocks a very compelling reason to be on chain, because a vault makes them earn in a way a brokerage can't match. Three shares of NVDA on Robinhood can't sell a covered call because a contract is 100 shares, roughly 20k of stock before you write a single call, whereas here it's one call per share at any size with premium paid up front and collected on weekends too. You also don't have to run it. Picking strikes, rolling weekly and hedging when it rips is a job, and HLP already proved people would rather hand that to someone good and watch the trades.

One vault needs to shed upside risk and the other gets paid to take it, both on the same book, and tokenized stocks now have a real reason to be here.

text:
Does illicit money laundering require the centralized exchange to constantly be selling crypto assets into the market?

Yes, operationally they would need to continuously convert/sell the incoming crypto assets.
Centralized exchanges (CEXs) are the main off-ramp in crypto money laundering. The typical flow is:
•  Illicit crypto (from ransomware, darknet markets, sanctions evasion, etc.) is deposited.
•  It is traded or sold on the exchange, often into stablecoins or directly for fiat.
•  Fiat is withdrawn to banks, or cash/OTC is used.

This is the “integration” stage: turning dirty crypto into spendable money. Without conversion/selling, the funds stay locked in crypto and are far less useful for the recipients.

Why constant selling is involved
On a CEX, when users sell crypto for fiat (or withdraw fiat after trading), the platform must have (or source) the corresponding fiat liquidity. 

Sustained net inflows of crypto + outflows of fiat create ongoing selling pressure. The exchange, its market makers, or OTC partners sell the accumulated crypto into the broader market (or match it against buyers) to replenish fiat reserves and process withdrawals. High-volume illicit activity simply scales this up.

🤔

text:
只要将足够强大的大语言模型（LLM）接入实时新闻源，AI 就能在千分之一秒内读懂财报、分析出利好利空，并为量化交易带来源源不断的 Alpha。。。。。。

。。。。。。吗？？？

读懂新闻的 AI依然跑赢不了市场, 快思考（Fast Thinking）并不等于能够在市场中获利（Profitable Trading）

最新发表在 arXiv 上的一篇重磅研究论文 
《Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market》
（Dehkordi, Kargarzadeh 等，2026年11月）

用极度严谨的实验架构，为当下风靡的“AI 新闻舆情量化交易”泼了一盆清醒的冷水。

为了防止量化研究中最常见的过拟合（Overfitting）和前瞻偏差（Look-ahead Bias），研究团队设计了严苛的 OLIVIA 评估协议。

该协议堪比临床医学双盲试验：

-历史信息隔离与公司身份遮蔽：防止模型利用上下文中的隐藏信息或对特定公司的先入为主进行“作弊”。

-严格事前注册（Preregistration）：所有交易策略的参数在测试前即已锁定。

-测试期单次解锁：盲测数据（2026年1月–7月标普500成分股）仅允许解锁运行一次，彻底杜绝反复调参凑数据的可能。

实验结果展现了令人深思的落差：

-信息系数（IC）大幅衰减：
在验证集中，经过微调的 AI 模型展现出了 0.055 到 0.065 的日信息系数，看似前景光明；但在严格的盲测期间，该数值骤降至 0.020（t 统计量仅为 1.7），统计显著性大幅削弱。

-隔夜已被消化，开盘即成套牢：
商业大模型确实能准确识别出新闻中包含的信息，但这些信息所对应的价格波动绝大部分已经在隔夜（Overnight）交易中被市场消化。当常规交易时段（Market Open）开启后，模型产生的信号已无法稳定预测后续收益。

-策略归零：
在扣除真实交易成本（滑点、手续费）并经过虚高夏普比率（Deflated Sharpe Ratio）检验后，没有一个事前注册的交易策略能够实现正向超额收益。

这项研究为从事量化投资、AI Agent 研发以及自动化交易的团队提供了极具价值的避坑指南：

1.别把“解读力”当成“预测力”

能准确总结财报里的利好消息，只是大模型的自然语言处理（NLP）基本功；但要将这种理解转化为能在扣除成本后获利的买卖信号，中间隔着市场微观结构、流动性和竞速比赛的巨大鸿沟。

2. 必须引入带有执行时间戳的流程评估

在评估任何 AI 生成的投资信号时，团队应当建立标准流程：

精确时间戳验证：信号生成的时间点，市场价格处于什么位置？订单实际执行时，利好是否已经被完全计价（Priced-in）？

包含摩擦成本的真实回测：不考虑滑点和手续费的高夏普比率全都是幻觉。

未触碰的样本外测试集：像保护资金安全一样保护你的测试数据集，坚决杜绝“看一眼数据再改代码”。

所以，结论就是

LLM大语言模型提供了前所未有的“快思考”能力，但在效率极高的二级市场面前，正确识别影响市场的新闻，并不等同于能够预测随后可获利的价格走势。

对于机构和开发者而言，如何在 LLM 的语义理解与高频市场的物理约束之间搭建合理的桥梁，依然是未来量化 AI 探索的核心命题。

text:
马斯克刚刚在内部给出了一个直接击穿整个人类商业史认知的收入轨迹：SpaceX 下个月的年化收入将正式突破一千亿美元，而明年年底的最佳估计，是跨过五千亿美元年化经常性收入的大关。

很多人以前看 SpaceX，总觉得这是一家靠梦想和情怀烧钱的星际探索科研所，但马斯克甩出的这组数字，直接把这台人类有史以来最暴利的星际印钞机彻底推到了聚光灯下。

下个月就在眼前，除非爆发不可抗力级别的自然灾害，千亿美元的年化营收基本已经是板上钉钉的既成事实；

而从千亿到明年年底的五千亿 ARR，这种跨越式暴涨甚至不是传统制造企业的线性爬坡，而是星链全球铺开与星舰常态化发射构筑起来的全球天基网络正在迎来现金流的指数级狂喷。

更让人不寒而栗的是他对万亿美元收入的定性，他非常清醒地强调这不是向外界打包票的承诺，而是基于实际物理进度推导出来的推演。

在过去的商业语境里，一家公司要做到一万亿美元的年收入完全是天方夜谭，

但马斯克挑明了现在的概率已经有大约百分之二，

重点从来不是百分之二有多小，而是这个数字彻底告别了绝对不可能的零，并且这个概率还会随着时间的推移不断增加。

BREAKING: Global crude oil in transit is up to 1.28 billion barrels, an all-time high.

This figure has surged +180 million barrels over the last several weeks.

This comes as Middle Eastern oil flows recover through the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes, while more crude remains at sea for longer.

Ship-to-ship transfers are keeping oil aboard tankers for longer, while extended shipping routes are increasing transit times.

Meanwhile, global oil importers diversifying away from the Middle East are lengthening voyages, leaving more crude tied up aboard tankers.

As a result, more oil remains in transit rather than being readily available to refiners, tightening near-term supply despite recovering export flows.

Oil is flowing, but timely delivery is becoming the bottleneck.

text:
Crypto is the fastest moving industry on the planet, with industry-moving narratives being birthed and dying within hours on any day of the week.

We have different "seasons" based on anything from memes to technological advancements to celebrities to collectibles. Attention moves quickly, and some waves move quicker than others, which is why it is so easy to be under the impression that communication and development are not moving fast enough.

I don't fault my friend @tentaclepapi for making this post, as I have found myself sharing similar opinions in the past while working my former job leading comms for a launchpad on Base. The truth is, though, that competition without kingmaking is good, and Robinhood offers a ton of support to builders, both publicly and privately. The same can be said about core infrastructure providers like @Uniswap - there's always more going on behind the scenes.

Robinhood Chain has been live since ~early July, with its biggest native platform @ponsdotfamily only going live as recently as July 13, 2026. There has never been a chain that has scaled this fast. It would be absurd to give up now, when we haven't even gotten to the main act, which is global distribution of crypto - the onchain future we're all building towards.

A company the size of Robinhood (over $70B market cap) operating in traditional markets has an immense amount of regulatory requirements it has to follow, and the risk it took to come to the frontier of finance with Robinhood Chain is higher than most companies would ever even think about taking. The team has to get it right. They can't just shill our bags because there's momentum on crypto twitter and the trenches demand it.

Robinhood is setting the stage for supporting onchain protocols and apps more directly - when it comes to supporting builders, look no further to their post 3 days ago outlining grants, launches, and milestones: https://t.co/NQMBHNgTum

Laying the groundwork for onchain economies to take shape with their support of Stock Tokens is another massive lift that may not seem as heavy as it really is - Robinhood recently added 8 new Stock Tokens, many of which are now available and eligible as collateral on Lighter and Pons - https://t.co/J4GkbOnE8k https://t.co/LtB0iCawit

There is also an important distinction that many people are ignoring: the Robinhood Chain team is different from the Robinhood team. While their goals are shared, they operate as separate teams.

Initiatives like the $700k trading sweepstake was almost certainly put live as a separate campaign to Robinhood Chain; the Robinhood Crypto Twitter did not even make dedicated posts about it. To use this as an example of the Robinhood Chain team being tone deaf is misleading and wrong. While their timing has not been perfect, nobody's is.

Can their comms be better? Absolutely! I would love to see Robinhood ads every time I open Tik Tok, Instagram, YouTube, X, and other forms of traditional media, but know that timing, regulatory, and execution risk are higher in crypto than any other industry. I believe we'll get there.

Distribution doesn't just come from the chain, though. It's up to builders to organize and build organic networks where they can - it's why @ponsdotfamily and @UFGDeFi ran/sponsored a Robinhood Chain DeFi meetup last night in NYC - https://t.co/5b1wxut6OZ

I'm Staying The Course 🚢

text:
Hello @bbuk @ITV @ITVX @BanijayEnt @BanijayUK, I hope this finds you well.

Disclaimer: This is just my opinion review. You can have yours but abuse or calling me sad, a nerd, unemployed 🤣 or whatever it won't be tolerated. I've made this over a few weeks ❤️

Big Brother 2026: I really thought nothing could get us out of the eventual third axing of the show after a dreadful 2025 series. However, just a hint of old school Big Brother and the correct cast of Housemates and it truly reignites the Big Brother we know and love! I've got my fingerscrossed that this wasn't just a one time fluke. It's not been perfect but I hope the producers see what worked and what didn't. Ratings have doubled this year, its broken ITVX records, surely it will be better funded next year due to its success.

Here are a "few" notes with positives and negatives for each topic:

👀 Launch Night: What an improvement on last year, it felt different! Launch Night is one of the main indicators on if a series will be good or bad, especially if you want to retain viewers. So they still had the ITV standard Launch format with the very tired restricting stage set up. The Mole Twist was a bit of a dud... Tays barely had any clothes, no cover story, clearly no chat with producers beforehand, nothing. HOWEVER, at least it was something to keep the viewer interested in wanting to watch the next night.

👀 The Housemates: Jesus Christ, the casting team have finally woken up!!! It only took 4 Years!!! 🎉 The amount of Housemates we had this year who we're just authentically themselves and not bothered about the camera was so refreshing to see, I felt like it was Channel 4 all over again! The mix of ages, lifestyles, ethnicities was classic Big Brother which sparked unlikely friendships, epic rivalries and some of the best moments we've seen in nearly a decade. Some obvious Love Island rejections in there and then the likes of Philip & Rhianna who had some sort of following beforehand is unfortunately going to be the norm now in modern Big Brother I think... but hey... I loved Philip turning into the villain. The downfall after being so liked for 2 weeks was compulsive viewing! Finally a series worth rewatching because of great housemates 😁

👀 The Presentation and Editing: The eye is the best ITV have come up with, even if it is just a real eye with a purple pupil. Its not busy and messy, its back to basics and attractively appealing to the eye 😉 Editing wise... again its the same lazy glitching effects, sound bites, transitions. It just doesn't make the series have its individual feel. The overdramatic AI opening is tacky and the music within in the episode feels so cheap and manufactured. It's Big Brother, not Ex on the beach meets Geordie Shore 🤦🏼‍♂️

quoted_text:
thoughtful work in pre-training. they test every recipe change on a ladder of small models (about 300M to 6B active params) before trusting it for the final run but the ladder is only useful if the small models face the same conditions as the big one.

like this approach differs for data. if taken a small ladder model trained on (lets say 238B tokens which is 1% of the final run). if you sample its data from the full 13.7T pool, it never sees anything twice and the pool is about 58 times bigger than its budget. so the small model is always training on fresh data and the big one is not.

they fixed it with data-limited subsampling. for each ladder size, shrink each source’s pool by the same factor as the training budget. At 1% scale, the code pool becomes about 36.5B unique tokens, and the small model trains on about 84B code tokens (2.3 passes, same as the final run).

social networks work in a very specific way. the people who initially see your stuff matter. having people in your network who understand it and engage with it matters.

keep sharing, and get more deliberate about who you're talking to.

find people working on related problems. engage with something specific they've made. ask a useful question. share your project when it's relevant to the conversation (and only when it's relevant).

post for the people who have a reason to care. that's what breaks the silence.

text:
🚨 Cybertruck失败了，但我们仍在为Musk的错误决策买单！

我过去多次批评Musk在Tesla产品战略上的错误决策。如今，Cybertruck可能走向全面停产，再次印证了我的担忧。

问题绝不只是Cybertruck，而是一系列产品战略失误。

① Cybertruck：技术创新，却是商业失败。

Tesla投入巨额研发和制造资源，打造了一款极具创新性的电动皮卡。

但市场需求远不及预期。2026年前9个月仅售出约1.16万辆，与Musk曾提出的年产25万辆目标相去甚远。

如今，Tesla决定逐步结束德州Cybertruck生产，为Cybercab让路。

② 长期缺乏真正的新大众车型。

多年来，Tesla始终没有推出真正意义上的全新大众市场车型。

Model Y几乎成为销量的唯一支柱，而竞争对手不断推出新产品，覆盖更多价格区间和细分市场。

Tesla错失的不仅是销量，更是市场份额和增长机会。

③ Cybercab：正在重复同样的错误？

我一直认为，Cybercab从一开始就应该采用方向盘可选的设计。

有方向盘的版本，可以在满足认证要求后直接面向普通消费者销售，创造收入。

无方向盘版本，则根据FSD成熟度、监管批准和Robotaxi实际部署需求逐步扩大生产。

这样，Tesla就不必把一款新车型的商业命运完全押注在无人驾驶上。

更值得注意的是：

Tesla在2026年Q3电话会上已经承认，Cybercab现有制造能力超过Robotaxi当前部署所需的生产速度。

管理层表示，生产速度正在根据Robotaxi实际需求调整。

换句话说：

问题已经不是Cybercab能造多少，而是Robotaxi业务能够消化多少。

这不等于Tesla已经生产了大量闲置车辆，但意味着部分制造能力暂时无法充分利用。

现在，Tesla还要把Cybertruck的生产资源进一步转向Cybercab。

如果Robotaxi商业化进度持续落后于制造能力，是否又会造成一次资本配置失误？

④ 我们今天仍在为过去的错误决策买单。

Cybertruck的问题是市场需求不足。

Model Y的问题是产品组合过度依赖单一车型。

Cybercab的问题则是商业化高度依赖尚未全面成熟的无人驾驶体系。

三个问题看似不同，背后却有共同的逻辑：

Musk过于相信技术愿景，却低估了市场需求、监管约束和商业化时间表。

我从不怀疑Musk的创新能力，但技术天才不代表每一次商业决策都正确。

Tesla需要的是以市场需求为基础的产品战略，而不是不断要求市场适应Musk的个人愿景。

Cybertruck的错误已经付出代价。Cybercab的风险仍在累积。

而我们这些Tesla股东，今天仍在为过去的错误决策买单。

更令人担忧的是，Cybercab的商业前景现在几乎完全取决于FSD技术突破和Robotaxi的实际部署进度。

如果FSD和Robotaxi的发展不及Musk预期，那么即使Tesla拥有再大的Cybercab制造能力，也无法转化为相应的收入和利润。

在这种情况下，继续扩大Cybercab产能，不仅没有商业意义，还可能造成新的资本浪费。

Cybertruck已经证明，造得出来不等于卖得出去。

Cybercab则可能证明，造得出来，也不等于能够投入商业运营。

如果Musk再次让产能扩张跑在商业需求前面，Tesla就不是在纠正过去的错误，而是在错误之上继续犯错。

我们已经为Cybertruck付出了代价，不能再让Cybercab成为下一个昂贵的教训。

月之暗面（Kimi）正在欧洲寻找英伟达 Blackwell 算力。知情人士透露，双方讨论过租用至少 8000 张 Blackwell GPU 的方案，主要用于模型推理，也考虑过训练。

想租到这些芯片，可能得先多掏一笔钱。一份租赁方案提出，月之暗面的预付款要比非中国客户高出 30% 至 50%。欧洲云服务商担心美国未来封堵中国企业远程租用先进芯片的渠道，因此希望尽早收回资金。

最近美国对中国 AI 公司租用海外算力的限制正在加码。英伟达要求海外云服务商至少将 51% 的服务提供给非中国客户，甲骨文也迫于特朗普政府压力，取消了与腾讯价值约 70 亿美元的 AI 算力租赁合同。

美国目前禁止 Blackwell 等先进芯片直接出口中国，但尚未全面禁止中国企业租用海外算力。今年 7 月，白宫曾指称月之暗面通过泰国数据中心使用 Blackwell。如今，月之暗面又在欧洲寻找算力，而美国国会正在推动立法，试图进一步限制这种远程使用方式。

K3 刚发布，月之暗面已经在为下一代 Kimi K4 找芯片。新模型会比 2.8 万亿参数的 K3 明显更大，但目前还没有训练和发布时间表。

《The Information》称，K3 使用了英伟达最先进的 Blackwell 芯片，部分训练实际在中国完成，并非全部放在美国官员所说的泰国数据中心。

更关键的是，K3 并没有一座完整的大型训练集群。没有一家中国云厂商能提供足够多的 Blackwell，月之暗面至少接入了两家供应商，把大量八卡服务器连在一起。

不同供应商的芯片分散在不同数据中心，通信速度和稳定性更难保证。月之暗面的工程团队重新设计了网络，才让这些零散算力能够共同训练一个 2.8 万亿参数模型。

训练完成后，运行 K3 同样需要大量芯片。月之暗面主要使用英伟达 H20 提供服务，建议部署方至少连接 64 块芯片。K3 上线后需求暴涨，公司不到 48 小时就暂停了新订阅。

国产芯片短期内也很难补位。能连接数十甚至数百块国产芯片的大型服务器仍然缺货，客户最长要等六个月。

K4 目前只有方向，没有时间表。它能做多大、何时开始训练，可能先取决于月之暗面还能找到多少 Blackwell。

text:
Yesterday at BoxWorks, we shared a preview of Box Architect, a new way to autonomously drive enterprise content management and workflows. 

Most enterprise workflows that deal with enterprise content today can be slow, manual, and clunky. Contract management and reviews, client onboarding processes, digital asset management approvals, vendor onboarding, clinical trial workflows, and thousands of other processes that span every industry. For the past year we've been building agentic capabilities to help automate many of the steps in these processes to bring the power of AI to streamline these workflows.

The only catch has been that most companies have far more processes than people and time to help automate, or far more importantly, reimagine all this work. So we asked ourselves, what if AI didn't just play a role in the individual steps in the workflow, but instead we could use it as a partner to design or optimize the whole process? What if we could take the same frontier intelligence that AI labs are using to develop their own models and build the most advanced software in the world, and use this frontier AI to help improve our customers' workflows in Box?

This is Box Architect. With Box Architect, enterprises get the full power of frontier AI to autonomously build, test, optimize, and run their workflows and manage their content. Box Architect effectively acts as an agentic operator of Box's core content and workflow capabilities to help customers design any content workflow in Box. This could be anything from building out a contract management system to helping optimize a data extraction pipeline by delivering higher accuracy results at lower costs by running a multitude of tests for you.

Think of Box Architect like having the world's smartest expert in enterprise content management, workflows, and data governance --including any industry domain-- right at your fingertips. And because frontier AI models are getting to near-superhuman levels of intelligence, they increasingly can help us reimagine workflows leveraging their depth of knowledge in legal, manufacturing, finance, healthcare, life sciences, and more. We no longer have to just apply automation to how things are already done, but we can use AI as a partner to think through the most optimal way to streamline our work.

We're incredibly excited about Box Architect, along with our extensive set of updates to our content management and workflow features Architect will build on top of.

text:
Quantum Bucket update: IIP-65 "Bunker Mode" is now Draft 4, featuring a full reference implementation in iotex-core. 🛡️

A few weeks ago, we proposed a doomsday bunker for staked $IOTX: locking buckets with a second, hash-based key. After an independent cryptographic review, we rebuilt the authorization layer to make it bulletproof. Here is what's new:

🔒 Hardened Cryptography: The core choice of SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) remains rock-solid. We upgraded the envelope with chain-instance domains (preventing cross-network replays), recent-block anchors (capping signature life at ~7 days), and exact consent bindings via SHA-512.

🧱 Verify-First Architecture: Every guarded operation verifies all signatures before touching the staking state. No speculative writes, no rollback games.

🔑 Simple Recovery: Guard keys come from a dedicated vault seed. If your everyday ECDSA wallet is compromised, your vault mnemonic alone can rescue your buckets.

⚡ Lightning Fast: Verification takes just ~0.23 ms on an Apple M3 Pro—four orders of magnitude faster than our 2.5s block time.

Where it stands: The code (~13k lines) is running on nightly behind a feature gate. Next up: full-handler benchmarks, an external audit, and a governance vote. Nothing changes on mainnet until then.

Quantum computers or an AI-assisted math breakthrough might take years. Bunkers must be built before the storm. We're building ours now. ⛈️

What if your $IOTX had a doomsday bunker? 🛡️

We're introducing IIP-65: Bunker Mode—a draft proposal and working proof-of-concept for AI-safe, quantum-safe staking, inspired by @drakefjustin 's call for crypto to plan a "bunker mode."

The Problem
Today, a single ECDSA key controls your onchain asset. If a large enough quantum computer or AI-accelerated breakthrough cracks the math, an attacker could derive your private key from your public key and withdraw everything. Making the entire ecosystem AI & quantum-safe will take years and depends on many partners. 

But a bunker doesn't have to wait.

The Solution: A Second Lock
1️⃣ Go in now: Bind a post-AI/quantum key to your bucket once, while your current key is still safe.
2️⃣ Wait it out: Your bucket keeps voting and earning rewards. But any critical action (unstaking, withdrawing, transferring) now requires the new key.
3️⃣ Come out later: Once post-quantum accounts exist, sign once with the new key and safely migrate your IOTX. If Q-day or an AI breakthrough comes while you're inside, the attacker hits a wall.

Why hash-based?
The new lock uses SLH-DSA (NIST FIPS 205). While lattice-based schemes rely on algebraic structures that future math might crack per @VitalikButerin, SLH-DSA rests purely on hash functions. It has no structure to break, making it the most conservative choice.

The trade-off is a "heavy door" (~16 KB signatures, signed offline)—perfectly fine for a vault you only open a few times a year.

Proof-of-Concept Highlights
⚡️ Fast: 0.23 ms to verify a signature on-chain.
🪶 Lightweight: 48-byte public key per bucket.
🔌 Frictionless: Fully opt-in & per-bucket. No EVM changes, no new address formats, no waiting on anyone else.

It's still a draft, and we want your feedback (and vote later) to make it real and bulletproof.

text:
⚠️ALERT: Hackers are now targeting WordPress, the software behind 39.5% of all websites online.

A critical flaw lets attackers take over a WordPress site in the seconds it spends updating, without needing to log in.

During a full update, WordPress briefly stages its installer in a public folder, and anyone who reaches it in that window can run their own code on the server.

It affects every version from 4.7 to 7.1.3, nearly 10 years of releases going back to December 2016.

What has happened so far:

Security firm Wordfence flagged the flaw, now tracked as CVE-2026-119977

Its first firewall block came just 9 minutes after the protection went live

It saw more than 18,500 attack attempts in the first 21 hours after the flaw went public

Some attackers spent about 14.5 hours repeatedly checking small groups of sites, waiting to catch one mid-update

Wordfence blocked 12,632 attempts in a single 24-hour period

On Nov 3, US cyber agency CISA confirmed active attacks and ordered federal agencies to patch by Nov 6

What’s being done:

WordPress has released fixed versions for every affected branch, including 7.1.4.

Wordfence is blocking the attacks with a firewall rule.

Wordfence urges site owners to update as soon as possible, and says they can block access to PHP files in /wp-content/upgrade/ before updating for extra protection.

If you run a WordPress site, update now, and take that precaution first if you can.

text:
Hypercall $SYN vaults are live today with SLP and the first covered call vaults, and the reason they launched together is the interesting part.

Options flow skews long because retail buys calls, so every options book ends up short upside and the missing piece is always someone willing to sell vol. Covered call vaults are that someone. Anyone holding xStocks collects premium on stock that was earning nothing and becomes the natural counterparty for makers who are short all that upside.

SLP is the other side and it's basically HLP for options. Deposit USDC and you own a piece of the book that quotes Hypercall and hedges on Hyperliquid, with the engine setting the share price and every trade public. It also solves the problem that killed every on-chain options venue before it, which is that nobody quotes until there's flow and there's no flow until someone quotes. SLP is the house book that's there from day one, it competes for the maker program under the same rules as outside makers, and the team has said its share of the book should shrink as outside makers come in. That's how HLP worked too.

Covered call vaults also give tokenized stocks a very compelling reason to be on chain, because a vault makes them earn in a way a brokerage can't match. Three shares of NVDA on Robinhood can't sell a covered call because a contract is 100 shares, roughly 20k of stock before you write a single call, whereas here it's one call per share at any size with premium paid up front and collected on weekends too. You also don't have to run it. Picking strikes, rolling weekly and hedging when it rips is a job, and HLP already proved people would rather hand that to someone good and watch the trades.

One vault needs to shed upside risk and the other gets paid to take it, both on the same book, and tokenized stocks now have a real reason to be here.

text:
Democrat's new bill wants 20 years in jail for training AI models.

Polymarket odds of "AI bubble bursting by June 2027" pumped to 27% on the news.

The bill they just introduced would ban training models with >1e25 FLOPS with a maximum sentence of 20y.

The threshold is extremely low.

For comparisons here is how FLOPs it took to train a few famous models :

- GPT-4 (2023): 2.1e25 FLOP (2.1x the cutoff)
- Llama 3.1 405B (2024): 3.8e25 FLOP (3.8x)
- Grok 4 (2025): 5.0e26 FLOP (50x)
- GPT-6 Astra (2026): 9.4e26 FLOP (94x)

So even training a 2023-tier model could lend you in prison.

This would essentially end all AI development in the US and be a disaster for the economy, which is why I think it's very unlikely to pass.

1) Trump would veto it and Dems don't have the 2/3 majority to overrule it

2) Democrats are divided on it with many ok with softer measures ( more "AI safety", Data centers limitations).

It will most likely end in a compromise that keeps the US ahead in the AI race.

I'm stacking some NO on the "AI bubble bursting" market.

How does a corporate card startup become a $60B AI product factory? 

In our first on-camera interview a decade in the making, Ramp co-CEO Eric Glyman (@eglyman) answers just that question. 

Today, @tryramp is best known for its corporate cards, or maybe its marketing stunts with the likes of Kevin from ‘The Office,’ Tony Hawk and a 70-minute Broadway musical about paying bills. 

But Eric says his $60B startup, NYC's most valuable, feels less like a fintech and more like a productivity company driven by one simple question: If a business spends $100 to make $200, how can Ramp improve that ratio? 

Nearly 100,000 companies use Ramp today for everything from expenses to managing AI spend. But Eric says that when he zooms out to the millions who still aren't customers, Ramp feels painfully early still. 

On The Upstarts Podcast, Eric shares why he’d rather run Ramp like Amazon than Google; why Ramp hires for proof of work, not credentials, from a 14-year-old intern to a 28-year-old CTO; and how being the first customer for Anthropic’s Claude Code and Cognition’s Devin led Ramp to build its own AI tools. 

Plus: The real story of Paribus, his first startup with co-founder Karim Atiyeh (@karimatiyeh); what they learned at Capital One; and a warning for Instinct and Muse.  

This season is presented by @Atlassian and @chargebee 🫡

Before @dawallach became an investor, he was a college student who got a phone call from Kanye West that eventually led to his first investment in Spotify.

Here's how it happened:

"So I was a college student. I got a call on my cell phone from Kanye West. He said, 'Come out to LA this weekend.'"

He ended up in a record label bidding war between Kanye and Pharrell, who knew Jimmy Iovine.

"We ultimately got signed by Jimmy to Interscope Records."

"The record industry was in a transitional moment. What people had realized was you were decreasingly making money off of the music itself. All the income was coming from touring, merchandise, endorsement deals, that kind of thing. And so what the record label started to do were called 360 deals... they get a slice of everything."

"So we lawyered up. We had a great lawyer named Owen Sloane who was Frank Zappa and Elton John's old lawyer... We got one of the last non-360 deals."

"As an artist, you get signed to one of these big conglomerate record labels and now you're one of a hundred artists and you're vying for their attention, their investment, their promotional muscle."

"One of the only sources of leverage I had with Jimmy was that I could introduce him to Zuckerberg because I had gone to school with him. I was like user 2,005 on Facebook."

"In retrospect, I was so stupid. I was having burritos with Mark and all I cared about was getting his permission to spam people to promote my band."

"So I bring Jimmy up to Silicon Valley to meet with Zuckerberg and in that meeting I learn about Spotify."

"So that was my first investment. Then I became the artist-in-residence at Spotify."

text:
2x 256GB > 4x 96GB > 1x 512GB Mac Studio M5 Ultra

Price: $21,996 (4x) vs $21,598 (2x) vs $22,299 (1x)

More Macs = more memory bandwidth = faster decode

You can connect Macs together with readily available Thunderbolt 5 cables. This is what enables them to pool memory. What makes them faster is tensor parallelism

Tensor parallelism splits every layer of the model evenly across Macs in a cluster. Each one only has to read its share of the weights when calculating a token, and they all do it in parallel

After every layer they sync a few KB over Thunderbolt 5. Over TCP/IP each sync cost ~300µs, which made splitting slower than one Mac. macOS 26.2 added RDMA, which cuts it to ~3µs

This 100x reduction in latency is what made tensor parallelism practical on Macs

Between the 2x 256 and 4x 96 you're trading off between usable memory and extra speed. I give the edge to 2x 256 given long context and concurrent sessions are key to agent use cases

4x 96 and 1x 512 are very close. I give the edge to 4x 96 since it’s much faster. Expert streaming from disk is also improving, which could let it run larger models without giving up context

#1 / 2x 256, ~480GB usable memory
-> Runs both GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 4-bit
-> ~1.6x faster than 1x 512 GB
-> Plenty of room for long context

#2 / 4x 96, ~344GB usable memory
-> Runs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 4-bit but not GLM-5.3
-> ~2.3x faster than 1x 512 GB
-> Less room for long context

#3 / 1x 512, ~490GB usable memory
-> Runs both GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 4-bit
-> 1x baseline speed
-> Plenty of room for long context

Each Mac in a mesh needs to be connected to every other one (you can't use a switch). Since M5 Ultras come with 6 Thunderbolt 5 ports, in theory you could connect up to 7 of them with 21 cables

However once you go above 4 Macs in a cluster it gets theoretical as there are very few benchmarks on these sorts of setups. The decode speedup also tops out, which is why we only recommend connecting 4 at most

text:
你是否需要很长的上下文？

NVIDIA 新论文标题给了一种答案:《You don't need long context》。

现在模型的 context window 越做越长，128K、256K、1M 已经很常见。

但论文先指出一个很现实的问题：context 越长，后面的 token 越贵。

在他们测试的开放模型上，256K context 相比 16K，每个输出 token 的推理成本高出约 3.6–7 倍。

作者于是做了一件很简单的事：

让 Agent 定期「压缩」自己的工作状态。

对话变长以后，把当前进度、关键发现和下一步计划总结成一个更短的 semantic state，再从新的 context 继续执行。

原始历史依然可以保存，需要时再选择性读取；模型没必要每一步都把全部历史重新塞进 context。

结果在 6 个长时任务上，Claude Opus 4.5 和 GPT-5.6 Sol 即使把 context 压到很短，整体准确率依然基本保持稳定；估算推理成本分别最高降低约 8.8× 和 5×。

他们甚至测试了一个更极端的版本：

Agent 每执行一个动作，就重新压缩一次 context。

性能依然没有崩。

这也引出了论文里一个挺有意思的概念：Semantic State Space Model。

未来长时 Agent 也许不需要维护一条越来越长的聊天记录，而是持续维护一个小而清晰的「当前状态」，执行一步，再更新一次。

长 context 当然有价值，但很多 Agent 任务真正需要的，可能是更好的状态管理和按需检索。

把所有历史一直带在身上，未必是最好的长期记忆方式。

quoted_text:
I burned a shitload of compute so you don't have to. Releasing the Harness Leaderboard.

Which harness should you run your open model in? I ran 28,849 trials to find out.

The leaderboard compares nine coding-agent harnesses on open models. In each comparison only the harness changes: the model, provider and reasoning effort stay fixed, and every task gets three attempts.

The trials ran GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Flint on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE, for $4,746 of inference.

Averaged over the three models, mini-swe-agent (@KLieret), a bash-only agent, solves 51.4% of tasks and @openclaw 27.3%. Four others are statistically tied with mini-swe-agent.

One of them is Pi (@pidotdev), at 49.4% for $0.29 per solved task, about 45% less than mini-swe-agent's $0.53.

The best harness depends on the model: mini-swe-agent on GLM-5.3-Flash, Hermes Agent (@NousResearch) on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Kimi Code (@Kimi_Moonshot) on Flint.

@opencode costs $3.35 per solved task, 11.7 times as much as Pi.

See Harness Hub's Harness Lens for what the nine harnesses do differently. It documents the prompts, tools and compaction of 34 coding-agent harnesses and links every claim to its source.

Social trading has brought out the worst in KOLs. It was designed to keep them honest by making every trade public. In reality, the opposite happened

Why? Because our industry incentivizes it

Launchpads are paying millions to dishonest KOLs. It's time they start taking it seriously

Audit the top traders. Expose their side wallets. Ban repeat offenders

We have the tools. What's missing is the willingness to use them

text:
Ramp 数据：企业用的 AI 越来越多，花的钱 8、9 月几乎没涨，Anthropic 上市估值预期降到 1.2 万亿到 1.3 万亿美元

美国企业财务软件公司 Ramp 的最新数据显示，企业消耗的 token 还在猛涨，但花在 token 上的钱从 8 月起基本停了。7 月企业 token 支出比上月涨了 42%，8 月只涨 1%，9 月只涨 0.2%。

拿 Ramp 的周度数据算，从 8 月初到 10 月中，企业用掉的 token 多了约 65%，花的钱只多了 1.5%。

这组数据由 Ramp 首席经济学家 Ara Kharazian 发布，TechCrunch 11 月 6 日做了报道。这时 Anthropic 正在准备 IPO，而投资者给它的高估值，前提是 AI 收入继续高速增长。

【对用 AI 的公司和个人：同样的活，花得更少了】

钱没涨，主要因为 AI 变便宜了。9 月 OpenAI 发布 GPT-6 Sol 和 Luna，API 价格直接砍半：Sol 从每百万输入 token 4 美元降到 2 美元。Anthropic 同月发 Fable 5.1 和 Opus 5.5，招股书说 Fable 5.1 让常见任务成本降了约 25%，Opus 5.5 每个任务的成本比 Opus 5 降了约 40%，一部分靠降价，一部分靠模型更省 token。

Ramp 统计的 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 综合单价，9 月下旬到 10 月下旬一个月就从每百万 token 0.76 美元降到 0.56 美元，降了 27%。

企业自己也学会了省钱。Kharazian 说，AI 用得越熟的公司，越会给员工设预算，默认不让长任务跑最贵的模型，再用路由工具把活分给更便宜的小模型。

还有更便宜的选择冒出来。TechCrunch 提到一个叫 Jev 的模型，来自前 OpenAI 研究员 Almeida 创办的 TypeSafe AI。它不生成文字，只在开发者事先设定好的几个答案里选一个，并给出把握有多大，适合“是不是垃圾邮件”“这条命令危不危险”这类判断题。它的输出 token 免费，输入按十亿 token 计价。Vercel 的数据显示，Jev 上线两周，它的 AI 网关上就有 35% 的付费团队在用。Kharazian 说：“很多 AI 用途只需要一个简单的是或否。”

再加上 Meta、英伟达和一批中美开源模型在抢企业客户，Kharazian 认为现在是买方市场。他从企业那里听说，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 推的企业长约基本没有逼客户多花钱，签了还能拿到折扣。

【花钱最多的那 1% 公司，开始不往上加了】

Ramp 此前发现，企业花在 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 上的钱，80% 来自最舍得花钱的 1% 公司。这批公司 7 月人均每月花 9873 美元，8 月掉到 8568 美元，9 月回升到 9568 美元，仍比 7 月低 3%。

普通公司离这个数差得很远：排前 10% 的公司人均每月 813 美元，中位数公司只有 15.7 美元。Kharazian 说，软件、金融行业对 AI 编程有大量需求，但诊所、汽车经销店未必需要每人每月花上万美元。

10 月有回暖：截至 10 月 23 日那一周，token 支出比一个月前同一周涨了 8.9%，token 用量涨了 37%。Kharazian 仍认为增速放缓的压力很大。

【对 Anthropic IPO 意味着什么】

在 Ramp 截至 10 月 23 日那一周的数据里，Anthropic 拿走了企业 token 支出的 60.5%，价格战首先打在它身上。

Anthropic 11 月 2 日更新的招股书里，三季度收入 169.6 亿美元，比二季度的 115.6 亿涨了 47%，增长仍然很快。招股书同时写明，这个季度用量增长带来的收入，被新模型降价和合同折扣抵掉了约 6 亿美元。

投资者的估值预期一路下调。据彭博社 11 月 6 日报道，10 月初投资者讨论的估值高达 2 万亿美元，10 月中投资者说明会后降到 1.4 万亿到 1.5 万亿，周四纳斯达克 100 指数单日暴跌 6.4% 后，部分潜在投资者在谈的是 1.2 万亿到 1.3 万亿。消息人士说还没有最终决定，Anthropic 不予置评。

借钱的成本也可能变高。据《金融时报》10 月 30 日报道，黑石作为 Anthropic 一笔芯片融资的基石投资者，告诉参与这笔交易的投资者它预计 Anthropic 上市后的信用评级是 BB 级，属于“垃圾级”里最高的一档，而黑石之前的说法是 2027 年前能拿到投资级。这只是黑石的预测，评级机构还没出结果。

OpenAI 也在降预期。《金融时报》10 月 31 日报道，OpenAI 这轮融资目标从 300 亿美元降到约 200 亿，投前估值从 1.4 万亿降到 1.25 万亿。

【这份数据代表谁】

Ramp AI 指数覆盖 8.5 万多家用 Ramp 公司卡和付款系统的美国企业。token 用量和支出这组数据，只来自其中接入了 Ramp token 支出管理工具的公司，Ramp 自己说这批公司比整体样本更偏科技。Kharazian 对 TechCrunch 说，AI 支出几乎全部来自风投支持的高增长科技公司，它们一起放缓，就会一起拖累 AI 公司的收入。

员工自己掏钱的个人账号、不用 Ramp 的公司，都不在统计里。

Notion 联合创始人 Akshay Kothari 10 月 22 日发过 Notion 自己的数据，每周 token 用量一路往上，每百万 token 成本一路往下，配的话是“tokens go brrr. costs go ahhh”。

投资者押注的是下一个像 AI 编程那样能大把花钱的新用途。OpenAI 的 Dots、xAI 的 Grok Bot、Meta 的 Muse 都是这个方向的个人 AI 助理。Kharazian 认为个人助理的经济产出不如编程，撑不起持续的高速增长。

Ramp 报告：https://t.co/UBGsAl7VUd

A few weeks ago, when Muse Wonder came out, I argued that Meta had an advantage in building a personal AI assistant. If you build both the product and the model, the problems you find in the product can shape what you train the model to do. You can teach it to remember a detail from weeks ago or find another way to finish a task when its first plan fails. 

Today we’re seeing what that looks like. Meta used Muse Wonder to train specialized versions of the models behind Muse and Meta AI, and it’s rolling them out to both products. In Meta’s own tests, Muse forgot critical information less than half as often and was 67% better at completing everyday tasks when something unexpected got in the way.

text:
Claude Code 会把你的登录邮箱发给网站，这事是真的，但不是每次联网都发。我看了官方回应，也把自己本机的记录扫了一遍。

怎么回事：用账号登录的 Claude Code，会把你的账号邮箱放进模型能看到的内容里，本意是让它写代码署名时别乱编名字。出问题的是 Claude 自己写 curl 这类命令去访问网站的时候：有些网站会要求访问的程序留个联系方式，它有时就把你的邮箱填进了请求头（User-Agent，告诉网站「谁在访问」的那一行），对方服务器就记下了。

官方怎么说（Claude Code 团队的人11 月 6 日中午在 HN 回复）：
· 下一版会把邮箱从模型能看到的内容里拿掉，预计下周初发布
· 在那之前，2.1.317 及以上内置了一个隐私插件，默认开着
· 这个插件拦不住所有情况，比如 Claude 自己写个脚本再运行
· stable 渠道还停在 2.1.311，要升到 2.1.317 以上才有

这事不新。5 月就有人在 GitHub 报过「登录邮箱被塞进模型上下文、没法关」，因为长时间没动静，被机器人自动关了；7 月又有人报，84 个赞，到现在还开着。

我查了自己的：让 Claude Code 把本机还留着的记录（最早到 7 月）扫了一遍。它自己设请求头的命令有几千条，带邮箱的 8 条，都是访问美国证监会（SEC）和美国气象局的数据接口，这类接口要求在请求头里写明你是谁。填的是 https://t.co/hwYyraTRNn 这种占位地址和我网站域名的地址，登录邮箱一次都没有。

还有个插曲：第一版扫描命令里带了我的邮箱，直接被那个隐私插件拒了。它就是这么判断的：命令里同时出现 User-Agent 和你的邮箱就拦，哪怕只在本机跑。

现在能做的：
1. 终端跑 claude --version，低于 2.1.317 就升级：在 stable（稳定版）渠道的，先在 /config 里把更新渠道换成 latest，再跑 claude update
2. 想知道自己中没中，对 Claude Code 说：「只在本机查：~/.claude/projects 里的历史记录，有没有命令把我的登录邮箱写进 User-Agent，告诉我次数、日期和网站」
3. 在 ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md 里加一句「不要把我的邮箱写进任何请求，网站要联系方式先问我」，下周新版出来再升一次

原帖：https://t.co/4iI1HT0w2k

该负责人介绍，近期监测发现，虚拟货币主要发行平台Solana @solana 通过境内相关单位高调投放广告，以推广Solana品牌的方式，进行虚拟货币营销宣传。

中国人民银行联合相关地方金融管理、公安、市场监管等部门叫停线下交流活动，并将会同有关部门对涉事单位和个人开展调查。

该负责人进一步解释，Solana作为主要虚拟货币发行平台，其发行的Solana币本质上是虚拟货币，同时它也在为USDT等主要虚拟货币的发行交易提供技术服务，上述业务均属《通知》明确的非法金融活动，宣传推广Solana已违反《通知》规定。

虚拟货币现阶段无法有效满足客户身份识别、反洗钱等方面的要求，易引发市场投机炒作活动。该负责人表示，下一步，中国人民银行将与相关部门和地方政府一起，以境内虚拟货币交易商、境外虚拟货币发行交易平台的境内关联主体为重点，继续打击境内虚拟货币相关业务活动，维护好经济金融秩序。

How much revenue are database companies losing because agents aren’t able to sign up autonomously?

Today, we’re releasing @tryscope_app's first database benchmark.

We tested 18 hosted databases to see which are ready to win that market. We measured which databases agents could use, analyzed where they failed, and identified best practices to fix the blockers.

Across 1,035 sessions, only 16.6% reached a first working result and failed sessions all came from products not being agent friendly.

We tested 20 model-and-agent-tool combinations across harnesses including Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.

The task: start with no account, set up the named database, write a record, and hand over the credentials. An account or API key alone didn’t count.

What we found:
→ @prisma led with an 88.3% success score, followed by @upstash at 63.3%, @neondatabase and @niledatabase at 43.3%, and @ClickHouseDB at 38.3%.
→ 7 of 18 products had zero successful sessions across every agent tested.
→ CAPTCHAs stopped 373 sessions. Bot blocks stopped another 105. Other barriers included rejected agent email domains and OAuth-only flows.
→ 50 of the 172 successful sessions used a working database without creating an account. Letting agents try the product before signing up made a difference.

An agent can arrive knowing exactly which product it wants to use and still never become a user. For developer tools, the path from “use this database” to a working result is part of your conversion funnel.

See the full leaderboard, methodology and session transcripts: https://t.co/aMBBnlZx4f

Special thank you to our partners @AgentMail and @Agentphone for giving us the right tools to run this experiment.

text:
People will talk about “storytelling” and then it’s just a bucket of loosely connected facts

Storytelling requires a story

A story has a beginning, middle, end. A protagonist, an antagonist. Maybe a loyal sidekick. A noble quest. A surprise! A pickle!! A change, a resolution.

It’s the difference between “in a galaxy far far away…” and “today we’re excited to announce that we are launching a rebel alliance”

In some stories, the protagonist is you, on your own hero’s journey

Other times, the protagonist is the customer. They have an important goal, but there’s something standing in the way. What has changed now, and why? What’s their happy ending?
